children.title: Dense Matrix Storage
children.top_down_role: Explicit dense coefficient and iterate storage for moderate matrix dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Matrix Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit storage model for a standard primal SDP with moderate matrix order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SDP with coefficient matrices \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), dense matrix storage represents every coefficient and matrix iterate \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) by all entries of an \(n\times n\) array, optionally retaining only one triangle by symmetry. The coefficient storage is \(\Theta((m+1)n^2)\) scalars, or \(\Theta((m+1)n(n+1)/2)\) under packed symmetric storage; each dense matrix iterate requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) scalars. Matrix inner products are evaluated as \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(A_iX)\) from these arrays.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store every coefficient and iterate explicitly as a dense symmetric array, requiring quadratic storage per matrix and quadratic storage times the number of constraints for all coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(C,A_i,X\in\mathbb S^n\)
All stored scalar entries have constant machine-word size
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\Theta(mn^2)\) and \(M_X=\Theta(n^2)\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order n

children.title: Sparse Matrix Storage
children.top_down_role: Explicit matrix representations organized around entry sparsity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Matrix Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-based storage of assembled SDP matrices with few nonzero entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\). Sparse matrix storage records, for each matrix, only triples \((p,q,v)\) with \(v=(A_i)_{pq}\ne0\), together with row or column pointers; one triangular half suffices when symmetry is enforced. If \(s_i\) is the number of stored entries of \(A_i\) and \(s_C\) that of \(C\), coefficient memory is \(\Theta(s_C+\sum_{i=1}^m s_i+n+m)\) machine words for a standard compressed format. The representation is exact provided omitted entries are interpreted as zero and mirrored triangular entries are reconstructed consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each symmetric coefficient by its nonzeros and index metadata; storage scales with the total nonzero count rather than with the full matrix area.
assumptions_latex: \(C,A_i\in\mathbb S^n\)
Omitted entries are exactly zero
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\Theta(s_C+\sum_{i=1}^m s_i+n+m)\) in a compressed sparse format.

notation.meaning: stored nonzero count of coefficient matrix i
stored nonzero count of the objective matrix

children.title: Block Matrix Storage
children.top_down_role: Explicit matrix representations preserving native cone-block structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Matrix Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit storage exploiting a known common block decomposition of SDP coefficients and iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an orthogonal decomposition \(\mathbb R^n=V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_k\) with \(\dim V_j=n_j\) makes every coefficient and admissible iterate block diagonal. Block matrix storage represents \(A_i=\operatorname{diag}(A_i^{(1)},\ldots,A_i^{(k)})\) and \(X=\operatorname{diag}(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(k)})\), where \(A_i^{(j)},X^{(j)}\in\mathbb S^{n_j}\), storing no off-block entries. Dense storage within blocks requires \(\Theta(\sum_{j=1}^k n_j^2)\) scalars per matrix, and positivity separates exactly as \(X\succeq0\) if and only if \(X^{(j)}\succeq0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store only the diagonal blocks induced by a common invariant decomposition; memory and semidefinite tests separate across those blocks.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and admissible iterates share the stated block structure
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_X=\Theta(\sum_j n_j^2)\) and \(X\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow X^{(j)}\succeq0\) for all \(j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Callable interface for applying the SDP constraint map without assembling all coefficient matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given coefficient matrices \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), a forward operator interface implements the linear map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) by returning \(y=\mathcal A(X)\) for any supplied \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), where \(y_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(A_iX)\). The interface may use structured products, generated coefficients, or streamed data rather than stored arrays, but it must return the same vector as explicit evaluation of all coefficient inner products, up to the declared numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward interface maps a symmetric matrix to all constraint inner products, while allowing coefficients to remain implicit or structured.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i,X\in\mathbb S^n\)
The arithmetic tolerance is specified by the implementation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathcal A(X))_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

children.title: Adjoint Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing dual-direction operator products.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Callable interface for applying the adjoint SDP constraint map without explicit coefficient assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constraint map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), an adjoint operator interface accepts \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and returns the symmetric matrix \(\mathcal A^*(y)\in\mathbb S^n\) defined by \(\mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_i\). The result may be returned as an explicit matrix or as an object supporting the matrix operations required by the solver. In either case it must represent the same linear combination as the assembled coefficients, up to the declared numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adjoint interface maps constraint-space weights to the corresponding weighted sum of symmetric coefficient matrices, explicitly or implicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\)
The arithmetic tolerance is specified by the implementation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_i\).

notation.meaning: adjoint of the SDP constraint operator

children.title: Operator-Pair Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements linking paired operator implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Pair Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-inner-product adjointness condition for a forward-adjoint SDP operator pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair of linear interfaces \(\widehat{\mathcal A}:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}^{*}:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) is compatible when, for every \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\langle\widehat{\mathcal A}(X),y\rangle_2=\langle X,\widehat{\mathcal A}^{*}(y)\rangle_F.\] In floating-point implementations, compatibility at tolerance \(\tau\ge0\) means the absolute difference of these two quantities is at most \(\tau\|X\|_F\|y\|_2\) for every tested nonzero pair. Exact compatibility makes the second interface the adjoint of the first under the stated inner products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and adjoint routines are compatible when their Euclidean and trace inner products agree, exactly or within a declared scaled numerical tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Both interfaces are linear on their stated domains
The domain uses the Frobenius inner product and the codomain the Euclidean inner product
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle\widehat{\mathcal A}(X),y\rangle_2=\langle X,\widehat{\mathcal A}^{*}(y)\rangle_F\).

children.title: Implicit Coefficient Operators
children.top_down_role: Procedural representations of structured coefficient maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Coefficient Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Procedural representation of structured SDP coefficients through forward and adjoint evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit coefficient representation of an SDP constraint map consists of procedures computing \(\mathcal A(X)\) and \(\mathcal A^*(y)\), where \((\mathcal A(X))_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\) and \(\mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_i\), without requiring explicit storage of every \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\). The procedures may exploit formulas, transforms, low-rank factors, or data-generation rules. They represent the assembled SDP exactly when both identities hold for every admissible \(X\) and \(y\), and their forward-adjoint pair satisfies the trace-inner-product compatibility identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured procedures replace stored coefficient matrices while reproducing both constraint evaluations and weighted coefficient sums with a compatible operator pair.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\) define a linear constraint map
Both procedural interfaces act on all solver-admissible arguments
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implicit and assembled models define the same \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal A^*\).

children.title: Memory-Bounded Operator-Access Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operator-access regimes constrained by memory or data-pass budgets.

children.title: Streaming Operator Access
children.top_down_role: Sequential operator access under restricted data retention.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Operator Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way access model in which coefficient records are processed sequentially.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A streaming-access SDP model presents coefficient records \(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_N\) in a fixed sequential order. During a pass, an algorithm may read each record once, update an internal state, and discard the record; it may not revisit an earlier record until a new pass begins. A forward or adjoint evaluation is streaming-compatible if its required output can be accumulated from these records and the current query using internal memory independent of storing all \(N\) records. The access model includes the stream order, restart permission, and numerical precision as part of the problem specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient data arrive sequentially; records cannot be revisited within a pass, and operator outputs must be accumulated without retaining the entire stream.
assumptions_latex: The finite stream \((r_t)_{t=1}^N\) determines the coefficient operator
Stream order and restart rules are fixed in advance
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(r_t\) is accessed at most once per pass and need not remain stored afterward.

notation.meaning: number of records in one pass

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the particular sequential-access, restart, ordering, and memory conventions. Because streaming models vary materially in these details, the stated model requires an inspectable citation.

children.title: Pass-Limited Operator Access
children.top_down_role: Operator access governed by a fixed data-pass budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Pass-Limited Operator Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-access model imposing a fixed bound on complete traversals of coefficient data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one pass mean a complete sequential traversal of the coefficient data sufficient to expose every record once. An algorithm has \(P\)-pass-limited operator access if, over its entire execution, it initiates at most \(P\in\mathbb N\) such traversals and performs no coefficient queries outside them. Internal computation between passes is unrestricted except by separately stated memory and arithmetic budgets. Adaptivity is allowed: the state and query parameters used in pass \(p+1\) may depend on all outputs accumulated through pass \(p\), but the total traversal count remains at most \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm may traverse all coefficient data at most a prescribed number of times, although later passes may adapt to information from earlier ones.
assumptions_latex: A pass has a fixed, declared meaning for the data source
\(P\in\mathbb N\) is specified before execution
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total number of complete data traversals is at most \(P\).

notation.meaning: maximum number of complete data passes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the selected definition of a complete pass, exclusion of all out-of-pass queries, or adaptive-pass convention. These choices materially determine the access model.

children.title: Memory-Bounded Operator Access
children.top_down_role: Operator evaluation under restricted working memory.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Bounded Operator Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator oracle model restricting persistent working storage independently of coefficient-data size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the coefficient data contain \(N\) machine words. An operator-access algorithm is \(M\)-memory-bounded if, excluding read-only input and write-only output, its persistent state and temporary workspace contain at most \(M\) machine words at every time, where typically \(M=o(N)\). The bound includes stored iterates, sketches, indices, and cached coefficient records. An operator query is admissible only when its implementation, including intermediate values, respects the same bound. Thus the model forbids materializing any dense or sparse coefficient collection whose storage exceeds \(M\), even if that collection could be generated procedurally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All persistent and temporary workspace, including iterates and cached records, must fit within a declared budget smaller than the full coefficient data.
assumptions_latex: Memory is counted in fixed-precision machine words
Read-only input and write-only output are excluded from workspace
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_t M_t\le M\), typically with \(M=o(N)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a plausible memory model, but no source supports its treatment of input, output, temporary oracle workspace, fixed precision, and the optional sublinear condition. These conventions must be sourced.

children.title: Matrix-Free SDP Method Model
children.top_down_role: Algorithm architectures that avoid assembling full coefficient matrices, Newton matrices, or primal iterates.

children.title: Matrix-Free First-Order Methods
children.top_down_role: First-order architectures using operator products and partial spectral information.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free First-Order Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected first-order template using operator calls and partial spectral projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R\), a closed convex feasible set \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\), an initial \(X_0\in\mathcal F\), and stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), compute \(G_k=\nabla f(X_k)\) using forward and adjoint operator calls, then set \[X_{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathcal F}(X_k-\eta_kG_k).\] The projection is evaluated through matrix-vector products and partial eigenspace computations rather than full matrix assembly or diagonalization. Stop when a declared feasibility-and-stationarity residual is at most \(\varepsilon\), or when the iteration budget is exhausted, and return the final feasible iterate or its low-rank factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly form gradients through operator calls and project using partial spectral information, stopping at a prescribed residual tolerance or iteration limit.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal F\)
The projection oracle returns an exact or tolerance-controlled projection
\(X_0\in\mathcal F\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the last projected iterate \(X_k\in\mathcal F\), or a factor representing it.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

children.title: Matrix-Free Second-Order Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton and augmented-Lagrangian architectures using iterative inner linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Second-Order Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact Newton template with Hessian actions and iterative inner solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a twice differentiable merit function \(\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), an initial point \(z_0\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon,\xi_k>0\), compute \(g_k=\nabla\Phi(z_k)\). Approximately solve \[H_kp_k=-g_k,\qquad H_kv=\nabla^2\Phi(z_k)v,\] by an iterative Krylov method using only Hessian-vector products assembled from forward and adjoint SDP operator calls, until \(\|H_kp_k+g_k\|_2\le\xi_k\|g_k\|_2\). Choose a globalization step \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and stop when the declared primal-dual residual is at most \(\varepsilon\); return \(z_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute inexact Newton directions with Krylov iterations and operator-based Hessian products, globalize the step, and stop at a primal-dual residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is twice differentiable on the iterates' domain
Hessian-vector products are available without explicit Hessian assembly
The globalization rule accepts a well-defined step
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns an iterate with declared residual at most \(\varepsilon\), unless its iteration budget is exhausted.

notation.meaning: Hessian or generalized Newton operator at iteration k

children.title: Full Eigenspace Computation
children.top_down_role: Complete spectral access for projections and high-accuracy feasibility assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Eigenspace Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense symmetric eigendecomposition used for exact spectral projection and feasibility testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a real symmetric matrix \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), initialize a dense symmetric eigensolver with \(A\). Compute an orthogonal matrix \(Q=[q_1,\ldots,q_n]\) and ordered eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\) such that \(A=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^\top\). For a scalar function \(f\), return \(f(A)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(f(\lambda_1),\ldots,f(\lambda_n))Q^\top\). In particular, the positive-semidefinite projection is \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(A)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\max\{\lambda_i,0\})Q^\top\), and \(A\succeq0\) exactly when \(\lambda_n\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute every eigenvalue and an orthonormal eigenbasis, enabling exact spectral functions, positive-semidefinite projection, and minimum-eigenvalue feasibility assessment.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) is represented explicitly in dense form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda)Q^\top\) and \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(A)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\max\{\lambda_i,0\})Q^\top\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order n

children.title: Partial Extreme-Eigenpair Computation
children.top_down_role: Selected eigenpair access for large-scale spectral and low-rank methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Extreme-Eigenpair Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free computation of selected algebraically extreme eigenpairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), an integer \(k<n\), and tolerance \(\tau>0\), initialize a nonzero trial subspace \(V_1\). Repeatedly expand it using products \(Av\), orthonormalize the new directions, and solve the Rayleigh--Ritz problem for \(V_j^\top A V_j\). Select the \(k\) largest or smallest Ritz pairs \((\theta_i,u_i)\), where \(u_i=V_jz_i\), and stop when \(\lVert Au_i-\theta_i u_i\rVert_2\leq\tau\) for every requested pair. Return only these eigenpair approximations and their residual norms; no complete eigenbasis is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand a matrix-free trial subspace, extract selected extreme Ritz pairs, and stop when all requested eigenpair residuals meet tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) admits matrix-vector products.
\(1\leq k<n\) and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Au_i-\theta_i u_i\rVert_2\leq\tau\) for each returned \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\).

notation.meaning: orthonormal trial-subspace basis at iteration j
selected Ritz value and Ritz vector

children.title: Inexact Spectral Oracles

children.title: Lanczos Eigenvalue Oracles
children.top_down_role: Krylov-based extreme-eigenpair computation for large operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Lanczos Eigenvalue Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric Lanczos oracle for an extreme Ritz pair and an a posteriori residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), choose \(q_1\) with \(\lVert q_1\rVert_2=1\), set \(q_0=0\) and \(\beta_0=0\), and for \(j=1,\ldots,m\) compute \(w=Aq_j-\beta_{j-1}q_{j-1}\), \(\alpha_j=q_j^\top w\), \(w\leftarrow w-\alpha_jq_j\), \(\beta_j=\lVert w\rVert_2\), and \(q_{j+1}=w/\beta_j\) when \(\beta_j>0\). Form the tridiagonal \(T_m\) from \(\alpha_j\) and \(\beta_j\). Return an extreme eigenpair \((\theta,z)\) of \(T_m\), the Ritz vector \(u=Q_mz\), and residual \(\lVert Au-\theta u\rVert_2=\beta_m|z_m|\); stop when this residual is at most \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos tridiagonalizes a symmetric operator by matrix-vector products and returns an extreme Ritz pair with a computable residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) is accessible through matrix-vector products.
\(m\leq n\) and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u=Q_mz\) and \(\lVert Au-\theta u\rVert_2=\beta_m|z_m|\leq\tau\) upon termination.

notation.meaning: last coordinate of the selected eigenvector of the tridiagonal matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Subspace Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized low-memory approximation of a dominant eigenspace for a positive-semidefinite operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\), target rank \(k\), oversampling \(p\geq2\), and power count \(q\geq0\), draw a Gaussian matrix \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times(k+p)}\). Form \(Y=A^{q+1}\Omega\) using successive matrix-block products and compute an orthonormal basis \(Q\) for \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\). Diagonalize \(B=Q^\top A Q=Z\Theta Z^\top\), retain its \(k\) largest eigenvalues, and return \(U=QZ_{(:,1:k)}\), \(\Theta_{1:k,1:k}\), and residual norms \(\lVert Au_i-\theta_i u_i\rVert_2\). Stop or enlarge the sketch when the requested residual criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian sketch and optional power iterations construct a small subspace whose Rayleigh–Ritz eigenpairs approximate the dominant spectrum.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\) admits matrix-block products.
\(1\leq k<n\), \(p\geq2\), and \(q\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U=QZ_{(:,1:k)}\) gives orthonormal Ritz vectors with \(U^\top A U=\Theta_{1:k,1:k}\).

children.title: Spectral-Oracle Accuracy Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Oracle Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three stopping policies for an inexact maximum-eigenvalue oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For queries \(A_t\in\mathbb S^n\), an inexact maximum-eigenvalue oracle returns a unit vector \(v_t\), lower estimate \(\theta_t=v_t^\top A_tv_t\), and certified upper estimate \(U_t\geq\lambda_{\max}(A_t)\). Its certified error is \(\delta_t=U_t-\theta_t\). A fixed regime requires \(\delta_t\leq\bar\delta\) for one prescribed \(\bar\delta\). An adaptive regime chooses a history-measurable tolerance \(\delta_t^{\mathrm{req}}\) and requires \(\delta_t\leq\delta_t^{\mathrm{req}}\). A certificate-driven regime performs spectral iterations until the computable inequality \(U_t-\theta_t\leq\delta_t^{\mathrm{req}}\) holds, then returns the accompanying bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed accuracy uses one tolerance, adaptive accuracy changes tolerance by iteration, and certificate-driven accuracy stops only when verified spectral bounds are sufficiently tight.
assumptions_latex: \(A_t\in\mathbb S^n\) for every query index \(t\).
\(\lVert v_t\rVert_2=1\) and \(U_t\geq\lambda_{\max}(A_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\lambda_{\max}(A_t)-\theta_t\leq\delta_t\), with \(\delta_t\) controlled by the selected regime.

children.title: Eigenvalue Separation Oracles
children.top_down_role: Spectral separation interfaces for violated semidefinite constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue Separation Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one separating inequality generated by a negative eigenvector of an affine matrix pencil.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_{i=1}^d x_iF_i\) with \(F_i\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:F(x)\succeq0\}\). At a query \(\bar x\), compute a unit vector \(v\) satisfying \(v^\top F(\bar x)v<0\). Every \(x\in K\) satisfies the affine inequality \(v^\top F(x)v\geq0\), whereas \(\bar x\) violates it. Thus the coefficients \(a_i=v^\top F_iv\) and constant \(a_0=v^\top F_0v\) give a verifiable separating cut \(a_0+\sum_i a_ix_i\geq0\). If no negative eigenvalue exists, the oracle certifies \(F(\bar x)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative eigenvector yields a rank-one affine inequality valid for every semidefinite-feasible point and violated by the query point.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb S^n\) is affine.
The spectral computation determines whether \(\lambda_{\min}(F(\bar x))<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^\top F(x)v\geq0\) for all \(x\in K\), while \(v^\top F(\bar x)v<0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoid-Method Complexity for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak feasibility complexity in the variable dimension under exact rational separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the spectrahedron \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:F(x)\succeq0\}\) with rational input data. Suppose \(K\subseteq B(0,R)\), and in the feasible case \(K\) contains a Euclidean ball of radius \(r>0\). With an exact polynomial-time eigenvalue separation oracle, the central-cut ellipsoid method decides feasibility and returns a point of \(K\) after \(O(d^2\log(R/r))\) oracle calls. If the rational encoding lengths of \(F_i\), \(R\), and \(r\) are polynomially bounded, each separation call and all ellipsoid arithmetic have polynomial bit complexity; hence the overall weak-feasibility procedure is polynomial in the input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under known inner and outer radii and exact spectral separation, ellipsoid feasibility uses quadratically many dimension-scaled logarithmic oracle calls and polynomial bit complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq B(0,R)\), and nonempty \(K\) contains a ball of radius \(r>0\).
The affine pencil and radius bounds are rationally encoded.
Exact eigenvalue separation runs in polynomial bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle count is \(O(d^2\log(R/r))\), and the weak-feasibility algorithm has polynomial bit complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Cutting-Plane Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative linear-master method using rank-one cuts from violated semidefinite constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\), initialize a tractable bounding polyhedron \(P_0\supseteq K=\{x:F(x)\succeq0\}\) and an empty cut set. At iteration \(t\), solve the linear master problem over \(P_t\) to obtain \(x_t\). If \(F(x_t)\succeq0\), return \(x_t\). Otherwise choose a unit vector \(v_t\) with \(v_t^\top F(x_t)v_t<0\), append the valid spectral cut \(v_t^\top F(x)v_t\geq0\), and set \(P_{t+1}=P_t\cap\{x:v_t^\top F(x)v_t\geq0\}\). Stop according to feasibility, objective-gap, or iteration tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successive linear master problems and add a rank-one eigenvector cut whenever the current point violates the semidefinite constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\) is a tractable polyhedron containing \(K\).
A minimum-eigenvalue oracle is available for every master solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\subseteq P_{t+1}\subseteq P_t\), and every infeasible iterate is excluded by its new cut.

notation.meaning: polyhedral master region at iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Outer-Approximation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer representation of a spectrahedron by finitely many rank-one quadratic-form inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\) and \(K=\{x:F(x)\succeq0\}\). Since \(F(x)\succeq0\) is equivalent to \(v^\top F(x)v\geq0\) for every unit vector \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), any finite set \(V\subseteq\{v:\lVert v\rVert_2=1\}\) defines the polyhedral outer approximation \(P(V)=\{x:v^\top F(x)v\geq0\text{ for all }v\in V\}\). It satisfies \(K\subseteq P(V)\). Moreover, if \(V_1\subseteq V_2\), then \(P(V_2)\subseteq P(V_1)\); adding negative-eigenvector directions therefore tightens the relaxation without removing feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finitely many unit-vector quadratic-form inequalities form a polyhedral superset of a spectrahedron, and adding directions monotonically tightens it.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb S^n\) is affine.
\(V\) is a finite set of unit vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\subseteq P(V)\), and \(V_1\subseteq V_2\) implies \(P(V_2)\subseteq P(V_1)\).

notation.meaning: finite collection of spectral test directions

children.title: Spectral Cut Management
children.top_down_role: Retention, aggregation, and removal regimes for accumulated spectral cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Cut Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory retention and deletion policy preserving a valid spectral outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain at iteration \(t\) a finite set \(V_t\) of unit spectral directions and the master region \(P(V_t)\). After generating a violated direction \(v_t\), assign each stored cut an activity or age score, retain a bounded subset \(R_t\subseteq V_t\) containing prescribed protected cuts, and set \(V_{t+1}=R_t\cup\{v_t\}\). Deleted cuts may enlarge the master region, but validity is preserved because every retained inequality is valid for the spectrahedron. Before accepting any candidate from the reduced master, call the eigenvalue separation oracle again; accept only if no violation exceeding the feasibility tolerance is found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep a bounded active set of spectral cuts, permit safe deletion of valid inequalities, and re-separate every candidate before declaring feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Every stored direction \(v\) has unit norm and defines a valid cut \(v^\top F(x)v\geq0\).
Candidates are rechecked by a spectral separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\subseteq P(V_{t+1})\), and cut deletion cannot create a false feasibility certificate when acceptance requires re-separation.

notation.meaning: stored spectral directions at iteration t

children.title: Primal Logarithmic-Barrier Methods
children.top_down_role: Primal-feasible barrier architectures.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Logarithmic-Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized equality-constrained primal logarithmic-barrier path for a standard-form semidefinite program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal SDP \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\). Choose \(X_0\succ0\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(X_0)=b\) and choose \(\mu_0>0\). For each \(\mu>0\), solve the equality-constrained barrier problem \(\min\{\phi_\mu(X)=\langle C,X\rangle-\mu\log\det X:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succ0\}\) to stationarity, for example by feasible damped Newton steps satisfying \(\mathcal A(\Delta X)=0\) and preserving positive definiteness. At a stationary point \(X(\mu)\), choose the equality multiplier \(y(\mu)\) and define \(S(\mu)=C-\mathcal A^*(y(\mu))\). Then \(S(\mu)=\mu X(\mu)^{-1}\), so \(X(\mu)S(\mu)=\mu I\). Reduce \(\mu\) and repeat; return a stationary central-path point once \(n\mu\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Follow the idealized primal log-determinant central path by solving each equality-constrained barrier subproblem to stationarity and decreasing the barrier parameter until its primal-dual gap is at most the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible point \(X_0\succ0\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(X_0)=b\) is available.
\(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, and its equality constraints are independent.
Each barrier subproblem is solved to stationarity before the barrier parameter is reduced.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At the returned central-path point, \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(X\succ0\), \(S=\mu X^{-1}\succ0\), \(XS=\mu I\), and \(\langle X,S\rangle=n\mu\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: linear equality-constraint operator from symmetric matrices to the constraint space
dual slack matrix obtained from barrier stationarity

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized dual-feasible logarithmic-barrier path for a standard-form semidefinite program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the dual SDP \(\max\{b^\top y:S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\}\). Choose \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(S_0=C-\mathcal A^*(y_0)\succ0\), and choose \(\mu_0>0\). For each \(\mu>0\), solve the barrier problem \(\max\{\psi_\mu(y)=b^\top y+\mu\log\det(C-\mathcal A^*(y)):C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succ0\}\) to stationarity, for example by damped Newton steps that preserve positive definiteness of the slack. At a stationary point, set \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\) and \(X=\mu S^{-1}\). Stationarity gives \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), and \(XS=\mu I\). Reduce \(\mu\) and repeat; return a stationary central-path point once \(n\mu\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Follow the idealized dual log-determinant central path by solving each slack-barrier problem to stationarity and decreasing the barrier parameter until the reconstructed primal-dual gap is at most the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A point \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(C-\mathcal A^*(y_0)\succ0\) is available.
\(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
Each barrier subproblem has a stationary maximizer and is solved to stationarity before the barrier parameter is reduced.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At the returned central-path point, \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succ0\), \(X=\mu S^{-1}\succ0\), \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(XS=\mu I\), and \(\langle X,S\rangle=n\mu\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: dimension of the dual-variable and equality-constraint space

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\langle U,V\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(UV)\) on \(\mathbb S^n\), and consider the primal-dual pair \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:\mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ S\succeq0\}\). Its primal-dual central path is the family \((X(\mu),y(\mu),S(\mu))\), indexed by \(\mu>0\), satisfying
\[\mathcal A(X(\mu))=b,\qquad \mathcal A^*y(\mu)+S(\mu)=C,\qquad X(\mu)S(\mu)=\mu I,\qquad X(\mu),S(\mu)\succ0.\]
Every central triple has \(X(\mu)S(\mu)=S(\mu)X(\mu)\) and \(\langle X(\mu),S(\mu)\rangle=n\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly feasible standard-form primal-dual SDP, the central path consists of positive-definite feasible triples whose primal and dual slack matrices multiply to a positive scalar times the identity. The matrices commute, and their duality gap is n times that scalar.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Centrality Measures and SDP Central-Path Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frobenius, operator-norm, and one-sided spectral centrality measures and their associated SDP neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X,S\in\mathcal P\), with the source-defined average-complementarity quantity \(\mu=\mu(X,S)\), define \[d_F(X,S):=\|X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}-\mu I\|_F=\left(\sum_{i=1}^n(\lambda_i(XS)-\mu)^2\right)^{1/2},\] \[d_\infty(X,S):=\|X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}-\mu I\|=\max_{1\le i\le n}|\lambda_i(XS)-\mu|,\] and \[d_{-\infty}(X,S):=\max_{1\le i\le n}(\mu-\lambda_i(XS)).\] For strictly feasible iterates, these measures vanish only at central-path points, and \[d_{-\infty}(X,S)\le d_\infty(X,S)\le d_F(X,S),\qquad d_{-\infty}(X,S)<\mu(X,S)\iff X\succ0\text{ and }S\succ0.\] For \(0<\gamma<1\) and \(q\in\{F,\infty,-\infty\}\), define \[\mathcal N_q(\gamma):=\{(X,y,S)\in\mathcal F^0(P)\times\mathcal F^0(D):d_q(X,S)\le\gamma\mu(X,S)\}.\] The neighborhoods \(\mathcal N_F(\gamma)\) and \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\) are called the narrow and wide central-path neighborhoods, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extract defines three spectral measures of how far SDP complementarity is from μI. The one-sided measure is bounded above by the operator-norm measure, which is bounded above by the Frobenius measure. Thresholding these measures by γμ defines three central-path neighborhoods; the Frobenius and one-sided versions are respectively the narrow and wide neighborhoods. For strictly feasible iterates, a measure vanishes only at a central-path point.
assumptions_latex: X,S\in\mathcal P
0<\gamma<1
(X,y,S)\in\mathcal F^0(P)\times\mathcal F^0(D)\text{ for neighborhood membership}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_{-\infty}(X,S)\le d_\infty(X,S)\le d_F(X,S),\quad d_{-\infty}(X,S)<\mu(X,S)\iff X\succ0\text{ and }S\succ0,\quad \mathcal N_q(\gamma)=\{(X,y,S):d_q(X,S)\le\gamma\mu(X,S)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled Primal–Dual SDP Central-Path Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scaling-dependent short-step update for strictly feasible semidefinite primal–dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given strictly feasible primal and dual solutions \((\bar X,\bar S)\) with \(\bar t=k/\operatorname{Tr}(\bar X\bar S)\) and \(\|\bar t\,\bar X^{1/2}\bar S\bar X^{1/2}-I\|_2\leq\kappa\), choose \(\chi\in(0,1)\) and set \(t_+=(1-\chi/\sqrt{k})^{-1}\bar t\). Choose \(Q\succ0\) such that \(Q\bar XQ\) and \(Q^{-1}\bar SQ^{-1}\) commute. Determine \((\Delta X,\Delta S)\) from \(\Delta X\in\mathcal L\), \(\Delta S\in\mathcal L^\perp\), and \[Q(\Delta X\bar S+\bar X\Delta S)Q^{-1}+Q^{-1}(\Delta S\bar X+\bar S\Delta X)Q=\frac{2}{t_+}I-[Q\bar X\bar SQ^{-1}+Q^{-1}\bar S\bar XQ].\] Then set \(X_+=\bar X+\Delta X\) and \(S_+=\bar S+\Delta S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from strictly feasible primal and dual SDP solutions in the prescribed central-path neighborhood, increase the path parameter, select a positive-definite scaling that makes the scaled primal and dual matrices commute, solve the linearized symmetrized complementarity equation together with the primal and dual subspace equations, and add the resulting direction to the current pair.

\bar t=\frac{k}{\operatorname{Tr}(\bar X\bar S)}
\left\|\bar t\,\bar X^{1/2}\bar S\bar X^{1/2}-I\right\|_2\leq\kappa
\chi\in(0,1)
Q\succ0
(Q\bar XQ)(Q^{-1}\bar SQ^{-1})=(Q^{-1}\bar SQ^{-1})(Q\bar XQ)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_+=\bar X+\Delta X,\qquad S_+=\bar S+\Delta S,\quad (\Delta X,\Delta S)\text{ satisfies the stated linearized system with }\Delta X\in\mathcal L,\ \Delta S\in\mathcal L^\perp.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Posedness and Neighborhood Invariance of the Scaled SDP Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness, strict-feasibility preservation, neighborhood invariance, and short-step progress for the scaled primal–dual SDP update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\chi\leq\kappa\leq0.1\). Let \((\bar X,\bar S)\) be strictly feasible primal and dual solutions, set \(\bar t=k/\operatorname{Tr}(\bar X\bar S)\), and suppose \(\|\bar t\,\bar X^{1/2}\bar S\bar X^{1/2}-I\|_2\leq\kappa\). Apply update \((U)\), choosing \(Q\succ0\) so that \(Q\bar XQ\) and \(Q^{-1}\bar SQ^{-1}\) commute, and set \(t_+=(1-\chi/\sqrt{k})^{-1}\bar t\). Then the update system has a unique solution, \(X_+\) and \(S_+\) are strictly primal and dual feasible, respectively, \(t_+=k/\operatorname{Tr}(X_+S_+)\), and \((t_+,X_+,S_+)\in\mathcal N_\kappa\). Consequently, repeated updates remain in \(\mathcal N_\kappa\), increase the path parameter by a factor \(1+O(k^{-1/2})\) per step, and achieve an absolute constant-factor increase in \(O(\sqrt{k})=O(\sqrt{\theta(K)})\) steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For 0 < chi <= kappa <= 0.1, the scaled update applied to a strictly feasible SDP pair in the specified central-path neighborhood has a unique search direction. The updated pair remains strictly feasible, satisfies the trace normalization, stays in the same neighborhood, and yields a constant-factor increase in the path parameter after order square root of k updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SDP Predictor–Corrector Neighborhood Invariants and Iteration Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parity-dependent neighborhood, complementarity, and complexity guarantees for the stated primal-dual SDP predictor–corrector algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\tau\in(0,1/15]\). For every even \(k\ge 0\), \((X^k,y^k,S^k)\in\mathcal N_F(\tau)\), \(\alpha_k=1/\mathcal O(\sqrt n)\), and \(X^{k+1}\bullet S^{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)(X^k\bullet S^k)\). For every odd \(k\ge 0\), \((X^k,y^k,S^k)\in\mathcal N_F(2\tau)\) and \(X^{k+1}\bullet S^{k+1}=X^k\bullet S^k\). Consequently, the algorithm terminates in at most \(\mathcal O(\sqrt n\,L)\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the neighborhood parameter is at most 1/15, even predictor steps stay in the narrower neighborhood and reduce complementarity, while odd corrector steps stay in the doubled neighborhood and preserve complementarity. The stated SDP algorithm terminates in O(sqrt(n) L) iterations.
assumptions_latex: \text{The iterates and step sizes are generated by the stated predictor-corrector algorithm.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The parity-dependent neighborhood and complementarity properties hold, and termination occurs within }\mathcal O(\sqrt n\,L)\text{ iterations.}

children.title: Linear-Scaling Potential Reduction
children.top_down_role: Potential-reduction architectures based on linear scaling.

assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible primal matrix \(X\) and a differentiable barrier potential \(\Phi\) are available.
A descent direction exists in the primal affine tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted step preserves primal feasibility and positive definiteness and strictly decreases \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic primal linear-scaling potential-reduction template; historical variants differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a strictly feasible \(X\), set \(D=X^{1/2}\) and represent a tangent displacement as \(\Delta X=DHD\), where \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(\mathcal A(DHD)=0\). Choose \(H\) from a bounded local model, such as \(\|H\|_F\le\beta<1\), to minimize the linearization \(\langle\nabla\Phi(X),DHD\rangle\). Select \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) by backtracking until
\[X^+=D(I+\alpha H)D\succ0,\qquad \Phi(X^+)\le\Phi(X)-c\alpha\bigl|\langle\nabla\Phi(X),DHD\rangle\bigr|\]
for a fixed \(c\in(0,1)\). Repeat until the chosen potential or optimality tolerance is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear scaling expresses feasible matrix steps in coordinates normalized by the current iterate, then uses line search to obtain a positive-definite potential decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Scaling Potential Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has no citation and describes a generic scaled feasible-descent template rather than an identifiable linear-scaling potential-reduction algorithm. The potential, local model, direction rule, and convergence criterion must be tied to a specific sourced variant before the mathematical statement can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Projective-Scaling Potential Reduction
children.top_down_role: Potential-reduction architectures based on projective scaling.

assumptions_latex: A homogenized semidefinite formulation with a positive normalization functional is available.
The current normalized matrix lies in the interior of its affine cone section.

notation.meaning: Potential on the normalized cone section.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic projective normalization framework rather than a uniquely identified historical algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(Z)=\langle G,Z\rangle>0\) on the relevant cone interior and normalize rays by \(\pi(Z)=Z/g(Z)\), so \(g(\pi(Z))=1\). Starting from a feasible normalized \(Z\succ0\), choose a tangent direction \(H\) satisfying the homogeneous affine constraints and \(g(H)=0\), with a local bound ensuring \(Z+\alpha H\succ0\). Select \(\alpha>0\) by line search and set
\[Z^+=\pi(Z+\alpha H).\]
Accept the step only when all normalized affine constraints hold and \(\Phi(Z^+)<\Phi(Z)\). Iterate until the potential or projective optimality residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projective scaling works on normalized rays of a homogenized semidefinite cone and accepts positive-definite normalized steps that decrease a potential.
knowledge_statements.title: Projective-Scaling Potential Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition of the symmetric matrix-space scalings used by the SDP primal-dual potential-reduction framework; the final alternative is labeled (e.9) in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathcal S^n\to\mathcal S^n\) be linear. If (a) \(T^*=T\) and \(T\) is nonsingular; (b) \(T(S)=T^{-1}(X)=:V\); (c) \(T(X^{-1})=T^{-1}(S^{-1})=V^{-1}\); (d) \(\lambda:=\lambda_{\min}(V)=\lambda_{\min}(X^{1/2}SX^{1/2})^{1/2}\); and, as condition (e), at least one of the following holds: \((e.1)\) \(\langle d_x,TF''(X)T(d_x)\rangle\leq\eta/\lambda^2\) and \(\langle d_s,T^{-1}F''(S)T^{-1}(d_s)\rangle\leq\eta/\lambda^2\), where \(\eta>0\) is an absolute constant; \((e.2)\) \(\langle d_x,TF''(X)T(d_s)\rangle\geq0\) and \(\langle d_x,T^{-1}F''(S)T^{-1}(d_s)\rangle\geq0\); or \((e.9)\) \(T^{-1}\circ F''(S)\circ T^{-1}=T\circ F''(X)\circ T\) and \(T\) is positive definite, then \(T\in\mathcal T(X,S)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Dual SDP Potential-Reduction Scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the main iteration pattern for an SDP primal-dual potential-reduction algorithm while leaving search-direction construction unspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given (C,A_1,\ldots,A_m,b,X^0,y^0,S^0,\epsilon), set k:=0. While X^k\bullet S^k>\epsilon, choose a direction (d_x,d_y,d_s) and a step \alpha>0 satisfying \[\phi_q(X^k+\alpha d_x,S^k+\alpha d_s)\le \phi_q(X^k,S^k)-\delta,\] set \[(X^{k+1},y^{k+1},S^{k+1}):=(X^k,y^k,S^k)+\alpha(d_x,d_y,d_s),\] and increment k. Upon termination, output (X^k,y^k,S^k).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose a primal-dual direction and positive step that decrease the potential by delta, update the variables, and stop when the SDP complementarity product is at most epsilon. The extract does not specify how to construct the direction or guarantee termination.
assumptions_latex: \delta>0
q\ge 1
\alpha>0\text{ at each executed update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If the loop terminates, then }X^k\bullet S^k\le\epsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform primal-or-dual potential decrease for an SDP update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step progress alternative for the specified SDP primal-dual potential-reduction construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf x_0\) be interior primal feasible and \(\mathbf y_0\) interior dual feasible. Define \(q=r+\lceil\sqrt r\rceil\), \(\mathbf s_0=\mathbf c-A^T\mathbf y_0\), \(\underline z_0=\mathbf b^T\mathbf y_0\), \(\mathbf x_1=\mathcal T^{-1}(\widetilde{\mathbf x}_1,\widehat{\mathbf x}_1)\) as in the stated construction, \(\mathbf y_1=\mathbf y(\underline z_0)\), and \(\mathbf s_1=\mathbf s(\underline z_0)\). Then there exists an absolute constant \(\delta\) such that
\[\psi(\mathbf x_1,\mathbf s_0)\le \psi(\mathbf x_0,\mathbf s_0)-\delta\quad\text{or}\quad \psi(\mathbf x_0,\mathbf s_1)\le \psi(\mathbf x_0,\mathbf s_0)-\delta.\]
If \(\alpha=0.55\) and \(\beta=0.3\), then \(\delta>0.1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from interior primal- and dual-feasible points and forming the specified updates, either the primal update or the dual update reduces the potential by an absolute constant. For alpha equal to 0.55 and beta equal to 0.3, that constant exceeds 0.1.

\mathbf y_0\text{ is interior feasible for the dual problem}
q=r+\lceil\sqrt r\rceil
\mathbf s_0=\mathbf c-A^T\mathbf y_0,\quad \underline z_0=\mathbf b^T\mathbf y_0
\mathbf x_1=\mathcal T^{-1}(\widetilde{\mathbf x}_1,\widehat{\mathbf x}_1),\quad \mathbf y_1=\mathbf y(\underline z_0),\quad \mathbf s_1=\mathbf s(\underline z_0)

children.title: Alizadeh-Haeberly-Overton Direction
children.top_down_role: A canonical symmetrized primal-dual direction.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\).
The current iterate satisfies \((X,y,S)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S_{++}^n\), and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An AHO direction is a solution of the affine residual equations and the identity-scaled symmetrized complementarity equation displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity-scaled AHO symmetrization of the primal-dual complementarity equation for a standard-form SDP.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.2, A primal-dual interior-point method, p. 44

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(H_I(M)=(M+M^T)/2\), \(r_p=b-\mathcal A(X)\), \(r_d=C-\mathcal A^*y-S\), and \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\). The Alizadeh-Haeberly-Overton direction \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\in\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\) satisfies
\[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*\Delta y+\Delta S=r_d,\]
\[H_I(\Delta X S+X\Delta S)=\sigma\mu I-H_I(XS).\]
Equivalently, its complementarity equation is
\[\tfrac12(\Delta X S+S\Delta X+X\Delta S+\Delta S X)=\sigma\mu I-\tfrac12(XS+SX).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a standard-form SDP with the displayed residuals, the AHO direction combines the linearized primal and dual feasibility equations with the identity-scaled symmetric part of the linearized complementarity equation.

children.title: Primal HKM Direction
children.top_down_role: Primal-oriented HKM scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal HKM Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-scaled HKM Newton direction for a strictly feasible primal-dual SDP iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and set \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\). For \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), the primal HKM direction is the solution \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) of \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[\Delta X+X\Delta S X=\sigma\mu S^{-1}-X^2,\] after expressing the symmetrized complementarity equation in the primal scaling. A step length \(\alpha>0\) is chosen so that \(X+\alpha\Delta X\succ0\) and \(S+\alpha\Delta S\succ0\); the updated iterate is \((X+lpha\Delta X,y+lpha\Delta y,S+lpha\Delta S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve primal and dual feasibility Newton equations together with the primal-scaled HKM complementarity equation, then take a positivity-preserving step.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\)
The displayed Newton system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) is the primal HKM search direction.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the SDP constraint map
Current primal and dual residual right-hand sides

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no citation supports the scaling convention. The complementarity equation, especially the terms \(-X^2\) and \(\sigma\mu S^{-1}\), cannot be identified reliably as the primal HKM equation without a specialist source. The update also contains the malformed text \(lpha\) instead of \(\alpha\).

children.title: Dual HKM Direction

knowledge_statements.title: Dual HKM Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-scaled HKM Newton direction for a strictly feasible primal-dual SDP iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and set \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\). For \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), the dual HKM direction is the solution \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) of \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[\Delta S+S\Delta X S=\sigma\mu X^{-1}-S^2,\] after expressing the symmetrized complementarity equation in the dual scaling. Choose \(\alpha>0\) preserving positive definiteness and output the corresponding updated primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve feasibility Newton equations with the dual-scaled HKM complementarity equation and take a step that keeps both matrix variables positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\)
The displayed Newton system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) is the dual HKM search direction.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the SDP constraint map
Current primal and dual residual right-hand sides

children.title: Nesterov-Todd Direction
children.top_down_role: Self-scaled primal-dual direction and symmetry framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov-Todd Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-cone scaling specialized to the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), define the Nesterov--Todd scaling matrix \[W=X^{1/2}(X^{1/2}SX^{1/2})^{-1/2}X^{1/2},\] so that \(WSW=X\). Given residuals \(r_p,r_d\), centering parameter \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), and \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\), compute \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) from the primal and dual feasibility Newton equations and the complementarity equation symmetrized in the common scaling induced by \(W\), equivalently after transforming both \(X\) and \(S\) to the same matrix \(W^{-1/2}XW^{-1/2}=W^{1/2}SW^{1/2}\). Output a positivity-preserving primal-dual step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale primal and dual matrices to the same positive-definite matrix, solve the symmetrized Newton equations there, and map the direction back.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\)
The scaled Newton system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting search direction is invariant under exchanging the scaled primal and dual variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaling matrix formula is standard and the algorithm kind is appropriate, but the candidate does not state the actual symmetrized complementarity Newton equation. The conclusion asserting invariance under exchange of the scaled variables is also insufficiently specified and uncited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nesterov–Todd Scaling and Direction for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the positive-definite NT scaling matrix, the corresponding primal-dual correction equation, and its Monteiro–Zhang parameterization. Context-dependent barrier subproblem formulas are not needed for the standalone definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,S\in\mathcal S_{++}^n\) and \(\nu>0\). Define \[W_{nt}:=S^{-1/2}\bigl(S^{1/2}XS^{1/2}\bigr)^{1/2}S^{-1/2}.\] Then \(W_{nt}SW_{nt}=X\) and \(W_{nt}X^{-1}W_{nt}=S^{-1}\). The Nesterov–Todd direction is the solution of the primal-dual feasibility equations and \[\Delta X+W_{nt}\Delta S W_{nt}=\nu S^{-1}-X.\] It is a Monteiro–Zhang direction with \(P=W_{nt}^{-1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive-definite primal and dual matrices, the Nesterov–Todd scaling is the metric geometric-mean scaling characterized by WSW=X. Using it in the primal-dual correction equation defines the NT direction, which is the Monteiro–Zhang specialization P=W^{-1/2}.
assumptions_latex: X,S\in\mathcal S_{++}^n
\nu>0
(\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\text{ satisfies the primal-dual feasibility equations}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{nt}SW_{nt}=X,\quad W_{nt}X^{-1}W_{nt}=S^{-1},\quad \Delta X+W_{nt}\Delta S W_{nt}=\nu S^{-1}-X,\quad P=W_{nt}^{-1/2}.

children.title: Kojima-Shindoh-Hara Family
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual directions organized through KSH symmetrization.

knowledge_statements.title: Kojima-Shindoh-Hara Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KSH symmetrization of the nonsymmetric matrix complementarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an invertible matrix \(P\), define \[H_P(M)=\tfrac12\bigl(PMP^{-1}+P^{-\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\bigr).\] At \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), a KSH-family direction \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) satisfies the linearized feasibility equations and \[H_P(\Delta X\,S+X\,\Delta S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS),\qquad \mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n.\] The parameter matrix \(P\) may depend on the current iterate; admissible choices are those for which the equation is a symmetric, well-defined Newton equation and the complete linear system determines a direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KSH directions arise by applying a similarity-based symmetrization to the linearized matrix complementarity equation, with the scaling matrix selecting the family member.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\)
\(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equation defines the complementarity component of the KSH direction family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is a suitable kind for this family, but the record gives a general similarity symmetrization without evidence that it exactly characterizes the Kojima-Shindoh-Hara family. The conditions distinguishing admissible KSH parameters from the broader Monteiro-Zhang framework are not supplied.

children.title: Monteiro-Tsuchiya Family
children.top_down_role: Direction families covered by extended path-following analyses.

knowledge_statements.title: Monteiro-Tsuchiya Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled symmetrization family used in path-following analyses of SDP directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\), and let \(P=P(X,S)\) be an invertible scaling selected from the Monteiro--Tsuchiya admissible class. The associated direction solves the linearized primal and dual feasibility equations together with \[H_P(\Delta X\,S+X\,\Delta S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS),\] where \[H_P(M)=\tfrac12\bigl(PMP^{-1}+P^{-\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\bigr).\] Different admissible scaling rules \(P(X,S)\) produce distinct members while retaining a symmetric complementarity equation suitable for path-following analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Monteiro–Tsuchiya family selects iterate-dependent scalings inside a common symmetrized complementarity Newton equation.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\)
\(P(X,S)\) belongs to the admissible Monteiro–Tsuchiya scaling class
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each admissible scaling rule determines one Monteiro--Tsuchiya primal-dual direction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits a direction-family container, but membership is defined only by reference to an unspecified Monteiro-Tsuchiya admissible class. A primary or authoritative secondary source is required to state the parameter class and distinguish this family from the general symmetrization framework.

children.title: Monteiro-Zhang Direction Framework
children.top_down_role: The organizing symmetrization framework associated with Monteiro-Zhang directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Monteiro-Zhang Direction Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified symmetrized Newton framework for primal-dual SDP search directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual SDP equations with \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). For any invertible \(P\), set \[H_P(M)=\tfrac12\bigl(PMP^{-1}+P^{-\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\bigr).\] The Monteiro--Zhang direction associated with \(P\) is the solution of \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[H_P(\Delta X\,S+X\,\Delta S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS),\qquad \mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n.\] Thus the feasibility linearization is fixed, while the choice of \(P\) determines the symmetrization and hence the direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monteiro–Zhang directions share the feasibility Newton equations and differ through an invertible scaling used to symmetrize linearized complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S	ext{ are in }mathbb S_{++}^n\)
\(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible
The complete Newton system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each admissible \(P\) determines a member of the Monteiro--Zhang direction framework.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the framework leaf, and the displayed symmetrization has a plausible standard form, but its attribution and residual conventions are unsupported. The assumption string also contains malformed notation, \(mathbb S_{++}^n\), rather than \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\).

children.title: Symmetrization Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter choices distinguishing direction variants within the broader framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetrization Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a scaling parameter defines a valid symmetric Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), a parameter rule \(P=P(X,S)\) is admissible for the similarity symmetrization \[H_P(M)=\tfrac12\bigl(PMP^{-1}+P^{-\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\bigr)\] only if \(P\) is real and invertible and the resulting linearized primal-dual system maps symmetric unknowns \(\Delta X,\Delta S\in\mathbb S^n\) to a symmetric complementarity equation. For algorithmic use, the combined feasibility and complementarity operator must additionally be nonsingular at the iterate. Orthogonal left multiplication leaves the symmetrization unchanged: \(H_{QP}=H_P\) for every orthogonal \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetrization parameter must be invertible, preserve a symmetric complementarity equation, and yield a nonsingular full Newton system; orthogonal left factors are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\)
\(P=P(X,S)\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\)
\(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\) when equivalence is invoked
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible parameters define well-posed directions, and \(P\) and \(QP\) define the same symmetrization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the claimed identity \(H_{QP}=H_P\) is generally false. With the displayed definition one obtains \(H_{QP}(M)=QH_P(M)Q^{\mathsf T}\), so orthogonal left multiplication gives an orthogonally congruent equation rather than the same operator. The broader necessity and sufficiency claims also require a source before a reliable replacement can be formulated.

children.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Maps
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices used to symmetrize primal-dual SDP systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence scalings preserving the positive-semidefinite cone and its trace pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an invertible \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), define the primal and dual congruence maps on \(\mathbb S^n\) by \[\mathcal T_W(X)=W^{-1}XW^{-\mathsf T},\qquad \mathcal T_W^{-*}(S)=W^{\mathsf T}SW.\] Both maps preserve positive definiteness, and they preserve the primal-dual pairing: \[\langle \mathcal T_W(X),\mathcal T_W^{-*}(S)\rangle=\langle X,S\rangle.\] A primal-dual scaling map is such a paired transformation, possibly with \(W\) chosen from the current interior iterate, used to express complementarity and its Newton linearization in scaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paired congruence maps scale primal and dual matrices inversely, preserve positivity, and leave their trace pairing unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible
\(X,S\in\mathbb S^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_W\) and \(\mathcal T_W^{-*}\) preserve the cone and satisfy pairing invariance.

notation.meaning: Real symmetric matrices of order n

children.title: Direction–Scaling Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between search-direction families and scaling choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Direction–Scaling Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search directions induced by choices of primal-dual scaling coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be an invertible scaling and transform \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) by \(\widehat X=W^{-1}XW^{-\mathsf T}\) and \(\widehat S=W^{\mathsf T}SW\). Linearize the chosen symmetric complementarity equation in the scaled variables, obtaining \((\Delta\widehat X,\Delta\widehat S)\). Mapping back by \[\Delta X=W\Delta\widehat XW^{\mathsf T},\qquad \Delta S=W^{-\mathsf T}\Delta\widehat SW^{-1}\] produces a primal-dual direction in the original coordinates. Scalings that induce the same symmetrization operator produce the same direction whenever the full Newton system has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaling selects coordinates for symmetric complementarity linearization; inverse congruence maps then give the corresponding original-coordinate search direction.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(W\) is invertible
The scaled complementarity equation is differentiable
The full Newton system has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent symmetrizations correspond to the same uniquely determined primal-dual direction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the correspondence leaf, and the inverse congruence formulas are consistent. However, the claim that identical symmetrization operators necessarily produce the same complete primal-dual direction depends on how feasibility equations and scaling-dependent terms are transformed; those hypotheses and the claimed equivalence class need an authoritative source.

children.title: Dense Schur-Complement Solves
children.top_down_role: Direct-factorization regimes for moderate constraint dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Schur-Complement Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage costs for direct dense factorization of the SDP Schur system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the reduced Newton equation be \(H\Delta y=g\) with dense symmetric positive-definite \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\). A dense Cholesky factorization \(H=LL^{\mathsf T}\) requires \(m^3/3+O(m^2)\) arithmetic operations and stores \(m(m+1)/2\) scalar entries for \(L\). Each subsequent solve with the same factorization requires two triangular substitutions and \(O(m^2)\) operations. These bounds exclude the application-dependent cost of assembling \(H\), which in an SDP can dominate factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense Cholesky costs one-third m cubed operations and quadratic storage; each solve afterward is quadratic, excluding Schur-matrix assembly.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\) is explicitly assembled and dense
Classical scalar arithmetic is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization cost is \(m^3/3+O(m^2)\), storage is \(m(m+1)/2\), and each solve costs \(O(m^2)\).

children.title: Sparse Schur-Complement Solves
children.top_down_role: Sparse-factorization regimes governed by fill and ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Schur-Complement Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fill-sensitive cost model for sparse direct solution of an SDP Schur system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\) be a sparse Schur-complement matrix and let \(\Pi H\Pi^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\) be a Cholesky factorization under a symmetric permutation \(\Pi\). Storage is \(\Theta(\operatorname{nnz}(L))\), a triangular solve costs \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(L))\), and numeric factorization costs \[O\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^m \ell_j^2\right),\] where \(\ell_j\) is the number of nonzeros in column \(j\) of \(L\). Consequently, sparsity of \(H\) alone gives no fixed complexity bound: elimination ordering and fill determine the cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse Cholesky storage and solve time depend on factor fill, while factorization depends on squared factor-column counts; ordering can change all three substantially.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\)
A symmetric elimination ordering \(\Pi\) is fixed
Scalar sparse Cholesky arithmetic is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Storage and arithmetic are governed by the nonzero pattern of \(L\), not solely by \(\operatorname{nnz}(H)\).

notation.meaning: Number of stored nonzeros in the Cholesky factor
Nonzero count in column j of L

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the sparse-solve leaf, and the fill-sensitive qualitative conclusion is plausible. No citation is supplied for the precise \(O(\sum_j\ell_j^2)\) factorization model or its column-count convention, so the quantitative statement cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Augmented KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Unreduced saddle-point representations of Newton equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unreduced saddle-point form of a primal-dual Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\) represent the linearized constraints and let \(G\in\mathbb S_{++}^q\) represent the scaled complementarity operator after vectorizing symmetric matrix variables. The Newton equations may be retained as the augmented KKT system \[\begin{pmatrix}G&A^{\mathsf T}\\ A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta z\\ \Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_z\\ r_p\end{pmatrix}.\] Eliminating \(\Delta z=G^{-1}(r_z-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y)\) gives the Schur equation \[(AG^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})\Delta y=AG^{-1}r_z-r_p.\] Thus the augmented and reduced systems are equivalent whenever \(G\) is invertible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unreduced Newton equations form a symmetric saddle-point system; eliminating the matrix-variable step yields the usual Schur-complement equation.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S_{++}^q\)
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\)
The right-hand sides have compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented KKT system is algebraically equivalent to the displayed Schur-complement system.

notation.meaning: Vectorized primal or matrix-variable Newton step

children.title: Preconditioned Krylov Solvers
children.top_down_role: Iterative linear solvers with SDP-specific preconditioning.

assumptions_latex: The SDP Newton equations have been reduced to an SPD Schur-complement system \(H\Delta y=b\).
The preconditioner \(P\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate \(\Delta y_k\) satisfies the prescribed relative preconditioned-residual tolerance, and its convergence is governed by \(\kappa(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\).

notation.meaning: SPD Schur-complement matrix and right-hand side
Newton-direction approximation at Krylov step k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned conjugate gradients applied to an SPD SDP Schur-complement equation.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.3 Structured linear algebra p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\Delta y_0\), set \(r_0=b-H\Delta y_0\), solve \(Pz_0=r_0\), and set \(p_0=z_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \(q_k=Hp_k\), \(\alpha_k=(r_k^{\mathsf T}z_k)/(p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k)\), \(\Delta y_{k+1}=\Delta y_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and \(r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kq_k\). Stop when \(\|r_{k+1}\|_{P^{-1}}\leq\tau\|b\|_{P^{-1}}\). Otherwise solve \(Pz_{k+1}=r_{k+1}\), set \(\beta_k=(r_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}z_{k+1})/(r_k^{\mathsf T}z_k)\), and \(p_{k+1}=z_{k+1}+\beta_kp_k\). In exact arithmetic, the standard CG estimate depends on \(\kappa(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply preconditioned conjugate gradients to the positive-definite SDP Schur system, stopping when the preconditioned residual is relatively small; a clustered preconditioned spectrum yields faster convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Krylov Solvers

children.title: Inexact-Newton Interior-Point Methods
children.top_down_role: Path-following methods using controlled approximate Newton solutions.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual iterates remain in a prescribed central neighborhood.
Each exact Newton matrix \(J_k\) is nonsingular and the computed direction has residual \(r_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Controlled forcing terms preserve the intended path-following progress; if \(\eta_k\to0\), the local inexact-Newton convergence can become superlinear under the usual regularity assumptions.

notation.meaning: KKT residual mapping and its Jacobian

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic feasible primal-dual path following with residual-controlled Newton solves.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 A primal-dual interior-point method p. 44
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(w_k\), choose a target \(\mu_{k+1}<\mu_k\) and compute an approximate direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(J_kd_k=-F_{mu_{k+1}}(w_k)+r_k\) with \(\|r_k\|_{J_k^{-1}}\leq\eta_k\|F_{mu_{k+1}}(w_k)\|_{J_k^{-1}}\), where \(0\leq\eta_k<1\). Choose the largest accepted step \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) that preserves positive definiteness and the designated central neighborhood, and set \(w_{k+1}=w_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop when the primal residual, dual residual, and normalized duality gap are at most \(\varepsilon\). The forcing sequence must be small enough that linear-solve error does not dominate the neighborhood contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve each primal-dual Newton equation, bound its residual by a forcing term, preserve positivity and centrality by step control, and stop when feasibility and gap tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Newton Interior-Point Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 A primal-dual interior-point method p. 44
source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A general KKT Jacobian need not define the norm involving its inverse, and the displayed residual test therefore requires a sourced formulation and norm. The expression uses a literal subscript "mu" rather than the introduced barrier parameter, and the superlinear-convergence conclusion is absent from the statement and lacks explicit regularity hypotheses.

children.title: Structured-Data Interior-Point Linear Algebra
children.top_down_role: Newton-system reductions exploiting block, sparse, or low-rank coefficient structure.

assumptions_latex: The constraint matrices admit known block, sparse, or low-rank representations.
The chosen primal-dual scaling matrices preserve compatible structure or permit structured matrix products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton system can be assembled and applied through blockwise, sparse, or low-rank operations without forming every dense \(n\times n\) intermediate.

notation.meaning: scaling operator acting on symmetric matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural representation of the SDP Schur complement, independent of a particular scaling choice.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.3 Structured linear algebra p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the scaled Schur matrix have entries \(H_{ij}=\langle A_i,\mathcal W(A_j)\rangle\). If \(A_i=\operatorname{diag}(A_i^{(1)},\ldots,A_i^{(q)})\) and \(\mathcal W\) acts blockwise, then \(H_{ij}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{q}\langle A_i^{(\ell)},\mathcal W_\ell(A_j^{(\ell)})\rangle\). If instead \(A_i=U_iV_i^{\mathsf T}+V_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\) with low column dimension, each inner product reduces to products involving the thin factors and the scaling action. Sparse representations analogously permit sparse assembly or matrix-free products \(v\mapsto Hv\). Thus structured Newton algebra is obtained by evaluating the same Schur operator through the supplied structure rather than changing the Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express the SDP Schur operator as sums of blockwise, sparse, or thin-factor operations, avoiding unnecessary dense intermediates while retaining the original Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Data Interior-Point Linear Algebra

The initial point lies in a fixed narrow central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-accurate point is obtained in \(O(\sqrt{\nu}\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton iterations; for the \(n\times n\) positive-semidefinite cone, \(\nu=n\).

children.title: Long-Step Complexity Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity organization for broad central neighborhoods.

assumptions_latex: A primal-dual method uses a fixed broad central neighborhood.
Each damped Newton step preserves that neighborhood and reduces \(\mu\) by a factor at most \(1-c/\nu\), for constant \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of Newton iterations needed for \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon\) is \(O(\nu\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\), hence \(O(n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) for \(\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative broad-neighborhood bound under an explicit per-step reduction hypothesis.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If accepted long steps satisfy \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-c/
u)\mu_k\) while retaining the iterate in a fixed broad central neighborhood, then \(\mu_k\leq(1-c/
u)^k\mu_0\leq\exp(-ck/
u)\mu_0\). Consequently, \(k\geq(
u/c)\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\) suffices for \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon\), and the iteration bound is \(O(
u\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\). For the logarithmic-determinant barrier on \(\mathbb S_+^n\), \(
u=n\). Faster bounds require stronger neighborhood and step-decrease properties of the particular long-step method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a broad-neighborhood reduction of order one over the barrier parameter per step, long-step path following needs order barrier-parameter times logarithmic-gap iterations.
