children.title: Potential-Reduction Complexity Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity organization through potential decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Potential-Reduction Complexity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract potential-decrease accounting applicable to primal-dual SDP potential-reduction methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi\) be a primal-dual potential such that \(\Phi(w)\leq\Phi_{\mathrm{tar}}\) implies the required feasibility and duality-gap accuracy. If every nonterminal iteration satisfies \(\Phi(w_{k+1})\leq\Phi(w_k)-\delta\) for a constant \(\delta>0\), then termination occurs within \(\left\lceil(\Phi(w_0)-\Phi_{\mathrm{tar}})/\delta\right\rceil\) iterations. This bound is polynomial when the initial potential excess and \(1/\delta\) are polynomially bounded in the SDP dimensions and the logarithm of the requested accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every nonterminal iteration decreases a qualifying primal-dual potential by at least a fixed positive amount, the initial potential excess divided by that decrease bounds the iteration count; polynomial parameter bounds yield polynomial complexity.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm maintains a potential \(\Phi_k\) bounded below by \(\Phi_{\mathrm{tar}}\).
Every nonterminal iteration decreases the potential by at least \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination occurs within \(\left\lceil(\Phi_0-\Phi_{\mathrm{tar}})/\delta\right\rceil\) iterations; polynomial bounds on the potential range and reciprocal decrease yield polynomial SDP complexity.

children.top_down_role: Computational scaling determined by matrix order, constraint count, and factorization structure.

children.title: Per-Iteration Computational Cost
children.top_down_role: Work incurred by one interior-point iteration.

assumptions_latex: The SDP has one dense \(n\times n\) matrix variable and \(m\) dense equality constraints.
A dense Schur-complement primal-dual implementation is used with classical matrix multiplication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One Newton iteration costs \(O(mn^3+m^2n^2+m^3)\) arithmetic operations and requires \(O(n^2+mn^2+m^2)\) stored scalars when all dense constraint matrices and the Schur matrix are stored.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative dense-arithmetic model; exploitable sparsity and fast multiplication are excluded.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.3 Structured linear algebra p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a dense Schur-complement implementation, factoring or applying the scaling matrices costs \(O(n^3)\); transforming all \(m\) dense constraint matrices costs at most \(O(mn^3)\); forming their \(m^2\) pairwise trace inner products costs \(O(m^2n^2)\); and factoring the dense \(m\times m\) Schur matrix costs \(O(m^3)\). Lower-order triangular solves and residual updates do not change the bound. Thus a conservative per-iteration cost is \(O(mn^3+m^2n^2+m^3)\), with storage \(O(n^2+mn^2+m^2)\). This count assumes classical dense kernels and explicit storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conservative dense Schur-complement iteration costs order m n-cubed plus m-squared n-squared plus m-cubed operations, with explicit dense constraint and Schur storage.
knowledge_statements.title: Per-Iteration Computational Cost

children.title: Arithmetic Complexity Bounds
children.top_down_role: Aggregate arithmetic cost across an SDP interior-point solve.

assumptions_latex: A short-step SDP method uses the logarithmic-determinant barrier on \(\mathbb S_+^n\).
Each dense Newton iteration has cost \(C(n,m)=O(mn^3+m^2n^2+m^3)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total dense arithmetic cost to reduce the duality-gap parameter from \(\mu_0\) to \(\varepsilon\) is \(O(C(n,m)\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total arithmetic count obtained by composing dense per-iteration cost with short-step iteration complexity.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.3 Structured linear algebra p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the logarithmic-determinant barrier, the short-step iteration bound is \(O(\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\). If every iteration is implemented by dense Schur-complement algebra costing \(C(n,m)=O(mn^3+m^2n^2+m^3)\), multiplication of the two bounds gives total arithmetic work \(O((mn^3+m^2n^2+m^3)\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\). This is an arithmetic-operation bound: it excludes bit-length growth, finite-precision stabilization, preprocessing, and structure-dependent reductions. Replacing the dense linear-algebra kernel replaces \(C(n,m)\) but not this composition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying the dense cost of one Newton step by the short-step iteration count gives the total arithmetic bound, excluding bit complexity and finite-precision effects.
knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic Complexity Bounds

children.title: Factorization-Structure Cost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cost variation induced by matrix order, constraint count, sparsity, and factorization structure.

assumptions_latex: The Newton equations reduce to an SPD Schur system \(H\Delta y=b\).
An elimination ordering and block partition for \(H\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization cost is controlled by the nonzero pattern of the Cholesky factor, ranging from blockwise sums to dense cubic cost; iterative application replaces factorization by structured matvec and preconditioner costs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost regimes induced by block structure, sparse fill, or matrix-free iterative solution.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.3 Structured linear algebra p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a permutation makes \(H\) block diagonal with block orders \(m_1,\ldots,m_q\), direct Cholesky factorization costs \(O(\sum_{j=1}^{q}m_j^3)\), rather than \(O(m^3)\). For a general sparse ordering with Cholesky factor \(L\), the numerical work is proportional, up to implementation constants, to \(\sum_{j=1}^{m}|L_{:,j}|^2\), while storage is \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(L))\); fill therefore determines the sparse-direct regime. If \(H\) is used only through products, a Krylov solve costs the iteration count times the cost of one structured product and one preconditioner application. These regimes concern solving the reduced system and do not include Schur-operator assembly unless it is performed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block diagonal structure gives a sum of block-cubic costs, sparse direct cost follows Cholesky fill, and matrix-free cost equals Krylov iterations times operator and preconditioner costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Structure Cost Regimes

children.title: Regular Solution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local solver behavior near regular primal-dual solutions.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual SDP KKT mapping \(F(w)=0\) is continuously differentiable near a solution \(w^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution is regular exactly when \(DF(w^*)\) is nonsingular; then it is locally isolated and the Newton equation has a unique direction near \(w^*\).

notation.meaning: primal-dual variables collected into one vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobian regularity of a fixed smooth local KKT formulation.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37
source_refs.source_title: Handbook of Semidefinite Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed smooth local formulation of the primal-dual KKT equations \(F(w)=0\), a solution \(w^*\) is regular when the linear map \(DF(w^*)\) is bijective on the formulation's ambient variable space. Equivalently in finite dimensions, \(\ker DF(w^*)=\{0\}\) and the domain and codomain have equal dimension. By local invertibility, this condition makes \(w^*\) an isolated zero and ensures that \(DF(w)d=-F(w)\) has a unique solution for every \(w\) sufficiently near \(w^*\). The definition is formulation-dependent when redundant constraints or nonsmooth complementarity equations are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular primal-dual solution has an invertible Jacobian for the chosen smooth KKT equations, making the local solution isolated and nearby Newton directions unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Solution Regimes

children.title: Strictly Complementary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local solver behavior near strictly complementary solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Complementary Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict complementarity for a primal-dual SDP optimal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an optimal primal-dual pair \((X^*,S^*)\) with \(X^*\succeq0\), \(S^*\succeq0\), and \(\langle X^*,S^*\rangle=0\), strict complementarity means \(X^*+S^*\succ0\). Equivalently, \(\operatorname{range}(X^*)\oplus\operatorname{range}(S^*)=\mathbb R^n\), or \(\operatorname{rank}(X^*)+\operatorname{rank}(S^*)=n\). The condition applies to the selected optimal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual SDP optimal pair is strictly complementary when the primal matrix and dual slack have complementary ranges spanning the whole space, equivalently when their ranks sum to the matrix order.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual optimal slack matrices satisfy \(X^*\succeq0\), \(S^*\succeq0\), and \(\langle X^*,S^*\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict complementarity holds exactly when \(X^*+S^*\succ0\), equivalently when \(\operatorname{rank}(X^*)+\operatorname{rank}(S^*)=n\).

children.title: Regularity–Complementarity Interaction
children.top_down_role: Local regimes determined jointly by regularity and complementarity structure.

assumptions_latex: A smooth, nonredundant local KKT formulation is used near an optimal pair \((X^*,S^*)\).
The pair is strictly complementary and the primal and dual constraint systems are nondegenerate on their active faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized KKT operator is nonsingular, so the optimal pair is locally isolated and the exact Newton iteration is locally quadratically convergent when started sufficiently close.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth KKT analysis under strict complementarity and two-sided nondegeneracy.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37
source_refs.source_title: Handbook of Semidefinite Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strict complementarity decomposes \(\mathbb R^n\) into the orthogonal ranges of \(X^*\) and \(S^*\), thereby fixing the local active-face geometry. If, in addition, the primal and dual constraint systems are nondegenerate on these faces and redundant KKT equations have been removed, the homogeneous linearized KKT system has only the zero solution. Hence \(DF(w^*)\) is nonsingular and \(w^*\) is a regular, locally isolated solution. If \(DF\) is locally Lipschitz, exact Newton iterates started sufficiently near \(w^*\) satisfy \(\|w_{k+1}-w^*\|\leq C\|w_k-w^*\|^2\) for some \(C>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity fixes the active-face splitting; combined with primal and dual nondegeneracy, it makes the reduced KKT Jacobian invertible and supports local quadratic Newton convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity–Complementarity Interaction

children.title: Rank-Changing Solution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local behavior near solutions with unstable primal or dual ranks.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Changing Solution Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local nonconstancy of the ranks of selected optimal SDP matrices under perturbation of problem data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\subseteq\mathbb R\), let \(t_0\) be an accumulation point of \(T\), and let \(X:T\to\mathbb S_+^n\) select an optimal primal matrix for each parameter. A rank-changing solution regime occurs at \(t_0\) when, for every neighborhood \(U\) of \(t_0\), there exist \(t,s\in U\cap T\) such that \(\operatorname{rank}X(t)\ne\operatorname{rank}X(s)\). Thus the selected nearby solutions cannot all be modeled by one fixed-rank matrix stratum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected family of optimal SDP matrices is in a rank-changing regime at a parameter value when every neighborhood contains selected solutions of different ranks, precluding one fixed-rank local stratum.
assumptions_latex: \(T\subseteq\mathbb R\), \(t_0\) is an accumulation point of \(T\), and \(X:T\to\mathbb S_+^n\) selects an optimal primal matrix for each \(t\in T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No neighborhood of \(t_0\) has constant rank for the selected solutions \(X(t)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system is weakly feasible when \(F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\ne\varnothing\) but \(F\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n=\varnothing\). Hence every feasible matrix is singular. Equivalently, the affine space \(\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\) intersects the positive-semidefinite cone but does not intersect its interior. Interior-point analyses requiring a strictly feasible primal starting point therefore do not apply directly to this formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly feasible SDP has feasible positive-semidefinite matrices, but every feasible matrix is singular, so primal Slater feasibility is absent.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible slice is contained in the boundary of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) and must be reduced to a proper face before it has cone-relative interior.

The feasible set is then contained in a proper face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\). Replacing the ambient cone by the minimal face containing \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n\) can restore relative strict feasibility, but the unreduced formulation has no positive-definite feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty spectrahedron has missing interior when its affine slice meets the semidefinite cone only on a proper face.

children.title: Central-Path Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Loss of ordinary central-path behavior near weakly feasible or boundary-only systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexistence of the standard strictly feasible primal-dual central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\). The standard primal-dual central path consists of \(X(\mu),S(\mu)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(y(\mu)\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(X(\mu))=b\), \(\mathcal A^*(y(\mu))+S(\mu)=C\), and \(X(\mu)S(\mu)=\mu I_n\) for \(\mu>0\). If the primal affine constraints contain no positive-definite \(X\), or the dual affine constraints contain no positive-definite slack \(S\), these equations have no solution. The unreduced standard central path therefore does not exist, although facial reduction may yield a path within smaller faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard primal-dual central path cannot exist when either the primal affine constraints or the dual affine slack constraints have no positive-definite feasible matrix; facial reduction may instead produce a path in smaller faces.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and the standard path requires \(X(\mu),S(\mu)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) for every \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If either affine feasible set contains no positive-definite matrix, the standard primal-dual central path does not exist.

notation.meaning: Linear constraint map and its adjoint.
Constraint right-hand side and symmetric objective matrix.
Primal matrix, dual multiplier, and dual slack on the central path.

children.title: Schur-Complement Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Linear-system instability caused by degeneracy and scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of the dense Newton Schur system under anisotropic semidefinite scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scaled Schur matrix \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) defined by \(H_{ij}=\langle A_i,WA_jW\rangle\), take \(n\) diagonal constraints \(A_i=e_ie_i^{\mathsf T}\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_n)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Then \(H=\operatorname{diag}(w_1^2,\ldots,w_n^2)\), and consequently \(\kappa_2(H)=\kappa_2(W)^2\). Thus anisotropy in this scaling is squared in the condition number of the Schur system even though the constraint matrices are orthonormal in the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For n diagonal orthonormal constraints, the Schur matrix condition number equals the square of the diagonal scaling matrix condition number.
assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), \(A_i=e_ie_i^{\mathsf T}\), and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_n)\) with \(w_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For this diagonal specialization, \(\kappa_2(H)=\kappa_2(W)^2\).

notation.meaning: The i-th standard coordinate vector in real n-space.
Trace inner product of symmetric matrices.

children.title: Memory Saturation
children.top_down_role: Solver limits caused by exhausted factorization or iterate storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard memory threshold for storing one packed dense triangular Schur factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a dense triangular factor of order \(m\) is stored in packed form, each scalar occupies \(q>0\) bytes, and indexing and allocator overhead are excluded. The factor then requires exactly \(q m(m+1)/2\) bytes. For a factor-storage budget \(B>0\), memory saturation occurs whenever \(q m(m+1)/2>B\). Additional Schur matrices, work arrays, pivot data, and iterates can only reduce the memory available to this factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A packed dense triangular factor exceeds a B-byte factor-storage budget when q times m(m+1)/2 is greater than B; other arrays can lower the practical threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(B>0\) is the factor-storage budget, \(q>0\) is the number of bytes per scalar, \(m\in\mathbb N\), and the triangular factor is stored in packed form without indexing or allocator overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The packed dense factor cannot fit in its prescribed memory budget when \(q m(m+1)/2>B\).

assumptions_latex: An interior-point implementation stores a constant number of unstructured dense matrices in \(\mathbb S^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense symmetric \(n\times n\) iterate needs \(n(n+1)/2\) stored scalars. Hence storing \(k\) primal, slack, scaling, and workspace matrices requires at least \(k n(n+1)/2=\Theta(kn^2)\) scalars. A full dense eigendecomposition or Cholesky factorization of one such matrix additionally costs \(\Theta(n^3)\) arithmetic. Thus increasing the semidefinite block order creates a quadratic-memory and cubic-spectral-work boundary even before the constraint Schur system is counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense semidefinite iterates require quadratic memory in block order, while their full factorizations or eigendecompositions require cubic arithmetic.

children.title: Finite-Precision Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Accuracy loss in poorly scaled or nearly singular instances.

assumptions_latex: A Newton system \(H\Delta y=r\) is solved in floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(u\kappa_2(H)\) approaches one, reliable forward accuracy can vanish and residual reduction may stagnate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy boundary for finite-precision Newton solves in ill-conditioned SDP iterations.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Algorithms and Software p. 41
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a backward-stable solve of \(H\Delta y=r\), the computed step solves \((H+E)\widehat{\Delta y}=r\) with \(\|E\|_2/\|H\|_2=O(u)\). Provided \(\kappa_2(H)\|E\|_2/\|H\|_2<1\), the relative forward error is bounded to first order by \(O(u\kappa_2(H))\). When \(u\kappa_2(H)\) is not small, meaningful digits in the Newton direction can be lost, so computed feasibility or complementarity residuals may cease decreasing despite exact-arithmetic progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A backward-stable Newton solve can still lose all useful digits when the system condition number is comparable to the reciprocal of machine precision.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Stagnation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the trace-normalized SDP \[p^*=\max\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ \operatorname{tr}X=1,\ X\succeq0\},\] maximizing the Lagrangian over \(\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{tr}X=1\}\) gives \(\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^*(y))\). Under strong duality, \[p^*=\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\bigl\{b^{\mathsf T}y+\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^*(y))\bigr\}.\] The reformulated dual is convex and generally nonsmooth where its largest eigenvalue has multiplicity greater than one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trace-normalized SDP dualizes to minimizing a linear function plus the largest eigenvalue of an affine symmetric matrix.

children.title: Primal Spectral Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Primal spectral models supporting eigenvector-based recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Spectral Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact maximum-eigenvalue penalty form of a primal SDP, with recovery from active eigenvectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the primal SDP \(p^*=\max\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and its dual \(\min_y b^{\mathsf T}y\) subject to \(\mathcal A^*y-C\succeq0\). If a primal optimum exists and \(\rho>\operatorname{tr}(X^*)\) for some primal optimum \(X^*\), then
\[
p^*=\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left[b^{\mathsf T}y+\rho\max\{\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^*y),0\}\right].
\]
At a minimizer, subgradients of the eigenvalue term are convex combinations of projectors onto its active maximum eigenspace. Multiplying such a combination by \(\rho\) yields a positive-semidefinite candidate whose feasibility equations provide a verifiable primal-recovery test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large trace penalty converts the SDP dual constraint into a maximum-eigenvalue objective; active eigenvectors then furnish candidate primal matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and primal-dual strong duality holds.
A primal optimum \(X^*\) exists.
\(\rho>\operatorname{tr}(X^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\min_y b^{\mathsf T}y+\rho\max\{\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^*y),0\}\), with primal candidates recoverable from active-eigenspace projectors.

children.title: Proximal Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Stabilized bundle models for nonsmooth SDP reformulations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
The oracle returns \(f(y)\) and some \(g\in\partial f(y)\) at every queried \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
The finite model is exact at the center: \(m_k(\bar y_k)=f(\bar y_k)\).
\(t_k>0\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration accepts a serious step when \(f(\bar y_k)-f(y_{k+1})\ge\eta\delta_k\), takes a null step otherwise, and terminates when \(\delta_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard stabilized cutting-plane method for a finite convex objective, including an explicit serious-step test.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 A short description of standard bundle methods p. 61
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I_k\) be a nonempty finite index set. Given a center \(\bar y_k\), oracle cuts \((y_i,f_i,g_i)\) satisfying \(f_i=f(y_i)\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\), define
\[
m_k(y)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(y-y_i)\}.
\]
For \(t_k>0\), compute
\[
y_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{m_k(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|y-\bar y_k\|^2\right\}
\]
and set \(\delta_k=f(\bar y_k)-m_k(y_{k+1})\). For a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), accept \(y_{k+1}\) as the new center when \(f(\bar y_k)-f(y_{k+1})\ge\eta\delta_k\); otherwise retain \(\bar y_k\) and take a null step. Add a new oracle cut at \(y_{k+1}\), optionally aggregate old cuts, and terminate when \(\delta_k\le\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle method minimizes an exact-at-center cutting-plane model plus a quadratic stabilizer, accepts a serious step when the actual decrease is a prescribed fraction of the explicitly defined predicted decrease, and otherwise refines the model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique proximal trial point and aggregate-error identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the unique stabilized cutting-model minimizer and relates its aggregate error, predicted decrease, and aggregate-subgradient norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mu_k>0\) and \(M_k>0\), the problem
\[
\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\check f_k(y)+\frac12\mu_k\|y-x_k\|_k^2\right\}
\]
has the unique solution
\[
y_{k+1}:=x_k-\frac1{\mu_k}W_k\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i g_i,
\]
where \(\bar\alpha\in\mathbb R^k\) solves the associated coefficient problem. Define
\[
\delta_k:=f(x_k)-\check f_k(y_{k+1})+\bar\varepsilon- rac12\mu_k\|y_{k+1}-x_k\|_k^2,
\qquad
\bar g_k:=\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i g_i.
\]
Then
\[
0\le\varepsilon_k:=\bar\alpha^T\widetilde e_k
=\delta_k-\frac1{2\mu_k}\|\bar g_k\|_{*,k}^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilized bundle model has a unique trial point given by a metric step along the aggregate subgradient. Its aggregate linearization error is nonnegative and equals the predicted-decrease quantity minus a squared dual-norm correction.
assumptions_latex: \mu_k>0
M_k>0
\bar\alpha\in\mathbb R^k\text{ solves the associated coefficient problem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_{k+1}=x_k-\frac1{\mu_k}W_k\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i g_i,\qquad 0\le\varepsilon_k=\bar\alpha^T\widetilde e_k=\delta_k-\frac1{2\mu_k}\|\bar g_k\|_{*,k}^2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence alternative for a proximal bundle sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded convergence result for the proximal bundle algorithm in the maximum-eigenvalue optimization context; the algorithm and update condition remain referenced by their source numbering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{x^k\}\) be generated by Algorithm 11.3.1 with \(\delta=0\), \(M_k=I_m\), and an update step satisfying (11.4.22). Then either \(\{x^k\}\) converges to a minimizer of \(f\), or \(f\) has no minimizer and \(\lVert x^k\rVert\to\infty\). In both cases, \(f(x^k)\downarrow\inf f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated algorithm parameters and update condition, the proximal bundle iterates either converge to a minimizer or, when no minimizer exists, become unbounded in norm. In either case, the objective values decrease to the infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\{x^k\}\text{ is generated by Algorithm 11.3.1}\)
\(\delta=0\)
\(\text{the update step satisfies (11.4.22)}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl[\{x^k\}\text{ converges to a point in }\operatorname*{argmin}f\bigr]\lor\bigl[\operatorname*{argmin}f=\varnothing\land\lVert x^k\rVert\to\infty\bigr],\qquad f(x^k)\downarrow\inf f.\)

children.title: Spectral Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle models retaining active eigenspace information.

assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex, and \(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) is affine.
Extreme eigenpairs of \(F(y)\) can be computed.
The retained model is a global minorant and is exact at \(\bar y_k\).
\(t_k>0\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration computes a stabilized trial point, updates the retained spectral subspace, and applies the explicit serious-step test based on \(\delta_k\).

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis of the retained spectral subspace
reduced spectral bundle model, possibly combined with retained affine cuts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle method retaining a compressed active eigenspace rather than only scalar subgradient cuts.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Specialized bundle methods p. 64
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(y)=h(y)+\lambda_{\max}(F(y))\), maintain a center \(\bar y_k\), an orthonormal matrix \(V_k\) spanning retained active eigenvectors, and optional affine minorants. Use the reduced spectral term
\[
h(y)+\lambda_{\max}\!\left(V_k^{\mathsf T}F(y)V_k\right)
\]
together with the retained cuts to form a global minorant \(\widehat f_k\) that is exact at \(\bar y_k\). Compute
\[
y_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\widehat f_k(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|y-\bar y_k\|^2\right\}
\]
and define \(\delta_k=f(\bar y_k)-\widehat f_k(y_{k+1})\). Evaluate extreme eigenvectors of \(F(y_{k+1})\), enlarge or compress the retained subspace, and accept a serious step when \(f(\bar y_k)-f(y_{k+1})\ge\eta\delta_k\) for a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\); otherwise take a null step. Terminate when \(\delta_k\le\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral bundle method solves a stabilized reduced-eigenvalue model, updates a retained active eigenspace from trial-point eigenvectors, and uses an explicit actual-versus-predicted decrease test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General serious/null-step spectral bundle method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle iteration for minimizing the maximum-eigenvalue objective using leading-eigenvector information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given $x_0\in\mathbb R^m$, $\delta>0$, $m_L\in(0,1/2)$, $\mu_0>0$, a prescribed minimal weight $\mu_{\min}$, and $M_0\succ0$, compute $f(x_0)$, a normalized leading eigenvector of $C-\mathcal A^Tx_0$, and an admissible initial model. At iteration $k$, solve
\[y_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\varphi_k(y)+\frac{\mu_k}{2}\|y-x_k\|_k^2\right\}.\]
Evaluate $f(y_{k+1})$ and a normalized, possibly $\epsilon$-approximate, leading eigenvector of $C-\mathcal A^Ty_{k+1}$, and update the admissible model. Stop when
\[f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})\leq\delta\bigl(|f(x_k)|+1\bigr).\]
If
\[f(x_k)-f(y_{k+1})\geq m_L\bigl(f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})\bigr),\]
set $x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}$, choose $\mu_{k+1}\in[\mu_{\min},\mu_k]$, and choose the next metric. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k$ and choose $\mu_{k+1}\in[\mu_k,10\mu_k]$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration minimizes the current spectral bundle model plus a quadratic proximal term, evaluates the maximum-eigenvalue objective and leading-eigenvector information, and updates the model. A candidate producing the required fraction of predicted decrease is accepted as a serious step; otherwise the method takes a null step. The stated relative model-gap test terminates the iteration.
assumptions_latex: x_0\in\mathbb R^m
\delta>0
M_0\succ0
\mu_{\min}\text{ is the prescribed minimal weight}
\varphi_k\text{ and }\mathcal W_k\text{ satisfy the referenced bundle-model admissibility conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The method takes serious or null steps according to the actual-versus-predicted decrease test and stops when }f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})\leq\delta(|f(x_k)|+1).

children.title: Mixed Polyhedral-Semidefinite Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Models combining polyhedral cuts with compact semidefinite spectral models.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) is affine and \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
\(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfies \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\).
For every \(i\in I\), \(\ell_i:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is affine and satisfies \(\ell_i(y)\le f(y)\) for all \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(m(y)\le f(y)\).

notation.meaning: basis of the compact spectral subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid lower-model representation combining ordinary cuts with a compact semidefinite spectral block.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.3 A large class of bundle methods p. 67
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(y)=h(y)+\lambda_{\max}(F(y))\) for \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), where \(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) is affine. Given a finite index set \(I\), global affine minorants \(\ell_i\le f\) for \(i\in I\), and a matrix \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfying \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\), define
\[
m(y)=\max\left\{\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(y),\ h(y)+\lambda_{\max}\!\left(V^{\mathsf T}F(y)V\right)\right\}.
\]
The function \(m\) is a global lower model of \(f\):
\[
m(y)\le f(y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb R^m.
\]
A proximal bundle step may minimize \(m(y)+(2t)^{-1}\|y-\bar y\|^2\) for specified \(t>0\) and center \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed bundle representation is the maximum of global affine cuts and a reduced semidefinite eigenvalue term; it remains a global lower model while retaining selected eigenspace structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral-semidefinite proximal bundle method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies initialization, stabilized trial-point computation, stopping, enlarged-subgradient oracle evaluation, and serious/null-step acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_1\) and \(\delta\ge0\), choose \(\mu_1>0\), \(\bar\varepsilon\ge0\), \(M\succ0\), and \(\omega\in(0,1)\). Set \(k=1\), \(y_1=x_1\), evaluate \(f(y_1)\), and choose \(g_1\in\partial f(y_1)\). At iteration \(k\), solve the prescribed polyhedral-semidefinite coefficient subproblem for \(\bar\alpha\), then set
\[
\bar g_k:=\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i g_i,
\qquad
y_{k+1}:=x_k-\frac1{\mu_k}W_k\bar g_k,
\]
and
\[
\delta_k:=f(x_k)-\check f_k(y_{k+1})+\bar\varepsilon- rac12\mu_k\|y_{k+1}-x_k\|_k^2.
\]
If \(\delta_k\le\delta\), stop. Otherwise compute the prescribed approximate oracle element \(g_{k+1}\in\delta_{\varepsilon}f(y_{k+1})\) and its error data. If
\[
f(y_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\omega\delta_k,
\]
set \(x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}\) and choose \(\mu_{k+1}>0\), \(M_{k+1}\succ0\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method solves a mixed polyhedral-semidefinite proximal bundle subproblem, forms a metric trial step from the aggregate subgradient, and stops when its decrease measure is below tolerance. Otherwise it calls an enlarged-subgradient oracle and accepts a serious step only when the prescribed fraction of predicted decrease is achieved; failing that, it takes a null step.
assumptions_latex: x_1\in\mathbb R^m
\delta\ge0
\bar\varepsilon\ge0
M\succ0
\omega\in(0,1)
g_1\in\partial f(y_1)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_k\le\delta\Rightarrow\mathrm{stop};\qquad f(y_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\omega\delta_k\Rightarrow x_{k+1}=y_{k+1};\qquad\mathrm{otherwise}\ x_{k+1}=x_k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global polyhedral component of the mixed spectral bundle method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the cutting-plane model, simplex aggregation subproblem, step tests, and approximate-optimality boundary of the mixed polyhedral-semidefinite method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For rich-oracle outputs \(W_i\) at \(y_i\), define
\[
\mathcal W_k=\operatorname{conv}\{W_1,\ldots,W_k\},\qquad e_i=\langle W_i,C\rangle,\qquad g_i=b-\mathcal AW_i,
\]
and
\[
\varphi_k(y)=\max_{1\le i\le k}\{e_i+g_i^Ty\}.
\]
With \(\Delta_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^k:\sum_i\alpha_i=1\}\), choose \(\bar\alpha\) to minimize
\[
\frac{1}{2\mu_k}\left\|\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i g_i\right\|_{k,*}^2-
\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i e_i-x_k^T\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i g_i
\]
over \(\Delta_k\), and set
\[
(\bar e_k,\bar g_k)=\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i(e_i,g_i).
\]
The aggregate \(\bar g_k\) is interpretable as an \(\epsilon_k\)-subgradient. The modified rules stop when \(\delta_k\leq\delta\) and accept a serious step when
\[
f(x_k)-f(y_{k+1})\geq m_L\delta_k.
\]
On a serious step, set \(x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}\) and choose \(\mu_{k+1}\in[\mu_{\min},\mu_k]\). With the approximate rich oracle, the stated analysis gives finite convergence with approximate optimality conditions; the exact-subgradient argument based on letting \(\delta\to0\) is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global component forms a maximum of affine cuts from the rich oracle's epsilon-subgradients. A quadratic program over the simplex produces an aggregate cut that remains interpretable as an epsilon-subgradient. The method stops when model decrease is below a positive tolerance and accepts a serious step when actual decrease reaches the prescribed fraction of model decrease. Its stated guarantee is finite convergence with approximate optimality, not the exact-subgradient limit obtained by sending the stopping tolerance to zero.
assumptions_latex: \epsilon>0
W_i\in\delta_\epsilon\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^Ty_i)
e_i=\langle W_i,C\rangle
g_i=b-\mathcal AW_i
\mu_k>0
\Delta_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^k:\sum_i\alpha_i=1\}
\delta>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi_k(y)=\max_{1\le i\le k}(e_i+g_i^Ty),\qquad (\bar e_k,\bar g_k)=\sum_i\bar\alpha_i(e_i,g_i),\qquad \delta_k\leq\delta\Longrightarrow\text{stop},\qquad f(x_k)-f(y_{k+1})\geq m_L\delta_k\Longrightarrow\text{serious step}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Near-active spectral enlargement and rich oracle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the local semidefinite information used by the mixed polyhedral-semidefinite bundle method for a maximum-eigenvalue objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), \(Z_k=C-\mathcal A^Ty_k\), and let \(P_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\) have orthonormal columns spanning the eigenspaces associated with eigenvalues of \(Z_k\) in \((\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)-\epsilon,\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)]\). Define
\[
\delta_\epsilon\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)=\{P_kVP_k^T:V\in\mathcal S_+^{r_k},\ \operatorname{Tr}V=1\}
\]
and, for \(f(y)=b^Ty+\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^Ty)\),
\[
\delta_\epsilon f(y_k)=\{b-\mathcal AW:W\in\delta_\epsilon\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)\}.
\]
Then
\[
\partial f(y_k)\subseteq\delta_\epsilon f(y_k)\subseteq\partial_\epsilon f(y_k).
\]
The rich oracle selects \(W_k\in\delta_\epsilon\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)\) such that \(g_k=b-\mathcal AW_k\) is the unique solution of
\[
\min\{\|g\|_{k,*}^2:g\in\delta_\epsilon f(y_k)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive tolerance, the enlargement retains eigendirections whose eigenvalues are strictly greater than the largest eigenvalue minus epsilon. Trace-one positive-semidefinite matrices supported on this near-active eigenspace define an enlarged spectral subdifferential. Its affine image contains the exact subdifferential and lies within the epsilon-subdifferential. The rich oracle returns its minimum-dual-metric-norm member.
assumptions_latex: \epsilon>0
Z_k=C-\mathcal A^Ty_k\in\mathcal S^n
P_k^TP_k=I_{r_k}
\operatorname{range}(P_k)\text{ spans the eigenspaces for eigenvalues in }(\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)-\epsilon,\lambda_{\max}(Z_k)]
f(y)=b^Ty+\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^Ty)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f(y_k)\subseteq\delta_\epsilon f(y_k)\subseteq\partial_\epsilon f(y_k),\qquad g_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{g\in\delta_\epsilon f(y_k)}\|g\|_{k,*}^2=b-\mathcal AW_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual mixed polyhedral-semidefinite bundle subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the proximal dual and optimal-solution relations for a bundle subproblem combining affine cuts with a compact semidefinite spectral model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Up to the multiplicative factor \(\mu_k>0\), the dual of the associated coefficient-form subproblem is
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\operatorname{minimize}_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,t\in\mathbb R}&t+\frac12\mu_k\|y-x_k\|_k^2\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}&f(x_k)-\widetilde e_i+g_i^T(y-x_k)\le t,\quad i=1,\ldots,k-1,\\
&(f(y_k)-\bar\varepsilon)I_{r_k}+Q_k^T\mathcal F(y-y_k)Q_k\preccurlyeq tI_{r_k}.
\end{array}
\]
If \((t_{k+1},y_{k+1})\) and \((\bar\alpha,\bar Z)\) solve the displayed dual and its associated primal subproblem, respectively, and
\[
g_k:=\mathcal F^*(Q_k\bar ZQ_k^T),
\]
then
\[
y_{k+1}=x_k-\frac1{\mu_k}W_k\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i g_i,
\qquad
t_{k+1}=\widetilde\varphi_k(y_{k+1}),
\]
where \(\widetilde\varphi_k(y)=\max_{1\le i\le k}\widetilde l_i(y)\),
\[
\widetilde l_i(y)=f(y_i)+g_i^T(y-y_i)-\bar\varepsilon
=f(x_k)+g_i^T(y-x_k)-\widetilde e_i\quad(i<k),
\]
and
\[
\widetilde l_k(y)=f(y_k)-\bar\varepsilon+\bar Z\bullet\left(Q_k^T\mathcal F(y-y_k)Q_k\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coefficient-form mixed bundle subproblem has a proximal dual containing the previous affine cuts and one compact semidefinite spectral constraint. Optimal primal and dual solutions determine the trial point through the aggregate subgradient, while the epigraph value equals the maximum of the resulting cutting models.
assumptions_latex: \mu_k>0
(t_{k+1},y_{k+1})\text{ solves the displayed dual problem}
(\bar\alpha,\bar Z)\text{ solves the associated primal subproblem}
g_k=\mathcal F^*(Q_k\bar ZQ_k^T)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_{k+1}=x_k-\frac1{\mu_k}W_k\sum_{i=1}^k\bar\alpha_i g_i,\qquad t_{k+1}=\widetilde\varphi_k(y_{k+1})

children.title: Second-Order Proximal Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle architectures enriched with local second-order spectral information.

assumptions_latex: The objective is finite and convex and admits a first-order spectral oracle.
\(m_k:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is a finite convex bundle minorant.
\(H_k\succeq0\), \(t_k>0\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
Second-order information is restricted to a locally stable active spectral subspace or replaced by a positive-semidefinite approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized subproblem is strongly convex and has a unique trial point \(y_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle step enriched by a positive-semidefinite local curvature model.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a center \(\bar y_k\in\mathbb R^m\), retain a finite convex bundle minorant \(m_k\), choose \(H_k\succeq0\) and \(t_k>0\), and compute
\[
y_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{m_k(y)+\frac12(y-\bar y_k)^{\mathsf T}H_k(y-\bar y_k)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|y-\bar y_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
The curvature matrix \(H_k\) is obtained from local second-order spectral information on a stable active eigenspace or from a positive-semidefinite approximation. Evaluate the objective and a new spectral oracle element at \(y_{k+1}\), apply a serious/null-step test with a prescribed acceptance fraction \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and update the bundle and \(H_k\). A specified predicted-decrease measure may be compared with a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) for termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order proximal bundle method adds a positive-semidefinite local curvature term to the stabilized bundle subproblem, evaluates a spectral oracle at the unique trial point, and then performs a serious or null step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order proximal bundle algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serious-step/null-step procedure using second-order spectral geometry, bundle aggregation, and a rich oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\delta>0\), \(\epsilon>0\), \(m_L\in(0,\tfrac12)\), and positive initial and minimum proximal-weight parameters, initialize \(k=0\), evaluate \(f(x_0)\), form \([M_0^*]_{\mathcal V_0}\), and solve the prescribed bundle subproblem for \(g_0\). At iteration \(k\), if \(y_k=x_k\), compute the decomposed direction \(d_k=v_k+u_k\), set
\[
y_{k+1}=x_k+\mu_k^{-1}d_k,
\qquad
\delta_k=g_k^T(y_{k+1}-x_k)+\tfrac12\mu_k\|y_{k+1}-x_k\|_k^2.
\]
If \(y_k\ne x_k\), solve the prescribed aggregation problem for \(\alpha\), set
\[
g_k=\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i g_i,
\qquad y_{k+1}=x_k-\mu_k^{-1}M_k^*g_k,
\qquad
\delta_k=\epsilon_k+\frac{1}{2\mu_k}\|\bar g_k\|_{k,*}^2.
\]
Stop when \(\delta_k\leq\delta\). Otherwise call the rich oracle at \(y_{k+1}\) and obtain \(g_{k+1}\in\delta_\epsilon f(y_{k+1})\). If
\[
f(y_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)-m_L\delta_k,
\]
set \(x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}\), choose \(\mu_{k+1}\in[\mu_{\min},\mu_k]\), and update \([M_{k+1}^*]_{\mathcal V_{k+1}}\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The branch selected by whether the current trial point equals the stability center constructs either a decomposed second-order trial step or an aggregated bundle step. The method stops when its decrease measure meets the tolerance, accepts a trial point only when the serious-step test holds, and otherwise records a null step.
assumptions_latex: x_0\in\mathbb R^m
\delta>0
\epsilon>0
m_L\in(0,\tfrac12)
\text{the initial proximal weight is positive}
\text{a prescribed minimum proximal weight is available}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_k\leq\delta\Rightarrow\text{terminate};\quad f(y_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)-m_L\delta_k\Rightarrow x_{k+1}=y_{k+1};\quad\text{otherwise }x_{k+1}=x_k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric and convex-analytic decomposition of the bundle subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the tangent and normal subspaces used in a second-order spectral bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the projection of \(F(x_k)\) onto \(\mathcal M_{r_k}\) is
\[
\widehat F_k=F(x_k)+P_kL_kP_k^T,
\]
then
\[
\mathcal U_k=(\mathcal A^T)^{-1}T_{\mathcal M_{r_k}}(\widehat F_k),\qquad
\mathcal V_k=\mathcal A N_{\mathcal M_{r_k}}(\widehat F_k).
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal U_k\) is the largest subspace on which the support function of \(\delta_\epsilon f(x_k)\) is linear, while \(\mathcal V_k\) is parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(\delta_\epsilon f(x_k))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bundle subspaces are respectively the inverse image of the tangent space and the image of the normal space at the projected spectral matrix. The first is also the largest subspace on which the indicated support function is linear, and the second is parallel to the affine hull of the indicated set.
assumptions_latex: \widehat F_k=F(x_k)+P_kL_kP_k^T\text{ is the projection of }F(x_k)\text{ onto }\mathcal M_{r_k}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal U_k=(\mathcal A^T)^{-1}T_{\mathcal M_{r_k}}(\widehat F_k),\quad \mathcal V_k=\mathcal A N_{\mathcal M_{r_k}}(\widehat F_k),\quad \mathcal U_k\text{ and }\mathcal V_k\text{ have the stated convex-analytic characterizations}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order expansion on a fixed eigenvalue-multiplicity manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic spectral model used by second-order proximal bundle methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in F^{-1}(\mathcal M_r)\) be regular and let \(g\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(x)\). For every \(d\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(F(x+d)\in\mathcal M_r\),
\[
f(x+d)=f(x)+g^Td+\tfrac12d^TH(x,g)d+o(\|d\|^2),
\]
where \(H(x,g)\in\mathcal S^m\) has entries
\[
H(x,g)_{ij}=2\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(A_iWA_j\bigl(f(x)I_n-F(x)\bigr)^\dagger\right),\qquad i,j=1,\ldots,m,
\]
and \(W\in\partial\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^Tx)\) satisfies \(g=b-\mathcal AW\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular point on the fixed-multiplicity manifold, every relative-interior subgradient yields a second-order expansion along displacements remaining on that manifold. The quadratic term is represented using a maximum-eigenvalue subgradient and the pseudoinverse of the spectral residual.
assumptions_latex: x\in F^{-1}(\mathcal M_r)\text{ is regular}
g\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(x)
d\in\mathbb R^m\text{ and }F(x+d)\in\mathcal M_r
W\in\partial\lambda_{\max}(C-\mathcal A^Tx),\quad g=b-\mathcal AW
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x+d)=f(x)+g^Td+\frac12d^TH(x,g)d+o(\|d\|^2)

children.title: Rich Spectral Oracles
children.top_down_role: Oracle interfaces returning active eigenspaces and recovery information.

knowledge_statements.title: Rich Spectral Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle returning an active eigenspace and matrix-valued subgradient information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(y)=h(y)+\lambda_{\max}(F(y))\), a rich spectral oracle at \(y\) returns \(f(y)\), an orthonormal basis \(U\) for the maximum-eigenvalue eigenspace of \(F(y)\), and the affine action needed to evaluate
\[
g_j(W)=\partial_j h(y)+\left\langle W,U^{\mathsf T}(\partial_jF)U\right\rangle,
\qquad W\succeq0,
\qquad \operatorname{tr}(W)=1.
\]
Thus every admissible \(W\) supplies a subgradient \(g(W)\in\partial f(y)\), while the entire returned eigenspace represents the exposed subdifferential face. A recovery-capable oracle may additionally return the linear feasibility residuals associated with \(UWU^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rich oracle returns the full active eigenspace and enough matrix data to generate every subgradient on its exposed face and test recovery candidates.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable at \(y\).
\(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(W)\in\partial f(y)\) for every \(W\succeq0\) satisfying \(\operatorname{tr}(W)=1\).

notation.meaning: basis of the active maximum-eigenvalue eigenspace
density matrix selecting an active-face subgradient

children.title: Multiple-Eigenvalue Nonsmoothness
children.top_down_role: Model instability near changing or repeated extreme eigenspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Eigenvalue Nonsmoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential structure of the maximum eigenvalue at a repeated active eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), and let the largest eigenvalue of \(A\) have multiplicity \(r\), with orthonormal active-eigenspace basis \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Then
\[
\partial\lambda_{\max}(A)=\left\{UWU^{\mathsf T}:W\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(W)=1\right\}.
\]
Consequently, \(\lambda_{\max}\) is differentiable at \(A\) exactly when \(r=1\). For \(r>1\), selecting only one active eigenvector selects only an extreme point of the subdifferential; arbitrarily small perturbations may change that eigenvector while the full active subspace remains the correct first-order object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a repeated largest eigenvalue, the subdifferential is the density-matrix hull of active eigenspace projectors, so a single eigenvector is unstable and incomplete.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(U\) has orthonormal columns spanning the largest-eigenvalue eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\lambda_{\max}(A)=\{UWU^{\mathsf T}:W\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(W)=1\}\), and differentiability holds exactly when \(r=1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a bundle method initially stores \(q_0\in\mathbb N\) affine cuts and adds exactly one cut after each oracle call, deleting and aggregating none. For every \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), after \(k\) calls the model contains
\[
q_k=q_0+k
\]
cuts. If each cut stores \(O(m)\) scalar data, including a subgradient in \(\mathbb R^m\), then bundle storage is \(O(mq_k)\). An epigraph formulation of the proximal cutting-plane subproblem has \(m\) optimization variables, in addition to its epigraph variable, and \(q_k\) cut inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one new cut per oracle call and no deletion or aggregation, the cut count and epigraph inequality count equal the initial count plus the number of calls, while storage is linear in the variable dimension times the cut count.

children.title: Bundle Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Compression of accumulated spectral information within bundle models.

assumptions_latex: For every \(i\in I_k\), the affine cut \(\ell_i\) satisfies \(\ell_i(y)\le f(y)\) for all \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
The coefficients \(\alpha_i\) are optimal epigraph multipliers for the stabilized model subproblem, satisfy \(\alpha_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i=1\), and vanish on inactive cut constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate satisfies \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(y)\le f(y)\) for all \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(y_{k+1})=m_k(y_{k+1})\).

notation.meaning: normalized epigraph multiplier for cut i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex aggregation of active cuts after solving a proximal bundle subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 A short description of standard bundle methods p. 61
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I_k\) be finite, let
\[
m_k(y)=\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(y),
\]
and let \(y_{k+1}\in\mathbb R^m\) solve the stabilized epigraph subproblem for this model. Let \(\alpha_i\ge0\) be its cut-constraint multipliers, normalized by \(\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i=1\), with \(\alpha_i=0\) for inactive cuts. Define
\[
\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(y)=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i\ell_i(y).
\]
The aggregate is a global affine minorant satisfying
\[
\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(y_{k+1})=m_k(y_{k+1}),
\]
and its slope is the multiplier-weighted slope appearing in the subproblem optimality condition. An aggregation update may retain this cut together with the newest oracle cut and any protected spectral information while deleting selected individual old cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized optimal multipliers combine the active affine cuts into one global minorant that preserves the solved model value and multiplier-weighted slope at the trial point.
knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Aggregation

children.title: Memory-Limited Bundle Regimes
children.top_down_role: Bundle management under restricted model-storage budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Limited Bundle Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-memory invariant preserving convergence-relevant model information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bundle iteration is memory-limited with budget \(M\ge2\) if its post-update index set satisfies \(|I_{k+1}|\le M\) and contains both the newest oracle cut and an aggregate cut formed from the multipliers of the preceding proximal subproblem. Formally,
\[
I_{k+1}=\{\mathrm{new},\mathrm{agg}\}\cup J_k,
\qquad |J_k|\le M-2.
\]
All retained cuts must remain global minorants, and protected columns representing an active spectral subspace must obey a separately specified rank budget. The newest cut supplies current oracle information, while the aggregate preserves the preceding subproblem's model value and stationarity combination despite deletion of individual old cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-memory bundle keeps at most M cuts while always retaining the newest cut and an aggregate of the preceding subproblem's active cuts.
assumptions_latex: The objective is convex and every stored cut is a global minorant.
The aggregate uses normalized optimal multipliers from the preceding proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|I_{k+1}|\le M\) while newest-cut information and the preceding stationarity aggregate are retained.

notation.meaning: maximum number of stored affine cuts

children.title: Bundle Local-Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local and superlinear behavior under stable active spectral structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Local-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional fast local behavior under stable active spectral structure and accurate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^*\) minimize a convex spectral objective, and suppose the active extreme-eigenvalue multiplicity is locally constant, its invariant subspace is separated from the remaining spectrum by a positive gap, and the reduced smooth problem satisfies a nonsingular second-order growth condition. Once a spectral bundle contains that active subspace, its local model identifies the correct exposed face. A proximal bundle scheme with consistent second-order models and eventually accepted full serious steps then reduces locally to a smooth Newton-type iteration on that face. Under these conditions the iterates converge superlinearly; with exact reduced Hessians and Lipschitz continuous reduced Hessian, the local rate is quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable active eigenspaces, a spectral gap, second-order growth, and accurate curvature can make a spectral bundle method locally Newton-like and superlinear or quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The active eigenvalue multiplicity is locally constant and spectrally separated near \(y^*\).
The reduced active-face problem has nonsingular second-order growth.
The bundle identifies the active subspace and its curvature models are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local serious-step sequence is superlinear; with exact Lipschitz reduced Hessians it is quadratic.

children.title: Full-Spectral PSD Projection
children.top_down_role: Exact projection using complete spectral decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Spectral PSD Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Frobenius projection onto the positive-semidefinite cone by complete eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), compute a complete orthogonal eigendecomposition \(A=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(\lambda_i^+=\max\{\lambda_i,0\}\) and return
\[
\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(A)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1^+,\ldots,\lambda_n^+)Q^{\mathsf T}.
\]
This matrix is the unique minimizer of \(\min_{X\succeq0}\|X-A\|_F\). For a dense symmetric matrix, a full eigendecomposition uses \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(n^2)\) storage. A stopping check may verify nonnegative returned eigenvalues and the orthogonal decomposition of positive and negative parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute every eigenpair, replace negative eigenvalues by zero, and reconstruct; this is the unique Frobenius-nearest positive-semidefinite matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S^n\).
Distance is measured with the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(A)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\max\{\lambda_i,0\})Q^{\mathsf T}\), uniquely.

notation.meaning: cone of real positive-semidefinite n-by-n matrices
Frobenius metric projection onto the PSD cone

knowledge_statements.title: Partial PSD Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated positive-eigenvalue projection for real symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric matrix \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and an integer \(1\le r\le n\), compute the \(r\) largest algebraic eigenpairs \((\lambda_i,u_i)\), ordered by \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_r\). Return \[P_{+,r}(X)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\max\{\lambda_i,0\}u_i u_i^{\mathsf T}.\] If fewer than \(r\) eigenvalues are positive, zero terms are retained implicitly. The output satisfies \(P_{+,r}(X)\succeq0\), has rank at most \(r\), and equals the full Frobenius projection \(P_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\) whenever every omitted eigenvalue is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain at most the largest r positive eigencomponents. The result is PSD and equals the exact PSD projection if no omitted eigenvalue is positive.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
\(1\le r\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{+,r}(X)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}P_{+,r}(X)\le r\).

notation.meaning: cone of real n-by-n positive semidefinite matrices

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly from the spectral formula for Frobenius projection onto the PSD cone

children.title: Approximate PSD Projection
children.top_down_role: Inexact PSD projection under controlled spectral accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate PSD Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based accuracy condition for an inexact PSD projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-approximate Frobenius projection of \(X\) onto \(\mathbb S_+^n\) when \[\|Z-P_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\|_F\le\varepsilon.\] A relative convention may instead require \(\|Z-P_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\|_F\le\varepsilon\|X\|_F\). Under the absolute convention, the projection objective obeys \[\|Z-X\|_F\le \operatorname{dist}_F(X,\mathbb S_+^n)+\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate PSD projection is PSD and lies within a prescribed absolute or relative Frobenius error of the exact cone projection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(\|Z-P_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\|_F\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Frobenius projection onto the PSD cone

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Eigenspace Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD approximation obtained by projecting within a prescribed orthonormal subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfy \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_r\). For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), the Frobenius-nearest matrix to \(X\) among PSD matrices whose range lies in \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\) is \[P_Q^+(X)=Q\bigl(Q^{\mathsf T}XQ\bigr)_+Q^{\mathsf T},\] where \((H)_+\) replaces the negative eigenvalues of \(H\in\mathbb S^r\) by zero. Equivalently, \(P_Q^+(X)\) uniquely solves \[\min_{Y\succeq0}\|X-QYQ^{\mathsf T}\|_F^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compress the matrix to a selected orthonormal eigenspace, project the compressed matrix onto the PSD cone, and lift it back.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_Q^+(X)=Q(Q^{\mathsf T}XQ)_+Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

PSD projection restricted to the range of Q

children.title: Alternating-Projection Methods for SDP
children.top_down_role: Projection cycles between affine structure and semidefinite cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternating-Projection Methods for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility iteration alternating between an affine matrix set and the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty closed affine set \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^n\), initialize \(X^0\in\mathbb S^n\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[Y^k=P_{\mathcal A}(X^k),\qquad X^{k+1}=P_{\mathbb S_+^n}(Y^k).\] Stop when both \(\operatorname{dist}_F(X^{k+1},\mathcal A)\le\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}_F(X^{k+1},\mathbb S_+^n)\le\varepsilon\), and output \(X^{k+1}\). If \(\mathcal A\cap\mathbb S_+^n\neq\varnothing\), the finite-dimensional alternating-projection theorem implies convergence to a point in the intersection, though generally not to the nearest intersection point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate Euclidean projections onto the SDP affine constraints and PSD cone until both feasibility residuals meet tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) is closed and affine.
\(\mathcal A\cap\mathbb S_+^n\neq\varnothing\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^k\to X^\star\in\mathcal A\cap\mathbb S_+^n\).

affine constraint set of the SDP feasibility problem

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block SDP Splittings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical two-block ADMM separating an SDP cone block from affine structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{X,Z}\ f(X)+g(Z)\) subject to \(AX+BZ=c\), where \(f\) may include the indicator of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(g\) may encode affine constraints. Given \(\rho>0\), initialize \((Z^0,U^0)\). For \(k\ge0\), set \[X^{k+1}\in\arg\min_X f(X)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|AX+BZ^k-c+U^k\|_F^2,\] \[Z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_Z g(Z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|AX^{k+1}+BZ-c+U^k\|_F^2,\] and \(U^{k+1}=U^k+AX^{k+1}+BZ^{k+1}-c\). Stop using primal and dual residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-block ADMM alternately minimizes over a cone block and a structural block, then updates the scaled multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each displayed subproblem has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^{k+1}=AX^{k+1}+BZ^{k+1}-c\) is the primal residual used in the multiplier update.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-consensus ADMM for separable SDP objectives with local matrix copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_Z\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(Z)\), introduce local matrices \(X_i\) and constraints \(X_i=Z\). Given \(\rho>0\), initialize \(Z^0\) and scaled multipliers \(U_i^0\). For \(k\ge0\), update in parallel \[X_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{X_i} f_i(X_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|X_i-Z^k+U_i^k\|_F^2,\] then set \[Z^{k+1}=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m(X_i^{k+1}+U_i^k),\qquad U_i^{k+1}=U_i^k+X_i^{k+1}-Z^{k+1}.\] Indicators inside \(f_i\) may impose local PSD or affine constraints. Stop when consensus and dual residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local SDP blocks update in parallel, a global variable averages their shifted values, and multipliers enforce agreement.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
A minimizer exists for every local update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_i^{k+1}-Z^{k+1}\) is the local consensus residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable ADMM with local SDP blocks coupled by one linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{X_1,\ldots,X_m} \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(X_i)+g(Z)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_iX_i+BZ=c\), with the collection \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)\) treated as one ADMM block. Given \(\rho>0\), minimize the augmented Lagrangian over all \(X_i\) with \(Z=Z^k\), exploiting separability when the quadratic coupling permits; next minimize over \(Z\); finally update \[U^{k+1}=U^k+\sum_{i=1}^m A_iX_i^{k+1}+BZ^{k+1}-c.\] Local functions may include PSD-cone indicators. Stop when primal and dual residuals satisfy prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group separable local SDP variables into one ADMM block, update them and the coupling block, then update the shared multiplier.
assumptions_latex: All \(f_i\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency-Coupling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear consistency conditions coupling local SDP copies or decomposed blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let local matrices \(X_i\in\mathbb S^{n_i}\) be coupled through linear maps \(E_i:\mathbb S^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^p\). A linear consistency regime has the affine form \[\sum_{i=1}^m E_iX_i=d.\] After including a global variable \(Z\) as an additional block, global consensus is represented by the constraints \(X_i-Z=0\) for every \(i\). Pairwise overlap consistency is represented by \[R_{ij}X_iR_{ij}^{\mathsf T}=R_{ji}X_jR_{ji}^{\mathsf T}\] on every edge \((i,j)\) of a coupling graph. Convergence results for a chosen ADMM splitting require formulation-specific assumptions, commonly including existence of a feasible primal-dual solution and attainment of the block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local SDP blocks may be coupled by global sums, equality to a common variable, or agreement of overlapping principal submatrices; convergence assumptions depend on the selected splitting.
assumptions_latex: Each \(E_i\) is linear.
Local variables belong to specified closed convex domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Corrected Multi-Block SDP Splittings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prediction-correction template for convergent multi-block SDP splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(X_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_iX_i=b\), with \(m\ge3\), form a Gauss–Seidel ADMM predictor \(\widetilde X^{k+1}\) by sequential augmented-Lagrangian minimization and a predicted multiplier \(\widetilde y^{k+1}\). Let \(w=(X_1,\ldots,X_m,y)\). Apply a correction \[w^{k+1}=w^k+M_k(\widetilde w^{k+1}-w^k),\] where the correction or proximal metric \(M_k\) is chosen so that the induced fixed-point map is averaged in a positive-definite metric. Stop when feasibility and block-stationarity residuals meet tolerance. PSD constraints are represented by indicators within selected \(f_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-block ADMM predictor is followed by a metric, proximal, or relaxation correction chosen to restore an averaged iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge3\) and every \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
The correction metric makes the full iteration averaged.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP Splitting Convergence Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for convergence of exact two-block convex SDP ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the two-block problem \(\min f(X)+g(Z)\) subject to \(AX+BZ=c\), a standard sufficient regime is: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions; a primal-dual saddle point exists; \(\rho>0\) is fixed; and both block subproblems are solved exactly. In finite dimensions, under the usual two-block ADMM operator assumptions—equivalently, maximal monotonicity of the associated subdifferentials together with existence of a zero—the iterates have vanishing feasibility and successive-update residuals. Convergence of the complete primal sequence additionally requires uniqueness, coercivity, or an appropriate rank or strong-convexity condition preventing nonunique block motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact two-block SDP ADMM needs closed convex blocks, a saddle point, positive penalty, and attained subproblems; stronger regularity may be needed for full iterate convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A primal-dual saddle point exists.
\(\rho>0\) and both block updates are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AX^k+BZ^k-c\to0\), with full iterate convergence subject to an additional regularity condition.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM Residual Convergence for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual convergence for exact finite-dimensional two-block SDP ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider exact two-block ADMM applied to \(\min f(X)+g(Z)\) subject to \(AX+BZ=c\), with fixed \(\rho>0\). Suppose \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, the block subproblems attain their minima, and a primal-dual saddle point exists. Define \(r^{k}=AX^{k}+BZ^{k}-c\) and, for the standard update order, \(s^{k}=\rho A^{*}B(Z^{k}-Z^{k-1})\). Then \[r^{k}\to0,\qquad s^{k}\to0,\qquad f(X^k)+g(Z^k)\to p^\star,\] and every convergent primal-dual subsequence has a primal-dual optimal limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard exact two-block assumptions, ADMM primal and dual residuals vanish, objective values converge, and cluster points are optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM Local Linear-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-linear contraction under an error bound for the ADMM fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the fixed-point operator representing a finite-dimensional SDP ADMM iteration \(w^{k+1}=T(w^k)\), and let \(\Omega=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). Suppose \(T\) is averaged in a norm \(\|\cdot\|_H\) and, on a neighborhood \(N\) of \(\Omega\), the error bound \[\operatorname{dist}_H(w,\Omega)\le\kappa\|w-Tw\|_H\] holds for some \(\kappa>0\). Then there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and a possibly smaller neighborhood such that every orbit remaining there satisfies \[\operatorname{dist}_H(w^{k+1},\Omega)\le q\operatorname{dist}_H(w^k,\Omega).\] Consequently, the fixed-point residual converges R-linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An averaged ADMM map converges locally linearly when distance to its solution set is bounded by its fixed-point residual.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is averaged in the \(H\)-norm.
\(\Omega=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
A local metric error bound holds near \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_H(w^{k+1},\Omega)\le q\operatorname{dist}_H(w^k,\Omega)\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\).

notation.meaning: positive-definite metric defining the local norm

authoritative fixed-point or ADMM theorem locator required

children.title: Direct Multi-Block ADMM Divergence

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Multi-Block ADMM Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-block scalar feasibility counterexample to the direct Gauss–Seidel extension of two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1=(1,1,1)^\top\), \(A_2=(1,1,2)^\top\), and \(A_3=(1,2,2)^\top\). Consider \(\min 0\) subject to \(A_1x_1+A_2x_2+A_3x_3=0\), with \(x_i\in\mathbb R\). Direct three-block ADMM sequentially minimizes the augmented Lagrangian over \(x_1,x_2,x_3\) and then sets \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\beta\sum_{i=1}^3A_ix_i^{k+1}\), where \(\beta>0\). Its linear iteration has an eigenvalue of modulus approximately \(1.0278>1\). Consequently, an initialization having a component in the associated invariant subspace produces an unbounded or nonconvergent sequence although the feasible problem has the solution \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concrete feasible three-block problem has a direct ADMM iteration with spectral radius above one, so suitable initializations diverge.
assumptions_latex: Each block is minimized exactly in Gauss–Seidel order.
The initialization has a nonzero component in an unstable invariant subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direct three-block ADMM iterates need not converge.

notation.meaning: Constraint column for scalar block i.

review_flags: Exact counterexample matrix and spectral-radius value require an authoritative ADMM divergence locator.

children.title: Penalty Imbalance

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational imbalance condition for residual-balanced ADMM penalty adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ADMM residuals \(r^k=Ax^k+Bz^k-c\) and \(s^k=\rho_kA^\top B(z^k-z^{k-1})\), fix \(\mu>1\), a scale floor \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}>0\), and an integer persistence window \(L\ge1\). Define \(\chi_k=\|r^k\|_2/\max\{\|s^k\|_2,\epsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}\}\). Penalty imbalance at iteration \(k\) means either \(\chi_j>\mu\) for every \(j=k-L+1,\ldots,k\), indicating persistently excessive primal residual, or \(\chi_j<\mu^{-1}\) throughout that window, indicating persistently excessive dual residual. The predicate is diagnostic and depends on the chosen residual scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty imbalance occurs when one ADMM residual persistently exceeds the other by a prescribed factor.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>1\), \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}>0\), and \(L\ge1\).
The displayed primal and dual residual conventions are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated persistent-ratio predicate identifies penalty imbalance.
review_flags: Threshold and persistence conventions require a residual-balancing source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the threshold, scale floor, persistence window, and residual convention define a particular diagnostic that needs source support.

children.title: Residual Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent lack of progress in primal or dual residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window diagnostic for stalled ADMM feasibility and stationarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k=\max\{\|r^k\|_2/\varepsilon_p,\|s^k\|_2/\varepsilon_d\}\), where \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d>0\) are stopping tolerances. Given \(m\ge1\) and \(\eta\in[0,1)\), residual stagnation at iteration \(k\ge m\) is the condition \(R_k>1\) and \((R_{k-m}-R_k)/\max\{R_{k-m},1\}\le\eta\). Thus the method remains outside its stopping region while its normalized worst residual decreases by at most the prescribed relative amount over the observation window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual stagnation means tolerances remain unmet while the normalized worst residual barely decreases over a fixed window.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d>0\), \(m\ge1\), and \(\eta\in[0,1)\).
Residuals are measured consistently throughout the window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality is the residual-stagnation diagnostic.
review_flags: Operational stagnation threshold and window convention need source support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-window condition fits Residual Stagnation, but its normalization, progress inequality, window, and threshold are bespoke conventions without supporting evidence.

children.title: Residual-Scale Mismatch

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Scale Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw residual balancing to remain invariant under constraint rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax+Bz=c\), use \(r^k=Ax^k+Bz^k-c\) and \(s^k=\rho A^\top B(z^k-z^{k-1})\). Replace the constraint data by \((\gamma A,\gamma B,\gamma c)\), where \(\gamma>0\), while holding \(\rho\) fixed. The corresponding residuals satisfy \(\widetilde r^k=\gamma r^k\) and \(\widetilde s^k=\gamma^2s^k\). Hence \(\|\widetilde r^k\|_2/\|\widetilde s^k\|_2=\gamma^{-1}\|r^k\|_2/\|s^k\|_2\) whenever \(s^k\ne0\). A raw residual-ratio penalty rule can therefore make different decisions on equivalent constraint scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent constraint scaling changes the raw primal-to-dual residual ratio, so residual balancing may select different penalties.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma>0\) and \(\rho\) is unchanged.
\(s^k\ne0\) when the residual ratio is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Raw residual balancing is not invariant under uniform constraint rescaling.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the transformation follows directly from the displayed residual definitions.
