children.title: PSD Projection Bottleneck
children.top_down_role: Dominance of repeated eigendecompositions in large semidefinite blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: PSD Projection Bottleneck
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic cost of exact projection onto a large positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Z\in\mathbb S^n\) with eigendecomposition \(Z=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)Q^\top\), the Euclidean projection is \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(Z)=Q\operatorname{diag}(\max\{\lambda_i,0\})Q^\top\). A dense exact eigendecomposition requires \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(n^2)\) storage. Consequently, an iterative SDP method performing this projection once per iteration incurs \(O(Nn^3)\) projection work over \(N\) iterations. If its remaining per-iteration operations cost \(o(n^3)\), repeated PSD projection is the leading dense-arithmetic bottleneck.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact dense PSD projection costs cubic time and quadratic storage, dominating iterations whose other operations are cheaper.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb S^n\) is represented densely.
Projection is computed by a full symmetric eigendecomposition.
Other per-iteration operations cost \(o(n^3)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cumulative projection cost over \(N\) iterations is \(O(Nn^3)\), with \(O(n^2)\) storage.

children.title: Basic PDHG for SDP

knowledge_statements.title: Basic PDHG for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned PDHG for a composite SDP with an explicit PSD proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{X\in\mathbb S^n} f(X)+g(\mathcal KX)\), where \(f(X)=\langle C,X\rangle+\delta_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\). Choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) with \(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\), initialize \(X^0,y^0\), and set \(\bar X^0=X^0\). For \(k\ge0\), compute \(y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma\mathcal K\bar X^k)\), \(X^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X^k-\tau(C+\mathcal K^*y^{k+1}))\), and \(\bar X^{k+1}=2X^{k+1}-X^k\). Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold, and output \(X^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basic PDHG alternates a dual proximal step, an explicit PSD projection, and primal extrapolation under a norm-based stepsize condition.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A saddle point exists.
\(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recurrence defines basic PDHG for the composite semidefinite program.
review_flags: A PDHG-specific authoritative source and convergence locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and recurrence fit Basic PDHG for SDP, but the stepsize regime and convergence-related assumptions require a specific authoritative PDHG locator.

children.title: Preconditioned PDHG for SDP

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned PDHG for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric PDHG with positive-definite primal and dual preconditioners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle formulation of \(f(X)+g(\mathcal KX)\), let \(T\succ0\) and \(\Sigma\succ0\) be self-adjoint metric operators satisfying \(\|\Sigma^{1/2}\mathcal KT^{1/2}\|<1\). Initialize \(X^0,y^0\) and \(\bar X^0=X^0\). Iterate \(y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g^*}^{\Sigma^{-1}}(y^k+\Sigma\mathcal K\bar X^k)\), \(X^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f}^{T^{-1}}(X^k-T\mathcal K^*y^{k+1})\), and \(\bar X^{k+1}=2X^{k+1}-X^k\). Here \(\operatorname{prox}_{h}^{M}(v)=\arg\min_u\{h(u)+\tfrac12\|u-v\|_M^2\}\). Stop at the selected residual tolerances and output the current primal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned PDHG replaces scalar stepsizes by compatible primal and dual metrics that balance the SDP operator.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(\Sigma\) are self-adjoint and positive definite.
A saddle point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metric proximal recurrence defines a convergent preconditioned PDHG regime.
review_flags: A variable-metric PDHG theorem locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric algorithm fits the preconditioned-PDHG leaf, but the operator-norm condition and claimed convergent regime require an inspectable variable-metric PDHG theorem.

children.title: Inexact PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG regimes using approximate proximal or spectral computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG with summably inaccurate primal and dual proximal evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_y^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma\mathcal K\bar X^k)\) and \(P_X^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(X^k-\tau\mathcal K^*y^{k+1})\). Inexact PDHG chooses \(y^{k+1}\) and \(X^{k+1}\) satisfying \(\|y^{k+1}-P_y^k\|\le\epsilon_k^y\) and \(\|X^{k+1}-P_X^k\|_F\le\epsilon_k^X\), then sets \(\bar X^{k+1}=2X^{k+1}-X^k\). If \(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\epsilon_k^X+\epsilon_k^y)<\infty\), the perturbations have finite total magnitude and the iterates converge to a saddle point whenever one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact PDHG retains convergence when proximal errors are controlled by a summable error budget.
assumptions_latex: A saddle point exists.
\(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\).
\(\sum_k(\epsilon_k^X+\epsilon_k^y)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inexact iterates converge to a saddle point under the stated absolute-error model.

notation.meaning: Exact proximal updates at iteration k.

review_flags: The precise admissible inexactness model requires an inexact-PDHG theorem source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Inexact PDHG, but convergence under the stated iterate-distance error model and summability condition depends on a precise inexact-PDHG theorem that is not cited.

children.title: Matrix-Free PDHG

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG implemented through operator products and iterative spectral routines without dense constraint matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume access to oracles returning \(\mathcal KX\), \(\mathcal K^*y\), and products \(Zv\) for symmetric matrices entering the PSD proximal step. Initialize \(X^0,y^0\) in an implicit or factored representation. At iteration \(k\), compute the standard PDHG dual update using the \(\mathcal K\)-oracle, form the primal affine operator through the \(\mathcal K^*\)-oracle, and evaluate its PSD projection by a symmetric Krylov eigensolver using only products \(Zv\). Extrapolate the resulting primal iterate and stop at prescribed residual tolerances. No explicit matrix representation of \(\mathcal K\) or \(\mathcal K^*\) is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free PDHG uses operator and matrix-vector products, including Krylov spectral projection, instead of assembling dense SDP operators.
assumptions_latex: The actions of \(\mathcal K\) and \(\mathcal K^*\) are available and mutually adjoint.
Required symmetric matrix-vector products are available.
Oracle and spectral errors satisfy the selected exact or inexact PDHG regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each PDHG update can be executed without explicitly assembling the linear SDP operator.

children.title: Approximate Spectral Projection in PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG behavior under inexact semidefinite-cone projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Spectral Projection in PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact PSD proximal update controlled by spectral-projection error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the primal PDHG step, let \(Z^k=X^k-\tau(C+\mathcal K^*y^{k+1})\). Replace the exact projection \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(Z^k)\) by a spectral approximation \(P_k(Z^k)\) satisfying \(\|P_k(Z^k)-\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(Z^k)\|_F\le\epsilon_k\), and set \(X^{k+1}=P_k(Z^k)\) and \(\bar X^{k+1}=2X^{k+1}-X^k\). The approximation may retain computed positive eigenpairs and discard unresolved modes. Under the basic PDHG stepsize condition, a summable budget \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\epsilon_k<\infty\) places this update within the absolute-error inexact-PDHG convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate PSD projection is admissible when its Frobenius errors are bounded by a summable sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\).
A saddle point exists.
\(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\epsilon_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The approximate spectral step is a convergent inexact-PDHG update under the stated error model.
review_flags: The projection-error criterion and convergence transfer require a specific inexact-PDHG source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The approximate-projection algorithm fits the leaf, but transferring the Frobenius projection-error bound into convergent inexact PDHG under mere summability requires a specific theorem locator.

children.title: PDHG Convergence Theory for SDP

children.title: PDHG Ergodic Gap Bounds for SDP
children.top_down_role: Averaged-iterate primal-dual gap families.

knowledge_statements.title: PDHG Ergodic Gap Bounds for SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard averaged-iterate saddle-gap estimate for finite-dimensional SDP formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(X,y)=f(X)+\langle\mathcal KX,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), and run basic PDHG with \(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\). Define \(\bar X_N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^NX^k\) and \(\bar y_N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^Ny^k\). For every comparison pair \((X,y)\) in the effective domains, the standard ergodic estimate is \[L(\bar X_N,y)-L(X,\bar y_N)\le\frac{1}{N}\left(\frac{\|X-X^0\|_F^2}{2\tau}+\frac{\|y-y^0\|_2^2}{2\sigma}\right).\] Thus the restricted primal-dual gap of averaged iterates is \(O(N^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged PDHG iterates attain a primal-dual saddle-gap bound proportional to one over the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A saddle point exists.
\(\tau\sigma\|\mathcal K\|^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ergodic primal-dual gap decreases at rate \(O(N^{-1})\).

notation.meaning: Cesàro averages of the first N iterates.

review_flags: The exact PDHG ergodic-gap theorem and constants require an authoritative locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the ergodic-gap leaf, but the displayed universal comparison-pair inequality and its exact constants require an authoritative PDHG theorem locator.

children.title: PDHG Nonergodic Residual Regimes
children.top_down_role: Last-iterate and fixed-point residual families.

knowledge_statements.title: PDHG Nonergodic Residual Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Last-iterate fixed-point residual bounds when the PDHG map is averaged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the PDHG fixed-point map on the primal-dual variable \(z=(X,y)\), and suppose \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged in a Hilbertian metric \(H\), with \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). For \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), define \(R(z)=z-Tz\). For every \(z^*\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|R(z^k)\|_H^2\le\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}\|z^0-z^*\|_H^2,\qquad \min_{0\le k<N}\|R(z^k)\|_H\le\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{(1-\alpha)N}}\|z^0-z^*\|_H.\] Moreover, the last-iterate residual satisfies \(\|R(z^k)\|_H\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For averaged PDHG maps, last-iterate residuals vanish and the best residual among the first iterations has an inverse-square-root bound.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged in metric \(H\), with \(0<\alpha<1\).
\(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-point residual is square summable, vanishes nonergodically, and has best-iterate rate \(O(N^{-1/2})\).

notation.meaning: Norm induced by the PDHG metric.

review_flags: An averaged-operator PDHG residual theorem locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual complexity bound is mathematically plausible for an alpha-averaged map, but both the exact coefficient and the specialization of the PDHG map to the stated Hilbertian metric require an inspectable theorem source.

children.title: PDHG Scaling-Stability Regimes

children.title: PDHG Step-Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Step-size choices governing PDHG stability for SDP.

knowledge_statements.title: PDHG Step-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-step stability condition for finite-dimensional convex SDP saddle formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) be linear, and consider \(\min_x f(x)+g(Kx)\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions and may include semidefinite-cone indicators. The scalar PDHG iteration with primal step \(\tau>0\), dual step \(\sigma>0\), and extrapolation parameter \(\theta\in[0,1]\) lies in the standard strict stability regime when \[\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1.\] Under saddle-point existence, this condition makes the usual PDHG convergence theorem applicable; equality is excluded unless a sharper problem-specific result is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard scalar PDHG convergence applies when the product of primal and dual steps, multiplied by the squared coupling-operator norm, is strictly below one.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A saddle point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\) is the standard strict scalar step-size regime.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional PDHG stability inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict scalar condition is standard and fits the condition container, but no citation with an inspectable theorem or section locator supports the stated theta range and convergence applicability.

children.title: PDHG Preconditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Preconditioning choices for balancing SDP operator geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: PDHG Preconditioning Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite operator preconditioning for convex SDP saddle systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle problem associated with \(\min_x f(x)+g(Kx)\), let \(T:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\) and \(S:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y\) be self-adjoint positive-definite primal and dual step operators. The standard preconditioned PDHG regime is \[\left\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\right\rVert<1.\] Equivalently, the block operator \[\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\] is positive definite. Diagonal, block-diagonal, or spectral preconditioners are admissible whenever they satisfy this inequality and preserve computability of the corresponding weighted proximal mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operator preconditioning is stable when the norm of the coupling operator scaled by the primal and dual metrics is strictly below one.
assumptions_latex: \(T\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\) are self-adjoint.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The weighted proximal subproblems are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\), equivalently \(\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succ0\).

notation.meaning: Primal and dual metric or step operators.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled-norm and block-positivity conditions are mathematically consistent and fit the container, but the algorithmic admissibility and convergence claim requires a specific variable-metric PDHG source.

children.title: Operator-Scaled Stability Regions
children.top_down_role: Stable parameter regions induced by scaled operator norms.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Scaled Stability Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent norm and block-positivity descriptions of the PDHG stability region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear operator \(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) and self-adjoint positive-definite operators \(T\) and \(S\), define the strict operator-scaled stability region by \[\mathfrak S_K=\left\{(T,S):T\succ0,\ S\succ0,\ \rho\!\left(T^{1/2}K^*SKT^{1/2}\right)<1\right\}.\] In finite dimensions, \((T,S)\in\mathfrak S_K\) holds exactly when \(\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\), and exactly when \[\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succ0.\] Thus the spectral-radius, scaled-norm, and Schur-complement descriptions determine the same strict PDHG stability region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral-radius, scaled-operator-norm, and block-positive-definiteness tests describe the same strict operator-scaled PDHG stability region.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(T\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((T,S)\in\mathfrak S_K\iff\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\iff\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succ0\).

notation.meaning: Positive-definite primal and dual scaling operators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional norm identity and Schur-complement equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three finite-dimensional characterizations are consistent and representation is the correct knowledge kind, but no inspectable source supports their identification as the PDHG stability region.

children.title: Primal Augmented-Lagrangian Methods
children.top_down_role: Multiplier methods centered on primal matrix variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Augmented-Lagrangian Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-variable augmented-Lagrangian iteration for equality-constrained SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A X=b,\ X\succeq0\}\). Choose \(y^0\), penalties \(\sigma_k>0\), and inner tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\). At iteration \(k\), compute an approximate minimizer \(X^{k+1}\succeq0\) satisfying the prescribed tolerance for \[\min_{X\succeq0}\ \langle C,X\rangle+\langle y^k,\mathcal AX-b\rangle+\frac{\sigma_k}{2}\lVert\mathcal AX-b\rVert^2,\] then update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma_k(\mathcal AX^{k+1}-b).\] Stop when primal feasibility, dual stationarity, and complementarity residuals meet their tolerances; output \((X^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the primal augmented Lagrangian over the positive-semidefinite cone, then update the equality multiplier using the primal residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
\(\sigma_k>0\).
Each primal subproblem is solved to tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}\) and \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma_k(\mathcal AX^{k+1}-b)\) define one primal augmented-Lagrangian step.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical augmented-Lagrangian iteration for a primal SDP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration fits the primal augmented-Lagrangian algorithm container, but the prescribed inner tolerance is not defined and no SDP augmented-Lagrangian source fixes the sign convention or stopping conditions.

children.title: Dual Augmented-Lagrangian Methods
children.top_down_role: Multiplier methods centered on dual variables and cone projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Augmented-Lagrangian Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced dual augmented-Lagrangian iteration using spectral cone projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual SDP \(\min\{-b^Ty:\mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ S\succeq0\}\), choose \(X^0\succeq0\) and \(\sigma_k>0\). Approximately minimize over \(y\) the reduced function \[\psi_k(y)=-b^Ty+\frac{1}{2\sigma_k}\left(\left\lVert\Pi_+\!\left(X^k+\sigma_k(\mathcal A^*y-C)\right)\right\rVert_F^2-\lVert X^k\rVert_F^2\right).\] With the resulting \(y^{k+1}\), set \[X^{k+1}=\Pi_+\!\left(X^k+\sigma_k(\mathcal A^*y^{k+1}-C)\right).\] Stop when primal-dual feasibility and complementarity residuals satisfy their tolerances; recover the slack from the eliminated cone subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the reduced dual augmented Lagrangian, then update the primal multiplier by projecting a shifted matrix onto the positive-semidefinite cone.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) is the adjoint constraint operator.
\(X^0\succeq0\) and \(\sigma_k>0\).
The reduced subproblem is solved to a controlled tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}=\Pi_+(X^k+\sigma_k(\mathcal A^*y^{k+1}-C))\) is the dual augmented-Lagrangian multiplier update.

notation.meaning: Frobenius projection onto the positive-semidefinite cone.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard cone-eliminated dual ALM formula for SDP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced projection formula is convention-dependent. A specific dual SDP augmented-Lagrangian derivation is required to validate the signs, reduced objective, multiplier update, and eliminated-slack recovery.

children.title: Decomposed Augmented-Lagrangian Methods
children.top_down_role: Block and structured decompositions embedded in multiplier frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed Augmented-Lagrangian Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-structured multiplier iteration for separable conic SDP models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(X_i):\sum_{i=1}^p\mathcal A_iX_i=b,\ X_i\in K_i\}\), where each \(K_i\) is a closed convex cone and SDP blocks use \(K_i=\mathbb S^{n_i}_+\). Given \(y^k\) and \(\sigma_k>0\), approximately minimize \[\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(X_i)+\left\langle y^k,\sum_{i=1}^p\mathcal A_iX_i-b\right\rangle+\frac{\sigma_k}{2}\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^p\mathcal A_iX_i-b\right\rVert^2\] by a convergent block solver, then set \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma_k\left(\sum_{i=1}^p\mathcal A_iX_i^{k+1}-b\right).\] Stop using coupling-feasibility and block-optimality residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the separable conic augmented-Lagrangian subproblem by a convergent block method, then update the shared multiplier from the coupling residual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(K_i\).
The block inner scheme converges to the required subproblem accuracy.
\(\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma_k(\sum_i\mathcal A_iX_i^{k+1}-b)\) couples the decomposed primal blocks.

notation.meaning: Closed convex cone for block i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer multiplier template is plausible and algorithm is the correct kind, but “a convergent block solver” does not identify an update regime or sufficient conditions. A source for a precise decomposed ALM variant is required.

children.title: Semismooth Newton Methods for SDP

children.title: Dual Semismooth Newton Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Semismooth Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Newton iteration for a dual SDP projection equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\) be the residual of a reduced dual SDP subproblem, with \(F(y)=\nabla\psi(y)\), where \(\psi\) contains the spectral projection \(\Pi_+\). Starting from \(y^0\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(y^k)\) and regularization \(\mu_k\ge0\), compute \(d^k\) from \[(V_k+\mu_k I)d^k=-F(y^k),\] and select a backtracking step \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) satisfying sufficient decrease of \(\psi\). Set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_kd^k\). Stop when \(\lVert F(y^k)\rVert\) meets tolerance; recover the matrix variables through the associated positive-semidefinite projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a regularized generalized Newton step to the reduced dual projection residual, globalized by line search, and recover matrices by spectral projection.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth.
\(V_k\in\partial F(y^k)\) is a generalized Jacobian element.
The regularized Newton system is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_kd^k\), where \((V_k+\mu_kI)d^k=-F(y^k)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical globalized semismooth Newton scheme

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a generic semismooth Newton template rather than a source-fixed dual SDP method. The exact reduced residual, generalized Jacobian, merit function, and sufficient-decrease condition require citation.

children.title: Semismooth Newton-Conjugate-Gradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Generalized-Newton methods with iterative inner linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Newton-Conjugate-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact generalized Newton method with conjugate-gradient inner solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a semismooth residual \(F(y)=0\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(y^k)\) and \(\mu_k>0\). Use conjugate gradients to compute \(d^k\) satisfying \[\left\lVert(V_k+\mu_kI)d^k+F(y^k)\right\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert F(y^k)\rVert,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1.\] Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by a merit-function line search and set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_kd^k\). Terminate when the nonlinear residual and required SDP feasibility residuals meet tolerance. Matrix-vector products with \(V_k\), rather than an explicitly formed generalized Hessian, define the inner linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve each regularized generalized Newton system by conjugate gradients, globalize the step by line search, and stop on nonlinear and SDP residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth.
\(V_k+\mu_kI\) is self-adjoint positive definite on the solved subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert(V_k+\mu_kI)d^k+F(y^k)\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert F(y^k)\rVert\) defines the inexact Newton-CG step.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard inexact semismooth Newton-CG template

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inexact Newton-CG template fits the algorithm container, but applicability of conjugate gradients depends on the selected generalized Jacobian and regularization. An SDP-specific source must support those properties and the stopping rule.

children.title: Majorized Semismooth Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Stabilized Newton frameworks for composite and additionally constrained SDP models.

knowledge_statements.title: Majorized Semismooth Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Majorized generalized Newton iteration for composite constrained SDP subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi(z)=h(z)+q(z)\), where \(h\) is differentiable and \(q\) is proper, closed, and convex, possibly encoding semidefinite and additional simple constraints. Define the proximal residual \(F(z)=z-\operatorname{prox}_q(z-\nabla h(z))\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(z^k)\) and a self-adjoint majorization operator \(M_k\succeq0\); compute an inexact direction from \[(V_k+M_k+\mu_kI)d^k=-F(z^k),\] select a line-search step ensuring decrease of an accepted merit function or majorant, and set \(z^{k+1}=z^k+\alpha_kd^k\). Stop when \(\lVert F(z^k)\rVert\) meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive-semidefinite majorization and regularization term to the generalized Newton system, then globalize the composite residual step by line search.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) has locally Lipschitz gradient.
The proximal residual \(F\) is semismooth.
\(M_k\succeq0\) majorizes the curvature omitted by the local model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((V_k+M_k+\mu_kI)d^k=-F(z^k)\) defines the majorized semismooth Newton direction.

notation.meaning: Generalized Jacobian element of the residual.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic majorized semismooth Newton construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a generic proximal-residual construction, but does not identify which majorized semismooth Newton SDP framework it represents or formally state the majorization inequality. Variant-specific evidence is required.

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Convergence for SDP

children.title: Global Multiplier-Convergence Regime
children.top_down_role: Global behavior under solvability and controlled subproblem accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Multiplier-Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex SDP augmented-Lagrangian convergence with summable inner errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-dimensional convex SDP having a nonempty primal-dual solution set. Apply an augmented-Lagrangian method with penalties \(\sigma_k\ge\underline\sigma>0\), and suppose each subproblem satisfies an inexact optimality condition with error vector \(e_k\) such that \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\). Then the multiplier sequence is a summably perturbed proximal-point sequence for the relevant maximal monotone dual optimality operator. Consequently, the multipliers converge to a dual solution; the constraint residuals converge to zero; every cluster point of the associated primal iterates satisfying the subproblem optimality conditions is primal optimal; and the corresponding objective values converge to the common primal-dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a saddle point, penalties bounded away from zero, and summable inner errors, augmented-Lagrangian multipliers converge and feasibility residuals vanish.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
\(\sigma_k\ge\underline\sigma>0\).
\(\sum_k\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\to y^\star\), the feasibility residuals tend to \(0\), and qualifying primal cluster points are optimal.

notation.meaning: Penalty parameter at outer iteration k.
Perturbation induced by inexact subproblem solution.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical ALM as an inexact proximal-point method

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplier conclusion resembles inexact proximal-point convergence, but the stated primal cluster-point and objective-value conclusions need additional hypotheses and a precise mapping from subproblem errors to proximal perturbations. An exact theorem source is required.

children.title: Local Fast-Convergence Regime
children.top_down_role: Accelerated local behavior under error bounds and solution regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Fast-Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local multiplier acceleration under metric subregularity and increasingly accurate subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the maximal monotone dual optimality operator associated with a convex SDP, and suppose \(T^{-1}\) is metrically subregular at \((0,y^\star)\) with modulus \(\kappa\). For augmented-Lagrangian multipliers generated with penalty \(\sigma_k\) and sufficiently small relative subproblem errors, once \(y^k\) is near the solution set \(Y^\star\), \[\operatorname{dist}(y^{k+1},Y^\star)\le\left(\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2+\sigma_k^2}}+o(1)\right)\operatorname{dist}(y^k,Y^\star).\] Hence fixed sufficiently large penalties give local linear convergence, while \(\sigma_k\to\infty\) together with vanishing relative inner errors gives Q-superlinear convergence of multiplier distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity yields local linear multiplier convergence; increasing penalties and vanishing relative inner errors make the multiplier distance converge superlinearly.
assumptions_latex: \(T^{-1}\) is metrically subregular at \((0,y^\star)\) with modulus \(\kappa\).
The iterates enter a neighborhood where the error bound holds.
Relative subproblem errors vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(y^{k+1},Y^\star)\le(\kappa/\sqrt{\kappa^2+\sigma_k^2}+o(1))\operatorname{dist}(y^k,Y^\star)\), with Q-superlinear convergence if \(\sigma_k\to\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal-point contraction under metric subregularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed contraction factor is theorem-specific. The regularity hypothesis may need metric subregularity of T at (y-star,0), or an explicitly equivalent property of its inverse, and the relative-error term must be quantified by a source.

children.title: Inexact Subproblem Regime
children.top_down_role: Outer convergence with controlled inner solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subproblem Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer augmented-Lagrangian convergence under absolute summability of inner errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the maximal monotone multiplier optimality operator for a solvable finite-dimensional convex SDP. Suppose an inexact augmented-Lagrangian step satisfies \[y^{k+1}=J_{\sigma_kT}(y^k)+e_k,\qquad J_{\sigma_kT}=(I+\sigma_kT)^{-1},\] where \(\sigma_k\ge\underline\sigma>0\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\). Then \((y^k)\) is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(T^{-1}(0)\), converges to a multiplier in \(T^{-1}(0)\), and has vanishing proximal residual. Thus any inner stopping rule that implies the displayed summable perturbation preserves outer multiplier convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented-Lagrangian convergence survives inexact inner solves when their induced proximal-point perturbations are summable and penalties stay positive.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is maximal monotone and \(T^{-1}(0)\ne\varnothing\).
\(\sigma_k\ge\underline\sigma>0\).
\(\sum_k\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\to y^\star\in T^{-1}(0)\) and \(\lVert y^k-J_{\sigma_kT}(y^k)\rVert\to0\).

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the scaled optimality operator.
Inner-solve perturbation in the multiplier step.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The summably perturbed resolvent theorem is plausible, but no source establishes that the relevant SDP augmented-Lagrangian step has exactly the displayed additive-error form or identifies an inner stopping rule that implies it.

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Penalty-Update Conditions

children.title: Bounded-Penalty Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence organization when penalty parameters stabilize.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and continuously differentiable on the primal matrix space.
The augmented-Lagrangian subproblems are solved with errors \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\operatorname{tr}X\leq\tau\}\), and let the convex differentiable function \(f\) have curvature at most \(C_f\) on \(\mathcal D\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The spectrahedron \(\mathcal D=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^2:X_{11}=1\}\) is unbounded because \(X_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,s)\in\mathcal D\) for every \(s\geq0\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of rank-one oracle atoms when the active eigenvalue lacks a gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the trace-one PSD domain, a linear oracle for \(G\in\mathbb S^n\) may return \(vv^{\mathsf T}\), where \(v\) is a unit eigenvector for \(\lambda_{\min}(G)\). knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Rank Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case rank accumulation under rank-one conditional-gradient updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X_0\in\mathbb S_+^n\) has rank \(r_0\), and conditional-gradient iterates satisfy \(X_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)X_t+\gamma_t\tau v_tv_t^{\mathsf T}\), with \(0\leq\gamma_t\leq1\) and \(\|v_t\|_2=1\). Then \(X_t\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(X_t)\leq\min\{n,r_0+t\}\). The bound can increase by one at each iteration when the newly selected vector lies outside the range of the current iterate; projection-free updates therefore do not by themselves keep rank uniformly bounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Storage Growth

children.title: Spectral-Atom Compression Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of compression strategies for controlling rank or storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Atom Compression Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and Frobenius-approximate limits of compressing PSD spectral atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\succeq0\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\). Any sum of \(k\) rank-one PSD atoms has rank at most \(k\), so exact representation of \(X\) requires \(k\geq\operatorname{rank}(X)\). Moreover, among PSD matrices \(Z\) of rank at most \(k\), the smallest Frobenius error is \(\min\|X-Z\|_F=(\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i^2)^{1/2}\). Thus compression below the rank is necessarily lossy, and achieving error at most \(\varepsilon\) requires the spectral tail to satisfy \(\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i^2\leq\varepsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact compression needs at least the matrix rank many atoms; approximate compression is possible only when the discarded eigenvalue tail is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact compression requires \(k\geq\operatorname{rank}(X)\), while Frobenius error \(\varepsilon\) requires \(\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i^2\leq\varepsilon^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Factorized PSD Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gram factorization of PSD matrices with an explicit rank cap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and an integer \(1\leq r\leq n\), there exists \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) such that \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) if and only if \(X\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq r\). Consequently, replacing an SDP variable \(X\succeq0\) by \(YY^{\mathsf T}\) enforces positive semidefiniteness and a rank bound automatically, while transforming affine constraints \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and a linear objective \(\langle C,X\rangle\) into quadratic expressions in \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix has an n-by-r Gram factor exactly when it is positive semidefinite with rank at most r.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(1\leq r\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\text{ for some }Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\iff X\succeq0\text{ and }\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq r\).

children.title: Factor Quotient Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Quotient Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal quotient model for fixed-rank positive semidefinite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:\operatorname{rank}(Y)=r\}\). The orthogonal group \(O(r)\) acts on this set by \(Y\mapsto YQ\), and \((YQ)(YQ)^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}\). For full-column-rank factors, \(YY^{\mathsf T}=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\) holds exactly when \(Z=YQ\) for some \(Q\in O(r)\). Hence the quotient \(\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}/O(r)\) is in bijection with the rank-\(r\) PSD matrices, removing the factorization's orthogonal nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-rank factors differing by a right orthogonal transformation represent the same PSD matrix, and these are the only such redundancies.
assumptions_latex: \(1\leq r\leq n\).
\(Y,Z\in\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predetermined factor dimension maintained throughout factorized optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a factor dimension \(r\), the fixed-rank regime solves over \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) without changing \(r\), using \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\). Its representable feasible set is \(\mathcal F_r=\{X\succeq0:\mathcal A(X)=b,\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq r\}\). It is equivalent to the original feasible set \(\mathcal F=\{X\succeq0:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\) only when every required solution is representable at rank at most \(r\); otherwise the factorized problem imposes a genuine rank restriction and can exclude all globally optimal SDP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed factor width restricts optimization to feasible PSD matrices of rank at most that width and may exclude the SDP optimum.

\(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a feasible or penalized factor \(Y_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_0}\). Adaptivity means that factor dimension is selected from computed diagnostics rather than fixed in advance.

The zero-padding transfer preserves the represented matrix because \(\widehat Y_k\widehat Y_k^{\mathsf T}=Y_kY_k^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Triggered Rank Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive Burer–Monteiro rank expansion driven by failure of a recovered dual slack to be positive semidefinite.

At an approximately stationary factor, compute a multiplier \(\lambda\) and slack \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(\lambda)\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\geq-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), stop and return \((YY^{\mathsf T},\lambda)\). Otherwise choose a unit vector \(v\) satisfying \(v^{\mathsf T}Sv< -\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), replace \(Y\) by \(\widehat Y=[Y\;0]\), and restart the factor solver from a feasible retraction of \(\widehat Y+tve_{p+1}^{\mathsf T}\). knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected first-order optimization on a smooth manifold of feasible SDP factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M_p=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}:\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})=b\}\) be a smooth embedded manifold and let \(f(Y)=\langle C,YY^{\mathsf T}\rangle\). Given \(Y_0\in\mathcal M_p\), iterate \(G_k=\operatorname{grad}f(Y_k)=\operatorname{Proj}_{T_{Y_k}\mathcal M_p}(2CY_k)\). Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a descent line search and set \(Y_{k+1}=R_{Y_k}(-\alpha_kG_k)\), where \(R\) is a retraction. Stop when \(\|G_k\|_F\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(X_k=Y_kY_k^{\mathsf T}\). Under standard bounded-level-set and line-search conditions, every accumulation point is Riemannian first-order stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the Euclidean gradient onto the feasible factor manifold, retract a line-searched step, and stop when the Riemannian gradient is small.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M_p\) is a smooth embedded manifold.
\(R\) is a first-order retraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Trust-Region Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order trust-region optimization on a smooth manifold of feasible SDP factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For smooth \(f:\mathcal M_p\to\mathbb R\), initialize \(Y_0\in\mathcal M_p\) and \(\Delta_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), approximately minimize \[m_k(\eta)=f(Y_k)+\langle\operatorname{grad}f(Y_k),\eta\rangle+\tfrac12\langle\eta,\operatorname{Hess}f(Y_k)[\eta]\rangle\] over \(\eta\in T_{Y_k}\mathcal M_p\) with \(\|\eta\|\leq\Delta_k\). Compare actual with predicted decrease, accept a successful step by setting \(Y_{k+1}=R_{Y_k}(\eta_k)\), and update \(\Delta_k\) by the trust ratio. Stop when \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(Y_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Hess}f(Y_k))\geq-\varepsilon_H\).

children.title: Constraint-Count Rank Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Count Rank Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-block Burer–Monteiro rank threshold expressed through the number of independent affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an SDP with one matrix variable \(X\in\mathbb S^n_+\), \(m\) independent affine equality constraints, and factorization \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). The constraint-count rank regime is \[\tau(p):=\frac{p(p+1)}2>m.\] Equivalently, the dimension \(\tau(p)\) of \(\mathbb S^p\) exceeds the number of independent scalar constraints. Under compactness and regularity of the factor-feasible set, this is the standard dimension condition used to obtain almost-every-cost second-order landscape guarantees.

assumptions_latex: \(m\) counts linearly independent affine equality constraints.

Landscape conclusions additionally require compactness and regularity of the product factor-feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Condition Tightness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of universal second-order optimality guarantees below the constraint-count rank threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the rank-one factorization of the SDP \(\min\{X_{12}:X\in\mathbb S^2_+,\ X_{11}=X_{22}=1\}\), namely \(X=yy^{\mathsf T}\) with \(y\in\mathbb R^2\). The factors \((1,1)\) and \((-1,-1)\) are isolated second-order critical points with objective value \(1\), whereas the global value is \(-1\). Here \(p=1\), \(m=2\), and \(p(p+1)/2\leq m\).

children.title: Generic-Cost Landscape Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Generic-Cost Landscape Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-every-objective benign-landscape theorem for a regular single-block Burer–Monteiro factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and its factorization over \(\mathcal M_p=\{Y:\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})=b\}\). Assume \(\mathcal M_p\) is nonempty, compact, and a smooth manifold, and that \(p(p+1)/2>m\), where \(m\) is the number of independent constraints. Then, for Lebesgue-almost every \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), every Riemannian second-order critical point \(Y\in\mathcal M_p\) is globally optimal for the factor problem, and \(YY^{\mathsf T}\) is globally optimal for the SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Above the triangular rank threshold, almost every cost matrix gives a factor landscape whose second-order critical points are globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M_p\) is nonempty, compact, and smooth.
The cost matrix is outside a Lebesgue-null exceptional subset of \(\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every Riemannian second-order critical factor \(Y\) yields a globally optimal SDP matrix \(YY^{\mathsf T}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard almost-all-cost Burer–Monteiro landscape theorem

children.title: Generic-Constraint Landscape Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Generic-Constraint Landscape Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-data regularity needed to place factorized SDP optimization on a smooth manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_{\mathcal A}(Y)=\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})\), constraint data \((\mathcal A,b)\) are regular at rank \(p\) when \[DF_{\mathcal A}(Y)[U]=\mathcal A(YU^{\mathsf T}+UY^{\mathsf T})\] is surjective onto \(\mathbb R^m\) for every \(Y\) satisfying \(F_{\mathcal A}(Y)=b\). Then \(b\) is a regular value and the feasible factor set is a smooth embedded manifold of codimension \(m\). For fixed \(\mathcal A\), Sard's theorem makes regular values generic in \(b\), provided regular values exist. This regularity supports, but does not replace, the separate generic-cost and rank hypotheses used for benign-landscape conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint data are regular when every feasible factor has a surjective constraint Jacobian; this produces the smooth manifold needed by landscape theorems.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{\mathcal A}:\mathbb R^{n\times p}\to\mathbb R^m\) is the quadratic constraint map.
The affine constraints are represented without redundant coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under surjectivity, \(F_{\mathcal A}^{-1}(b)\) is a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \(np-m\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the regular-value theorem gives the stated manifold conclusion
source required for the precise genericity class in joint SDP constraint data

knowledge_statements.title: Nongeneric Spurious-Critical-Point Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured objective and constraint data can create nonglobal second-order critical factors outside generic landscape hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{X_{12}:X\in\mathbb S^2_+,\ X_{11}=X_{22}=1\}\] and impose the factorization \(X=yy^{\mathsf T}\) with \(y\in\mathbb R^2\). Feasibility requires \(y_1^2=y_2^2=1\), so the factor-feasible set consists of four isolated points. At \(y=(1,1)\) and \(y=(-1,-1)\), the objective equals \(1\), although the global value \(-1\) occurs when \(y_1y_2=-1\). Because the tangent space at every feasible factor is \(\{0\}\), the two nonglobal factors satisfy both first- and second-order tangent-space criticality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one two-variable correlation SDP has isolated nonglobal factors that vacuously satisfy first- and second-order criticality.
assumptions_latex: Criticality is evaluated on the rank-one factor-feasible set.
The objective is the structured linear functional \(X\mapsto X_{12}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without the genericity and rank hypotheses, a factorized SDP may possess spurious second-order critical points.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Primal Optimality

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Primal Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global SDP optimality certified by a rank-deficient second-order critical factor and its multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) be feasible with \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)<p\). Suppose there is \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(SY=0\), where \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(\lambda)\), and the factorized Lagrangian has nonnegative second variation along every tangent direction. Choose nonzero \(z\in\ker Y\). For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the direction \(U=vz^{\mathsf T}\) is tangent, so second-order criticality gives \(2\|z\|_2^2v^{\mathsf T}Sv\geq0\). Hence \(S\succeq0\), and \((YY^{\mathsf T},\lambda,S)\) is a primal–dual certificate of global SDP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deficient factor supplies nullspace tangent directions that force its stationary dual slack to be positive semidefinite, thereby certifying global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is feasible and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)<p\).
A multiplier \(\lambda\) satisfies factor stationarity \((C-\mathcal A^*(\lambda))Y=0\).
The factorized Lagrangian has nonnegative curvature on the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) is globally optimal for the original SDP, with dual slack \(S\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: nonzero vector in the factor nullspace

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nullspace-generated tangent directions force positivity of the stationary slack

children.title: Dual-Certificate Recovery from Factors
children.top_down_role: Construction and checking of dual information from factorized critical points.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Certificate Recovery from Factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for an equality-constrained Burer–Monteiro factorization at a rank-deficient second-order critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) with \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). Suppose \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfies \(SY=0\), where \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(\lambda)\), and the factor Lagrangian Hessian is nonnegative on the linearized feasible space. If \(Yz=0\) for some nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), then the directions \(U=xz^{\mathsf T}\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), are linearized-feasible and yield \(x^{\mathsf T}Sx\ge0\). Hence \(S\succeq0\), and \((X,\lambda,S)\) is primal-dual feasible with \(\langle S,X\rangle=0\), certifying global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null direction of a rank-deficient factor converts second-order stationarity into positive semidefiniteness of the dual slack, yielding a checkable zero-gap optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})=b\), and a stationarity multiplier exists.
The factor Lagrangian Hessian is nonnegative on the linearized feasible space.
\(\operatorname{rank}(Y)<p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(\lambda)\succeq0\) and \(\langle C,X\rangle=b^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) for \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\).

children.title: Smooth-Manifold Stationarity Regime
children.top_down_role: Second-order analysis on regular factorized constraint manifolds.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Manifold Stationarity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First- and second-order stationarity for regular equality constraints on a factor manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^{n\times p}\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R^{n\times p}\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, and let \(\mathcal M=g^{-1}(0)\). If \(Dg(Y)\) is surjective, then \(\mathcal M\) is locally a smooth embedded manifold with tangent space \(T_Y\mathcal M=\ker Dg(Y)\). The point \(Y\) is second-order stationary when there is \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(\nabla f(Y)+Dg(Y)^*\lambda=0\) and \(\langle U,\nabla^2_{YY}(f+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g)(Y)[U]\rangle\ge0\) for every \(U\in T_Y\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under constraint regularity, factor feasibility is a smooth manifold, and second-order stationarity is Lagrangian stationarity plus nonnegative curvature along every tangent direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are twice continuously differentiable.
\(g(Y)=0\) and \(Dg(Y)\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\) satisfies the displayed first- and second-order manifold stationarity conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regular-level-set and second-order stationarity formulation is precise and the condition kind fits the regime, but no inspectable source supports it.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Constraint Stationarity Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a closed subset of a Euclidean space, let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable, and let \(x\) be a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(K\). Every Bouligand tangent direction \(d\in T_K(x)\) satisfies \(\langle
abla f(x),dangle\ge0\). If equality holds and \(w\in T_K^2(x;d)\) is a second-order feasible displacement, then \[\langle

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is closed and \(x\) is a local minimizer over \(K\).

children.title: Approximate Second-Order Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Finite-accuracy criticality and approximate optimality interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Second-Order Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-accuracy second-order stationarity on a regular factor constraint manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a Riemannian factor constraint manifold and let \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable. For tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H\ge0\), a point \(Y\in\mathcal M\) is an \((\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)\)-second-order stationary point if \[\|\operatorname{grad}f(Y)\|\le\varepsilon_g,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Hess}f(Y))\ge-\varepsilon_H.\] The minimum eigenvalue is taken over the self-adjoint Riemannian Hessian acting on \(T_Y\mathcal M\). An approximate-global-optimality theorem must separately quantify how these residuals, rank, and problem conditioning control the primal objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate second-order stationarity bounds the Riemannian gradient norm and permits only limited negative curvature; translating those residuals into an SDP gap requires additional conditioning estimates.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a smooth Riemannian manifold.
\(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(Y)\|\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Hess}f(Y))\ge-\varepsilon_H\).

children.title: Under-Parameterized Factor Models

knowledge_statements.title: Under-Parameterized Factor Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability fails whenever the factor width is below the rank required by every feasible or optimal SDP matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), every represented matrix \(YY^{\mathsf T}\) has rank at most \(p\). Consequently, if an SDP has no optimal solution of rank at most \(p\), its factorized problem cannot attain the SDP optimum; if every feasible matrix has rank exceeding \(p\), the factorized feasible set is empty. Concretely, the SDP with constraint \(X=I_n\), cone constraint \(X\succeq0\), and zero objective is feasible, whereas its factorization \(YY^{\mathsf T}=I_n\) is infeasible for every \(p<n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A width-p factor represents only rank-at-most-p matrices. If the SDP requires larger rank, factorization loses the optimum or even all feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) has \(p\) columns.
The original variable is represented exactly as \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Required rank exceeding \(p\) is a sharp representability obstruction for the factor model.

children.title: Singular Factor Constraint Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Factor Constraint Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A vanishing constraint Jacobian can make the linearized space strictly larger than the true tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the scalar constraint \(g(Y)=\|Y\|_F^2=0\) on \(\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). Its feasible set is the singleton \(\{0\}\), so the true tangent cone at \(Y=0\) is \(\{0\}\). However, \(Dg(0)=0\), and therefore the linearized constraint space \(\ker Dg(0)\) is all of \(\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). Thus the regular-level-set identity \(T_Y\mathcal M=\ker Dg(Y)\) fails, multipliers need not encode the geometry faithfully, and smooth-manifold stationarity tests cannot be applied without an additional constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an irregular factor constraint, the Jacobian kernel may contain directions that are not genuinely feasible, invalidating regular-manifold tangent and Hessian tests.

children.title: Factor Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling behavior arising from nonunique factor representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scaling laws for a positive semidefinite matrix and its single factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). For any scalar \(c\), the scaled factor \(cY\) represents \(c^2X\), not \(cX\). Moreover, \[\|X\|_2=\|Y\|_2^2,\qquad \|X\|_F\le\|Y\|_F^2,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(X)=\|Y\|_F^2.\] Thus maintaining a bound on the trace of the SDP iterate is equivalent to maintaining a Frobenius-norm bound on its factor. Factors representing the same matrix differ at least by right orthogonal transformations, which preserve all singular values and these scale quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD factorization squares scalar and spectral scales: trace equals the factor’s squared Frobenius norm, and the matrix spectral norm equals the squared factor spectral norm.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) and \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Factor magnitudes control matrix magnitudes quadratically according to the displayed identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of a positive semidefinite matrix is the square of conditioning of its nonzero factor spectrum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) have positive singular values \(\sigma_1(Y)\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r(Y)>0\), and set \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\). The positive eigenvalues of \(X\) are \(\sigma_i(Y)^2\), so the effective spectral condition numbers satisfy \[\kappa_+(X)=\frac{\lambda_1(X)}{\lambda_r(X)}=\left(\frac{\sigma_1(Y)}{\sigma_r(Y)}\right)^2=\kappa_+(Y)^2.\] Hence \(\sigma_r(Y)\downarrow0\) simultaneously causes factor ill-conditioning, approach to a lower-rank stratum, and amplification of perturbations in inverse or pseudoinverse operations used by local models and certificate recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small nonzero factor singular values are squared in the PSD matrix, so matrix conditioning deteriorates quadratically and pseudoinverse-based computations become unstable near rank loss.
assumptions_latex: \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\).
\(r=\operatorname{rank}(Y)\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_+(X)=\kappa_+(Y)^2\), with instability as \(\sigma_r(Y)\to0\).

notation.meaning: Condition number restricted to positive singular or eigenvalues

children.title: Rank-Identification Instability
children.top_down_role: Unstable identification of effective factor rank near ill-conditioned solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Identification Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical rank is discontinuous when a singular value lies at the chosen identification threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a threshold \(\tau>0\) and define numerical rank by counting singular values strictly larger than \(\tau\). For \(Y_\delta=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ldots,1,\tau+\delta)\), arbitrarily small positive and negative values of \(\delta\) produce numerical ranks differing by one, although \(\|Y_\delta-Y_0\|_2=|\delta|\). More generally, perturbations of spectral norm \(\eta\) can move each singular value by as much as \(\eta\). Therefore rank identification is stable only when the relevant singular values are separated from \(\tau\) by a margin larger than the perturbation level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a factor singular value is near the numerical-rank threshold, an arbitrarily small perturbation can change the identified rank; a spectral gap is required for stability.
assumptions_latex: Numerical rank uses a fixed threshold \(\tau>0\).
Perturbations are measured in spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reliable rank identification requires \(\min_i|\sigma_i(Y)-\tau|>\eta\) against perturbations bounded by \(\eta\).

children.title: Nyström PSD Sketches

knowledge_statements.title: Nyström PSD Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive semidefinite reconstruction from a randomized range sketch and its compressed Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and choose \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\). Define \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Omega^{\mathsf T}X\Omega\). The Nyström reconstruction is \[\widehat X=YW^\dagger Y^{\mathsf T}=X\Omega(\Omega^{\mathsf T}X\Omega)^\dagger\Omega^{\mathsf T}X.\] It is positive semidefinite and has rank at most \(k\). If \(\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(X\Omega)\), equivalently the sketch captures the entire range of \(X\), then \(\widehat X=X\). Otherwise it is a range-restricted positive semidefinite approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Nyström sketch reconstructs a PSD approximation from X times a test matrix and a small compressed Gram matrix, preserving PSD structure and becoming exact when the range is captured.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X=X\Omega(\Omega^{\mathsf T}X\Omega)^\dagger\Omega^{\mathsf T}X\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le k\).

notation.meaning: Test matrix for the range sketch

children.title: Two-Sided Matrix Sketches

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Matrix Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-rank reconstruction from independent sketches of a matrix range and co-range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), and \(\Psi\in\mathbb R^{m\times \ell}\). Store the two-sided sketches \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(Z=\Psi^{\mathsf T}X\), and reconstruct \[\widehat X=Y(\Psi^{\mathsf T}Y)^\dagger Z.\] If \(X=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) has rank \(r\), \(V^{\mathsf T}\Omega\) has row rank \(r\), and \(\Psi^{\mathsf T}U\) has column rank \(r\), then \(\widehat X=X\). Without these rank conditions, the same formula gives a compressed low-rank approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided sketches retain range and co-range information. A small coupling pseudoinverse reconstructs an exactly rank-r matrix when both test matrices capture its singular subspaces.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\) have compatible dimensions.
For exactness, both displayed subspace rank conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X=Y(\Psi^{\mathsf T}Y)^\dagger Z\), and under the stated rank conditions \(\widehat X=X\).

children.title: Streaming Rank-One Sketch Updates
