knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Rank-One Sketch Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-memory sketch maintenance for affine combinations with rank-one positive semidefinite atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\). For a PSD stream initialized by \(X_0=0\), store \(Y_0=X_0\Omega=0\) and \(W_0=\Omega^{\mathsf T}X_0\Omega=0\). Given an implicit update \(X_{t+1}=\alpha_tX_t+\beta_tv_tv_t^{\mathsf T}\) with \(\alpha_t,\beta_t\ge0\), compute \[q_t=\Omega^{\mathsf T}v_t,\qquad Y_{t+1}=\alpha_tY_t+\beta_tv_tq_t^{\mathsf T},\qquad W_{t+1}=\alpha_tW_t+\beta_tq_tq_t^{\mathsf T}.\] At any stopping time, output the Nyström reconstruction \(\widehat X_t=Y_tW_t^\dagger Y_t^{\mathsf T}\). The maintained sketches equal those of the implicit iterate exactly in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each rank-one PSD update, update the range sketch and compressed Gram matrix using only a matrix-vector product; reconstruct a PSD approximation when the stream stops.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is fixed throughout the stream.
\(\alpha_t,\beta_t\ge0\), preserving positive semidefiniteness.
Updates are evaluated in exact arithmetic for the stated invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\), \(Y_t=X_t\Omega\) and \(W_t=\Omega^{\mathsf T}X_t\Omega\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The update equations preserve both sketch invariants in exact arithmetic and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no evidence record supports the streaming construction.

children.title: Sketchy SDP Methods
children.top_down_role: Generic sketch-maintenance and terminal reconstruction frameworks for SDP iterates.

children.title: Sketch-Then-Reconstruct Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods optimizing compressed state and reconstructing a terminal PSD approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Then-Reconstruct Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage randomized compression for a PSD iterate followed by terminal low-rank recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an implicit matrix \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), target rank \(r\), and Gaussian test matrix \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) with \(k>r\), form and store \(Y=X\Omega\) while optimizing without retaining \(X\). At termination, compute \(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\), obtain a small symmetric matrix \(B\in\mathbb S^k\) from the available sketch by a prescribed least-squares or Nyström reconstruction, and set \(\widehat X=Q[B]_+^{(r)}Q^\top\), where \([B]_+^{(r)}\) retains the largest \(r\) positive eigenvalues. Output \(\widehat X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) of rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compress the implicit PSD iterate during optimization, then recover a rank-at-most-r PSD matrix from the terminal sketch using a small eigenvalue problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is accessible through products needed to form its sketch.
\(\Omega\) is independent of the optimization data used to construct \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le r\).

notation.meaning: rank-r truncation of the positive part of a symmetric matrix
matrix with orthonormal columns spanning the range of Y

review_flags: Exact reconstruction map varies among Sketchy SDP variants; a method-specific source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the method container, but no citation identifies the prescribed reconstruction map or establishes that the maintained sketch contains enough information to obtain B.

children.title: Online Sketch-Maintenance Methods
children.top_down_role: Incremental sketch updates synchronized with the outer optimization process.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Sketch-Maintenance Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental maintenance of a linear sketch under low-rank convex updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\). Initialize \(Y_0=X_0\Omega\). If the outer method updates \(X_{t+1}=(1-\eta_t)X_t+\eta_t V_t\), where \(0\leq\eta_t\leq1\) and \(V_t=v_tv_t^\top\succeq0\), update only the sketch by \[Y_{t+1}=(1-\eta_t)Y_t+\eta_t v_t(v_t^\top\Omega).\] Stop according to the outer optimization criterion and return \(Y_T\) to the reconstruction routine. In exact arithmetic, induction gives \(Y_t=X_t\Omega\) for every \(t\), without storing any dense \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply each rank-one convex update directly to the sketch; the maintained matrix equals the sketch of the unmaterialized outer iterate at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(X_{t+1}=(1-\eta_t)X_t+\eta_t v_tv_t^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_t=X_t\Omega\) for all \(t\geq0\).

notation.meaning: maintained range sketch of the implicit primal iterate

review_flags: The algebraic invariant is standard, but no supplied locator documents this Sketchy SDP update.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incremental sketch invariant is mathematically consistent and the algorithm kind fits, but no inspectable source locator supports its use in the intended Sketchy SDP method.

children.title: SketchyCGAL
children.top_down_role: Storage-efficient coupling of CGAL with PSD sketching and reconstruction.

children.title: SketchyCGAL Operator Model
children.top_down_role: Matrix-free constraint access combined with compressed primal state.

knowledge_statements.title: SketchyCGAL Operator Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free state and oracle interface for a standard-form primal SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the SDP \[\min_{X\succeq0}\ \langle C,X\rangle\quad\text{subject to}\quad \mathcal A X=b,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(X)=\alpha,\] SketchyCGAL represents the primal state by \(z_t=\mathcal A X_t\), \(c_t=\langle C,X_t\rangle\), and \(Y_t=X_t\Omega\), rather than by \(X_t\). An iteration may evaluate \(\mathcal A(vv^\top)\), \(v^\top Cv\), and an approximate minimum-eigenvector of \(C+\mathcal A^*y\). Thus it requires applications of \(\mathcal A\), \(\mathcal A^*\), and matrix-vector products with the resulting symmetric operator, but no dense primal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SketchyCGAL stores constraint values, objective value, and a range sketch, while accessing the SDP through linear-operator and minimum-eigenvector oracles.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\).
The trace bound \(\alpha\) is finite.
The required eigenvector oracle is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outer state can be updated without explicitly storing \(X_t\in\mathbb S^n\).

notation.meaning: constraint image of the implicit primal iterate

review_flags: A primary SketchyCGAL source is needed to certify the precise oracle interface and state variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the operator-model container, but the precise state variables, trace-constrained SDP form, and oracle interface require a primary SketchyCGAL source.

children.title: SketchyCGAL Reconstruction Interface
children.top_down_role: Low-rank PSD output recovery from maintained sketches.

knowledge_statements.title: SketchyCGAL Reconstruction Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD rank-constrained recovery from the terminal SketchyCGAL range sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the terminal sketch \(Y=X\Omega\), set \(H=(\Omega^\top Y+Y^\top\Omega)/2\) and let \(H_+^{\dagger/2}\) be the pseudoinverse square root of its positive part. Form \(Z=YH_+^{\dagger/2}\), compute a rank-\(r\) truncated singular value decomposition \(Z_r=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^\top\), and output \[\widehat X=U_r\Sigma_r^2U_r^\top.\] The reconstruction uses only \(Y\), \(\Omega\), and matrices of sketch dimension. It returns a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix with rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilized Nyström reconstruction converts the terminal range sketch into a rank-r PSD output using only small factorizations and a truncated SVD.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(Y=X\Omega\).
\(1\leq r\leq k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq r\).

notation.meaning: pseudoinverse square root of the positive part of H
best rank-r truncated SVD of Z

review_flags: The exact stabilized Nyström formula must be checked against the intended SketchyCGAL implementation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the reconstruction-interface container, but the stabilized Nyström formula and its identification with SketchyCGAL cannot be certified without a method-specific locator.

children.title: Sketchy SDP Approximation Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Approximation families separating reconstruction, objective, feasibility, and storage quality.

children.title: Low-Rank Reconstruction Quality
children.top_down_role: Approximation quality of reconstructed PSD outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Reconstruction Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected trace-norm quality of Gaussian Nyström reconstruction for a PSD matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), let \(X_r\) be its best rank-\(r\) approximation, and draw a standard Gaussian \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) with \(k>r+1\). For the untruncated Nyström approximation \(X_{\mathrm{nys}}=X\Omega(\Omega^\top X\Omega)^\dagger\Omega^\top X\), the expected trace-norm error obeys \[\mathbb E\|X-X_{\mathrm{nys}}\|_*\leq\left(1+\frac{r}{k-r-1}\right)\|X-X_r\|_*.\] A subsequent best rank-\(r\) PSD truncation has quality controlled, up to a reconstruction-dependent constant, by the same spectral tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian Nyström recovery approaches the best rank-r trace-norm error as sketch size exceeds r, with degradation governed by the discarded spectral tail.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(\Omega\) has independent standard Gaussian entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\|X-X_{\mathrm{nys}}\|_*\leq(1+r/(k-r-1))\|X-X_r\|_*\).

notation.meaning: best rank-r approximation obtained from the leading eigenpairs of X

review_flags: The exact expectation constant and the effect of terminal rank truncation require a randomized linear-algebra source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but the exact expected trace-norm constant requires an authoritative randomized Nyström source. The additional rank-truncation claim gives no explicit constant and also needs support.

children.title: Optimization-Quality Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of objective and feasibility quality to reconstructed outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Quality Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic transfer from nuclear-norm reconstruction error to objective and feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,\widehat X\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. If \(\|X-\widehat X\|_*\leq\delta\), then \[|\langle C,\widehat X-X\rangle|\leq\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}\delta,\qquad \|\mathcal A\widehat X-b\|\leq\|\mathcal AX-b\|+\|\mathcal A\|_{*\to\|\cdot\|}\delta.\] Consequently, an \(\varepsilon_f\)-feasible implicit iterate with objective gap at most \(\varepsilon_o\) yields a reconstructed iterate whose feasibility and objective errors are at most \(\varepsilon_f+\|\mathcal A\|_{*\to\|\cdot\|}\delta\) and \(\varepsilon_o+\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}\delta\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nuclear-norm reconstruction error adds linearly to objective and feasibility errors, with constants determined by the cost matrix and constraint operator.
assumptions_latex: \(\|X-\widehat X\|_*\leq\delta\).
\(\mathcal A\) is bounded from nuclear norm to the selected residual norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective and feasibility degradation are bounded by \(\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}\delta\) and \(\|\mathcal A\|_{*\to\|\cdot\|}\delta\).

notation.meaning: operator norm from nuclear norm to the chosen constraint-residual norm

review_flags: The deterministic inequalities are standard, but no supplied source locator supports this transfer statement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic norm-transfer inequalities are coherent and the property kind fits, but every source reference is absent, so the nontrivial transfer statement lacks required evidence.

children.title: Sketch Storage-Accuracy Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Organization of sketch size, target rank, and reconstruction quality.

children.title: Sketch Storage Budgets
children.top_down_role: Memory budgets determined by sketch dimensions and retained state.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch Storage Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory cost of maintaining a dense range sketch and compressed SDP residual state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ambient matrix dimension \(n\), sketch width \(k\), and \(m\) affine constraints, store \(\Omega,Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), the constraint image \(z\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(O(k^2)\) reconstruction workspace. The storage is \[O(nk+m+k^2)\] real numbers, or \(O(nk+m)\) when \(k\leq n\). If \(\Omega\) is generated reproducibly from a seed or structured transform, its explicit \(nk\) entries need not be stored, while the \(nk\)-entry sketch \(Y\) remains necessary for dense low-rank output recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense k-column primal sketch uses linear-in-n memory, plus constraint residuals and small reconstruction workspace, instead of quadratic matrix storage.
assumptions_latex: The maintained primal sketch has dimensions \(n\times k\).
The constraint image has dimension \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The storage requirement is \(O(nk+m+k^2)\) real numbers.
review_flags: A Sketchy SDP source is needed to confirm which auxiliary arrays are included in the advertised storage bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the storage-budget leaf, but a method-specific source is needed to verify which sketches and auxiliary arrays are included in the advertised bound.

children.title: Sketch Approximation Quality
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction quality associated with compressed SDP representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch Approximation Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-tail control of randomized PSD reconstruction error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the eigenvalues of \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) satisfy \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\), and let \(\widehat X_r\) be a rank-\(r\) reconstruction from a randomized sketch of width \(k>r+1\). A valid trace-norm guarantee has the form \[\mathbb E\|X-\widehat X_r\|_*\leq c_{r,k}\sum_{j>r}\lambda_j(X),\] where \(c_{r,k}\geq1\) depends on the sketch and reconstruction rule and decreases toward \(1\) as oversampling grows. Thus sketching error is small precisely when the spectral mass beyond rank \(r\) is small and the oversampling is adequate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected reconstruction error is controlled by the eigenvalue mass beyond the target rank, multiplied by a sketch-dependent oversampling factor.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
The sketch distribution and reconstruction rule admit a finite factor \(c_{r,k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\|X-\widehat X_r\|_*\leq c_{r,k}\sum_{j>r}\lambda_j(X)\).

notation.meaning: approximation factor determined by target rank, sketch width, and reconstruction rule

review_flags: A source is required to instantiate the approximation factor for the intended sketch and reconstruction map.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but the bound assumes without specifying a sketch theorem that a finite factor c_{r,k} exists. A source and an instantiated reconstruction rule are needed for a substantive claim.

children.title: Sketch-Size Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relationships among sketch size, target rank, storage, and reconstruction quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Size Tradeoff Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oversampling regimes linking sketch width, memory, and relative trace-norm accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Gaussian Nyström factor \(c_{r,k}=1+r/(k-r-1)\), achieving \(c_{r,k}\leq1+\varepsilon\) requires \[k\geq r+1+\frac{r}{\varepsilon}.\] Hence constant-factor approximation uses \(k=\Theta(r)\) and \(O(nr+m)\) storage, whereas a \((1+\varepsilon)\)-factor bound uses \(k=\Theta(r/\varepsilon)\) and \(O(nr/\varepsilon+m)\) storage. These regimes concern reconstruction relative to the best rank-\(r\) spectral tail and do not by themselves bound the outer optimization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant-factor recovery needs sketch width proportional to rank; near-best relative recovery increases width and memory by approximately a factor of one over epsilon.
assumptions_latex: The applicable reconstruction factor is \(c_{r,k}=1+r/(k-r-1)\).
\(0<\varepsilon\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k=\Theta(r)\) gives constant-factor recovery, while \(k=\Theta(r/\varepsilon)\) gives factor \(1+\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: allowed excess over the best rank-r tail factor

review_flags: The stated regimes depend on an exact Gaussian Nyström constant that requires source verification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the tradeoff-regime leaf, and the algebra follows from the stated factor, but that exact Gaussian Nyström factor is unsupported and controls every claimed regime.

children.title: SketchyCGAL Residual Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Optimization-residual and storage guarantees for the sketched projection-free architecture.

children.title: SketchyCGAL Optimization Residuals
children.top_down_role: Objective and feasibility behavior inherited from the outer CGAL process.

knowledge_statements.title: SketchyCGAL Optimization Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual preservation for the implicit CGAL iterate and additive degradation after reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose SketchyCGAL updates \(z_t=\mathcal AX_t\) and \(c_t=\langle C,X_t\rangle\) exactly alongside the sketch of the same implicit CGAL iterate \(X_t\). Then its reported feasibility residual \(\|z_t-b\|\) and objective value \(c_t\) are identical to those of unsketched CGAL. If the terminal reconstruction satisfies \(\|\widehat X_t-X_t\|_*\leq\delta_t\), then \[\|\mathcal A\widehat X_t-b\|\leq\|z_t-b\|+\|\mathcal A\|_{*\to\|\cdot\|}\delta_t\] and \[|\langle C,\widehat X_t\rangle-c_t|\leq\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}\delta_t.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sketch maintenance leaves the outer CGAL residuals unchanged; reconstruction adds errors proportional to its nuclear-norm discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: The compressed state is updated from exactly the same rank-one atoms and step sizes as CGAL.
\(\|\widehat X_t-X_t\|_*\leq\delta_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Implicit residuals equal CGAL residuals, and reconstructed residuals incur only the displayed additive terms.

notation.meaning: maintained affine image of the implicit iterate

review_flags: The transfer statement is deterministic; a primary source is still needed for the claimed SketchyCGAL state invariant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the residual-guarantee container. The additive norm bounds are coherent, but the asserted identity with unsketched CGAL depends on an undocumented SketchyCGAL state invariant.

children.title: SketchyCGAL Storage-Optimality Regime
children.top_down_role: Memory scaling tied to target output rank rather than full matrix size.

knowledge_statements.title: SketchyCGAL Storage-Optimality Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-scaled memory regime matching the size of a dense low-rank PSD output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose sketch width \(k=\Theta(r)\) for a target rank-\(r\) output and maintain the affine image in \(\mathbb R^m\). SketchyCGAL then uses \[O(nr+m)\] real numbers, excluding storage required by problem data and operator implementations. A dense factor representation \(UU^\top\) of a generic rank-\(r\) PSD matrix requires \(nr\) scalar entries up to lower-order invariances. Therefore, when \(m=O(nr)\), the algorithmic state is output-size optimal up to constant factors among methods returning an explicit dense rank-\(r\) factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With sketch width proportional to output rank, SketchyCGAL uses memory comparable to storing the requested low-rank factor itself.
assumptions_latex: \(k=\Theta(r)\).
The output is an explicit dense factor in \(\mathbb R^{n\times r}\).
Problem data and operator storage are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Storage is \(O(nr+m)\), and is \(\Theta(nr)\) when \(m=O(nr)\).

notation.meaning: dense factor of the recovered PSD matrix

review_flags: The lower-bound interpretation and SketchyCGAL accounting require a method-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits, but the SketchyCGAL memory accounting and the output-size optimality interpretation require a method-specific source and a precise lower-bound model.

children.title: Sketching Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rank mismatch, spectral-tail, and probabilistic reliability boundaries.

children.title: Sketch-Rank Underestimation
children.top_down_role: Loss of reconstruction quality when retained rank is too small.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Rank Underestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irreducible error caused by choosing a reconstruction rank below the significant PSD rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ldots,1,0,\ldots,0)\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have \(r+1\) unit eigenvalues. Every matrix \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^n\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)\leq r\) satisfies \[\|X-Z\|_*\geq1\qquad\text{and}\qquad\|X-Z\|_F\geq1.\] Thus no sketch or reconstruction algorithm constrained to rank \(r\) can recover \(X\) with error below one in either norm. More generally, the best possible rank-\(r\) nuclear-norm error is \(\sum_{j>r}\lambda_j(X)\), so insufficient target rank creates deterministic bias independent of sketch width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the target rank omits a significant eigenvalue, every rank-constrained reconstruction has unavoidable error, regardless of sketch randomness or optimization accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The reconstructed output is positive semidefinite with rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the displayed family, \(\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(Z)\leq r,\,Z\succeq0}\|X-Z\|_*=1\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers this low-rank approximation failure boundary.

children.title: Slow Spectral-Decay Regime
children.top_down_role: Weak low-rank compressibility and persistent reconstruction error.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow Spectral-Decay Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail-eigenvalue obstruction for rank-limited reconstruction of a positive semidefinite iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\), and let \(1\leq r<n\). Every positive semidefinite reconstruction \(\widehat X\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq r\) satisfies \[\|X-\widehat X\|_F\geq\left(\sum_{j=r+1}^n\lambda_j^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad \|X-\widehat X\|_2\geq\lambda_{r+1}.\] Consequently, if the spectral tail remains above a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon\), no rank-\(r\) sketch reconstruction can attain error at most \(\varepsilon\), irrespective of the embedding quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slow eigenvalue decay leaves a nonnegligible spectral tail, imposing unavoidable Frobenius- and operator-norm errors on every rank-limited sketch reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X-\widehat X\|_F\geq(\sum_{j>r}\lambda_j^2)^{1/2}\) and \(\|X-\widehat X\|_2\geq\lambda_{r+1}\) for every rank-\(r\) reconstruction \(\widehat X\).

notation.meaning: Eigenvalues of the target matrix in nonincreasing order.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-limited error bounds are mathematically standard and fit the failure-boundary container, but no inspectable source and locator are supplied for the Eckart–Young-type claim or its sketching interpretation.

children.title: Probabilistic Sketch Failure
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits associated with randomized embeddings and finite oversampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Sketch Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of deterministic accuracy guarantees for finite Gaussian sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\operatorname{diag}(I_r,\eta I_{n-r})\) with \(0<\eta<1\), and draw a Gaussian sketch \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times(r+p)}\) with finite oversampling \(p\). Partition \(\Omega=(\Omega_1^{\mathsf T},\Omega_2^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) conformably with \(X\). For every \(M>0\), the event \(\{\|\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_2>M\}\) has positive probability. On such events the sampled range \(\operatorname{range}(X\Omega)\) can poorly resolve the dominant eigenspace. Thus finite oversampling yields only probabilistic, not deterministic, reconstruction guarantees; independent repetition reduces but does not eliminate the failure probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite Gaussian sketch can be arbitrarily ill-conditioned with positive probability, so oversampling provides high-probability rather than deterministic reconstruction accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\operatorname{diag}(I_r,\eta I_{n-r})\) with \(0<\eta<1\).
\(\Omega\) is Gaussian with finite oversampling \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{\|\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_2>M\}>0\) for every finite \(M>0\).

notation.meaning: Sketch blocks corresponding to dominant and trailing eigenspaces.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon and content kind fit the node, but the unbounded-tail probability claim for the Gaussian block expression and the statement about repeated sketches require an authoritative randomized-linear-algebra source with a precise locator.

children.title: Randomized Spectral Computation
children.top_down_role: Randomized eigenspace computation used within large-scale SDP algorithms.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Spectral Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized subspace iteration for approximate leading eigenpairs of a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), target rank \(r\), oversampling \(p\geq2\), and power count \(q\geq0\). Draw \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times(r+p)}\) with independent standard Gaussian entries, form \(Y=X^{2q+1}\Omega\) using repeated matrix products with intermediate orthonormalization, and compute \(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\). Form \(B=Q^{\mathsf T}XQ\), compute \(B=U\Theta U^{\mathsf T}\), and return the leading \(r\) Ritz pairs \((\theta_i,Qu_i)\). Stop after the prescribed \(q\), or when the estimated residuals \(\|XQu_i-\theta_iQu_i\|_2\) meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian test matrix and optional power iterations identify a subspace in which a small eigenproblem yields approximate leading eigenpairs.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(r+p\leq n\), \(p\geq2\), and \(q\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output consists of \(r\) Ritz eigenpairs extracted from \(\operatorname{range}(X^{2q+1}\Omega)\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the randomized trial subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately an algorithm for randomized spectral computation, but no source supports the precise power-iteration exponent, stabilization procedure, oversampling condition, or stopping rule.

children.title: Randomized Low-Rank Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Randomized recovery of low-rank primal approximations from compressed state.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Low-Rank Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nyström reconstruction of a positive semidefinite matrix from a randomized range sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), target rank \(r\), and sketch size \(k\geq r\). Draw \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), form \(Y=XS\) and \(G=S^{\mathsf T}Y\), and define the Nyström reconstruction \(\widetilde X=YG^\dagger Y^{\mathsf T}\). Compute an eigenvalue decomposition of \(\widetilde X\), retain its \(r\) largest nonnegative eigenvalues, and output \(\widehat X=[\widetilde X]_r\). Then \(\widehat X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq r\), and the procedure requires only the sketch \(Y\), the small matrix \(G\), and matrix operations of width \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized Nyström sketch produces a positive semidefinite approximation, whose leading eigenspace gives the requested rank-limited reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(r\leq k\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X=[XS(S^{\mathsf T}XS)^\dagger S^{\mathsf T}X]_r\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq r\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the core matrix.
Best rank-r positive semidefinite spectral truncation of Z.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Nyström reconstruction is appropriately classified as an algorithm and is internally coherent, but the formula and storage claim lack a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: PSD Completion Theorem for Chordal Graphs
children.top_down_role: Structural organization of partial PSD matrices through clique representations.

children.title: Clique-Wise PSD Completion
children.top_down_role: Completion interfaces based on maximal-clique PSD constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Wise PSD Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive semidefinite completion theorem for partial matrices whose specified graph is chordal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal, with every diagonal specified, and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be its maximal cliques. A symmetric partial matrix \(X\), specified on the diagonal and edges of \(G\), admits a completion \(\overline X\in\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\) if and only if every fully specified principal submatrix satisfies \(X[C_j,C_j]\succeq0\). The clique matrices automatically agree on intersections because they are restrictions of the same partial matrix. If every clique submatrix is positive definite, a positive definite completion exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal sparsity graph, a partial symmetric matrix has a PSD completion exactly when every maximal-clique principal submatrix is PSD.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal and contains all diagonal positions.
\(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are the maximal cliques of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) has a positive semidefinite completion if and only if \(X[C_j,C_j]\succeq0\) for every \(j\).

children.title: Nonchordal Completion Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure of direct clique-wise equivalence without chordal extension.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonchordal Completion Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four-cycle counterexample to clique-wise PSD sufficiency outside chordal graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be the chordless cycle on vertices \(1,2,3,4\). Specify \(X_{ii}=1\), \(X_{12}=X_{23}=X_{34}=1\), and \(X_{14}=-1\), leaving \(X_{13}\) and \(X_{24}\) unspecified. Every maximal-clique submatrix is a positive semidefinite \(2\times2\) correlation matrix. Nevertheless, no positive semidefinite completion exists: in any Gram representation, the three correlations equal to \(1\) force the four unit Gram vectors to coincide, whereas \(X_{14}=-1\) forces the first and fourth vectors to be negatives. Hence clique-wise PSD is not sufficient without chordality or a chordal extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a chordless four-cycle, all edge clique matrices can be PSD while mutually incompatible correlations prevent any global PSD completion.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the chordless four-cycle.
The specified diagonal and edge values are as displayed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All maximal-clique submatrices are positive semidefinite, but the partial matrix has no positive semidefinite completion.

notation.meaning: Specified or unspecified entry of the partial symmetric matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-cycle construction is a valid counterexample and the selected content kind matches the boundary node, but the record supplies no inspectable citation or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Chordal Conversion Methods

children.title: Domain-Space Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Sparse primal representations using clique-local PSD blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Space Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-local representation of a PSD-completable partial matrix over a chordal graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), and let \(E_j\) select the coordinates in \(C_j\). A partial symmetric variable \(X\) on \(G\) is positive semidefinite completable exactly when there exist matrices \(X_j\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_j|}\) satisfying \(X_j=E_jXE_j^{\mathsf T}\) for every \(j\). Equivalently, one may optimize over the local blocks \(X_j\) and impose equality of entries on every clique intersection. With a clique tree, enforcing consistency only on adjacent clique intersections is sufficient for global consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal PSD-completable variable can be replaced by PSD clique blocks coupled by equality constraints on clique overlaps.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).
\(E_j\) selects the coordinates of \(C_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) is PSD-completable if and only if \(X_j=E_jXE_j^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) for all \(j\), with consistent overlap entries.

children.title: Range-Space Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Dual or aggregate-sparsity representations using clique-supported components.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-supported sum representation of a sparse positive semidefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), and let \(E_j\) select \(C_j\). Every matrix \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\) whose off-diagonal support is contained in \(E\) admits a decomposition \[Z=\sum_{j=1}^m E_j^{\mathsf T}Z_jE_j,\qquad Z_j\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_j|}.\] Conversely, every such sum is positive semidefinite and has support contained in the union of the clique edges. Thus a sparse PSD slack or aggregate coefficient can be represented by clique-supported PSD components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD matrix with chordal sparsity is exactly a sum of PSD matrices embedded on the maximal cliques.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).
The off-diagonal support of \(Z\) is contained in \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\) with chordal sparsity if and only if \(Z=\sum_jE_j^{\mathsf T}Z_jE_j\) for some \(Z_j\succeq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-supported sum representation is mathematically appropriate for the range-space decomposition container, but its equivalence requires a chordal sparse-PSD decomposition source with a precise theorem or section locator.

children.title: Clique-Consensus Formulations
children.top_down_role: Decomposed models with consistency coupling across clique intersections.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Consensus Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-tree consensus constraints for decomposed chordal semidefinite programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be the maximal cliques of a chordal graph and let \(T\) be a clique tree. Introduce \(X_j\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_j|}\) for each clique. For every tree edge \((i,j)\), let \(S_{ij}=C_i\cap C_j\) and impose \[X_i[S_{ij},S_{ij}]=X_j[S_{ij},S_{ij}].\] By the running-intersection property, these edge-wise equalities imply agreement of all copies of every shared entry. Consequently the local matrices define one globally consistent partial matrix, and any globally consistent collection satisfies these constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD clique variables represent one global partial matrix when adjacent cliques in a clique tree agree on their separators.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree satisfying the running-intersection property.
\(X_j\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_j|}\) for every maximal clique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tree-edge separator equalities are necessary and sufficient for global consistency of the clique-local entries.

notation.meaning: Separator C_i intersect C_j on a clique-tree edge.
Clique tree of the chordal graph.

children.title: Fill-Reducing Chordal Extensions

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Reducing Chordal Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination-order construction of a chordal extension with heuristic fill control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an undirected sparsity graph \(G=(V,E)\). Repeatedly select an uneliminated vertex \(v\), add edges making its current uneliminated neighborhood a clique, record \(v\), and eliminate it. A fill-reducing rule chooses \(v\) to minimize a surrogate such as the number of missing neighbor pairs or the resulting clique size. The original edges together with all added fill edges form a chordal graph \(G^+=(V,E\cup F)\), and the recorded order is a perfect elimination order for \(G^+\). Output \(G^+\), \(F\), and its maximal cliques; heuristic selection does not guarantee minimum fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-degree or minimum-fill elimination heuristic adds edges locally, producing a chordal extension while attempting to limit fill and clique sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elimination process returns a chordal extension \(G^+=(V,E\cup F)\) and a perfect elimination order for \(G^+\).

notation.meaning: Set of fill edges introduced during elimination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elimination procedure is appropriately classified as an algorithm and correctly distinguishes heuristic fill control from minimum fill, but the chordality and perfect-elimination-order claims require an inspectable graph-algorithm source.

children.title: Clique-Merging Strategies
children.top_down_role: Aggregation balancing linking constraints against cone costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Merging Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy aggregation of adjacent clique blocks using a cone-versus-consensus cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a clique tree \(T\) with clique sizes \(a=|C_i|\), \(b=|C_j|\) and separator size \(s=|C_i\cap C_j|\) on each edge. Assign each edge a merge score comparing the enlarged-cone cost, for example \((a+b-s)^3-a^3-b^3\), with the savings from removing \(s(s+1)/2\) scalar consensus equations. Repeatedly merge an adjacent pair whose chosen total score is negative, replace it by \(C_i\cup C_j\), update neighboring separators and scores, and stop when no admissible improving merge remains. Output the aggregated clique tree and its revised consensus constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy clique merging trades larger PSD cones against fewer separator equalities and stops when the selected cost model predicts no improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree.
A fixed computable cost model combines cone and consensus costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an aggregated clique cover for which no remaining adjacent merge improves the chosen local cost score.

notation.meaning: Size of the separator between two adjacent cliques.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the clique-merging container, but the proposed cubic cone-cost model, consensus savings, admissibility conditions, and update rule are method-specific and unsupported by any source.

children.title: Chordal Interior-Point Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Interior-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual interior-point iteration on clique PSD blocks and separator-consensus equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a chordally decomposed SDP with clique variables \(X_j\succ0\), dual slacks \(Z_j\succ0\), affine constraints, and separator-consensus equations, initialize a strictly feasible or embedded primal-dual point. At each iteration form the perturbed complementarity equations with parameter \(\mu>0\), linearize all primal, dual, consensus, and clique complementarity conditions, and solve the resulting sparse Newton system using the clique-tree structure. Choose primal and dual step lengths preserving \(X_j\succ0\) and \(Z_j\succ0\), update the iterates, decrease \(\mu\), and stop when primal residual, dual residual, and normalized duality gap meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal interior-point method applies primal-dual Newton steps to local PSD blocks while retaining separator coupling and sparse clique-tree linear algebra.
assumptions_latex: The SDP has a chordal clique decomposition with consistent separator constraints.
A strictly interior start or a homogeneous embedding is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns when the prescribed primal residual, dual residual, and duality-gap tolerances are satisfied.

notation.meaning: Primal clique block and corresponding dual slack.

children.title: Chordal Operator-Splitting Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Operator-Splitting Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM on clique-local PSD variables with separator-consistency constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a clique tree with clique variables \(X_k\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}\), let \(E_{ke}X_kE_{ke}^{\mathsf T}=Z_e\) enforce agreement on every separator incident to clique \(k\). Initialize \(X_k^0\succeq0\), \(Z_e^0\), and scaled multipliers \(U_{ke}^0\). At iteration \(t\), independently update each \(X_k\) by minimizing its local objective plus \(\frac{\rho}{2}\sum_{e\sim k}\|E_{ke}X_kE_{ke}^{\mathsf T}-Z_e^t+U_{ke}^t\|_F^2\) over \(\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}\). Update each \(Z_e\) by averaging its two incident shifted separator matrices, then set \(U_{ke}^{t+1}=U_{ke}^t+E_{ke}X_k^{t+1}E_{ke}^{\mathsf T}-Z_e^{t+1}\). Stop when primal and dual residual norms are below prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM alternates parallel clique-local PSD minimizations, separator averaging, and multiplier updates until clique overlaps agree to the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The converted objective is closed, proper, and convex.
The clique-consistency formulation has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output consists of PSD clique matrices whose separator inconsistencies satisfy the prescribed residual tolerance.

children.title: Chordal-Conversion Pathologies

children.title: Clique-Overlap Inflation
children.top_down_role: Growth in linking constraints from extensive clique intersections.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Overlap Inflation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts scalar linking equations introduced by clique-tree conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) be maximal cliques arranged as a clique tree \(T\). For each edge \(e=(i,j)\), write \(S_e=C_i\cap C_j\) and \(s_e=|S_e|\). Equality of the two symmetric principal submatrices on \(S_e\) imposes \(s_e(s_e+1)/2\) scalar equations. Hence the unreduced clique-tree conversion contains
\[L=\sum_{e\in E(T)}\frac{s_e(s_e+1)}{2}\]
scalar overlap equations. In particular, if \(s_e\ge s\) on \(r\) tree edges, then \(L\ge r s(s+1)/2\); large or repeated separators can therefore dominate the converted constraint system even when individual PSD blocks are moderate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator of size s creates s(s+1)/2 scalar consistency equations, so numerous large clique intersections can dominate the converted SDP.
assumptions_latex: The conversion equates one symmetric separator matrix on every clique-tree edge.

notation.meaning: separator associated with tree edge e

children.title: Conversion-Induced Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Loss of regularity caused by redundant consistency structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Conversion-Induced Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-rank failure caused by redundant separator-consistency equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal B\) map the tuple of clique matrices to all signed differences of duplicated separator entries, so consistency is \(\mathcal B(X)=0\). If the conversion contains redundant linking equations, then there exists \(0\ne y\) with \(\mathcal B^*y=0\). Consequently the equality-constraint Jacobian lacks full row rank. For any symmetric primal Hessian or scaling operator \(H\), the equality-constrained Newton matrix
\[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&\mathcal B^*\\ \mathcal B&0\end{pmatrix}\]
satisfies \(K(0,y)=(0,0)\) and is singular. Thus an equivalent chordal conversion can lose standard linear-independence regularity solely through its redundant consistency representation, even when the unconverted SDP does not exhibit that row-rank defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant overlap equations give a nonzero null multiplier, violate constraint independence, and make the corresponding equality-constrained Newton system singular.
assumptions_latex: \(\ker(\mathcal B^*)\ne\{0\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The converted equality Jacobian is row-rank deficient and \(K\) is singular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind and the conditional linear-algebra statement fit the node: a nonzero element of the kernel of the adjoint consistency operator causes row-rank failure and singularity of the displayed saddle-point matrix. No citation is supplied for the chordal-conversion interpretation, so the record requires a specific source.

children.title: Large-Treewidth Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Treewidth Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense local PSD work persists when chordal extensions have large treewidth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be the aggregate sparsity graph and let \(\widehat G\) be a chordal extension with largest maximal-clique size \(\omega\). Its width is \(\tau=\omega-1\). A method that explicitly projects each clique block onto \(\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}\) requires, under dense eigendecomposition arithmetic, \(O(|C_k|^3)\) work and \(O(|C_k|^2)\) storage for that block. Hence one iteration contains a largest-block cost of \(O(\omega^3)\) and storage of \(O(\omega^2)\). If every usable chordal extension has \(\omega=\Theta(n)\), clique decomposition does not reduce the asymptotic cubic cost or quadratic storage of the largest PSD operation relative to an order-\(n\) dense cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When treewidth is proportional to matrix order, the largest clique remains dense-scale, eliminating asymptotic savings in PSD projection and storage.
assumptions_latex: Clique projections use dense eigendecomposition.
\(n\) is the order of the original PSD matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\omega=\Theta(n)\), the largest local PSD operation costs \(O(n^3)\) work and \(O(n^2)\) storage.

children.title: Group-Invariant SDP Reduction
children.top_down_role: Restriction to symmetry-invariant matrix subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Group-Invariant SDP Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaging theorem for finite or compact orthogonal symmetry groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(\langle C,X\rangle\) over a convex feasible set \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb S^n\). Let a finite or compact group \(\Gamma\) act by \(X\mapsto Q_gXQ_g^{\mathsf T}\), where every \(Q_g\) is orthogonal. Suppose \(Q_g\mathcal FQ_g^{\mathsf T}=\mathcal F\) and \(Q_g^{\mathsf T}CQ_g=C\) for every \(g\in\Gamma\). For any feasible \(X\), its Haar average \(\bar X=\int_\Gamma Q_gXQ_g^{\mathsf T}\,d\mu(g)\) is feasible, satisfies \(Q_g\bar XQ_g^{\mathsf T}=\bar X\), and has \(\langle C,\bar X\rangle=\langle C,X\rangle\). Therefore the infimum is unchanged by restricting the SDP to the group-fixed matrix subspace; if an optimum is attained, an invariant optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging any feasible matrix over an objective-preserving compact symmetry group yields an invariant feasible matrix with the same objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is finite or compact and acts orthogonally.
The feasible set is convex and invariant under the action.
The objective matrix is invariant under the action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{X\in\mathcal F}\langle C,X\rangle=\inf_{X\in\mathcal F,\;Q_gXQ_g^{\mathsf T}=X\;\forall g}\langle C,X\rangle\).

children.title: Matrix-Algebra Block Diagonalization
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of invariant matrix algebras into smaller PSD blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Algebra Block Diagonalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wedderburn block representation of a symmetry-fixed real matrix algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a finite-dimensional real unital algebra closed under transpose, such as the commutant of an orthogonal group representation. There is an orthogonal change of basis and a real star-algebra isomorphism under which
\[\mathcal A\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^r I_{m_j}\otimes\mathbb F_j^{d_j\times d_j},\qquad \mathbb F_j\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C,\mathbb H\}.\]
For every self-adjoint \(X\in\mathcal A\), let \(X_j\) denote its self-adjoint component in the \(j\)-th simple factor. Then \(X\succeq0\) if and only if \(X_j\succeq0\) for all \(j\). Thus an invariant PSD constraint is representable by independent smaller real, complex, or quaternionic Hermitian PSD blocks, with multiplicities \(m_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetry-fixed matrix algebra decomposes into simple blocks, and positivity of an invariant matrix is equivalent to positivity of every smaller block.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is finite-dimensional, real, unital, and transpose-closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For self-adjoint \(X\in\mathcal A\), \(X\succeq0\iff X_j\succeq0\) for every simple factor \(j\).

notation.meaning: real division algebra of the j-th simple factor
self-adjoint block representing X in factor j

children.title: Multiple-PSD-Block Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-PSD-Block Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise proximal-gradient iteration on a product of PSD cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(X_1,\ldots,X_p)=f(X_1,\ldots,X_p)+\sum_{j=1}^p\delta_{\mathbb S_+^{n_j}}(X_j)\), where \(f\) is differentiable and convex, choose \(0<\alpha\le1/L\) for a Lipschitz constant \(L\) of \(\nabla f\). Initialize each \(X_j^0\succeq0\) and update in parallel by
\[X_j^{t+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^{n_j}}\!\left(X_j^t-\alpha\nabla_j f(X_1^t,\ldots,X_p^t)\right),\qquad j=1,\ldots,p.\]
Stop when the product-space fixed-point residual \(\big(\sum_j\|X_j^{t+1}-X_j^t\|_F^2\big)^{1/2}/\alpha\) is at most the requested tolerance. The method preserves the native cone product and requires eigendecompositions only of the individual blocks, not of one aggregated PSD matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected-gradient updates each native PSD block separately and stops when the product-space fixed-point residual is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
The product-cone problem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate satisfies \(X_j^t\succeq0\), and the returned iterate has the prescribed fixed-point residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorized formulas for SDP constraint and adjoint operators.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 Special Cases and Structure Exploitation p. 86
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_i=U_iD_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\), where \(U_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_i}\), \(D_i\in\mathbb S^{r_i}\), and \(r_i\ll n\). Define \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) by \(\mathcal A(X)_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\), and let \(\mathcal A^*\) be its adjoint. Then, for every \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[\mathcal A(X)_i=\operatorname{tr}(D_iU_i^{\mathsf T}XU_i),\qquad \mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m U_i(y_iD_i)U_i^{\mathsf T}.\]
Thus an implementation may store the factors \(U_i,D_i\), evaluate each constraint through the compressed matrix \(U_i^{\mathsf T}XU_i\), and apply the adjoint as a sum of matrices of rank at most \(r_i\), without forming or storing dense coefficient matrices \(A_i\). For dense \(X\), forming \(XU_i\) by dense arithmetic costs \(O(n^2r_i)\); this factorization is a storage and structured-operator representation and does not by itself imply lower arithmetic cost than a direct dense inner product with an already stored \(A_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank factors give exact compressed formulas for the SDP constraint operator and its adjoint and avoid storing dense coefficient matrices; the factors alone do not guarantee a cheaper dense constraint evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Plus-Low-Rank SDP Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint clique-local and low-rank representation of SDP data operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose each coefficient matrix has a decomposition \(A_i=S_i+U_iD_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\), where the sparse matrices \(S_i\) share a chordal extension with maximal cliques \(C_k\), and \(U_iD_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\) has rank \(r_i\ll n\). \[\langle A_i,X\rangle=\sum_k\langle S_{ik},X_k\rangle+\operatorname{tr}(D_iU_i^{\mathsf T}XU_i),\]
provided the clique-supported pieces satisfy \(S_i=\sum_kE_k^{\mathsf T}S_{ik}E_k\). The sparse contribution is therefore evaluated clique-locally, while the dense structured contribution uses low-rank products. This representation combines chordal PSD blocks and factorized data without expanding the low-rank term into a dense coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse coefficient contributions can be evaluated on chordal clique blocks while dense low-rank contributions remain in factorized form.

children.title: Packing SDP Methods
children.top_down_role: Specialized algorithms for positive semidefinite packing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Packing SDP Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-exponential multiplicative update for positive packing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the packing problem \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:\sum_i x_iA_i\preceq I,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(A_i\succeq0\) and \(c_i>0\), choose \(\eta>0\). Initialize \(x^0=0\) and \(L^0=0\). At iteration \(t\), set \(W^t=\exp(\eta L^t)\), choose \(i_t\in\arg\min_i\langle W^t,A_i\rangle/c_i\), select \(\delta_t>0\) satisfying \(\eta\delta_t\|A_{i_t}\|_2\le1\), and update \(x_{i_t}^{t+1}=x_{i_t}^t+\delta_t\) and \(L^{t+1}=L^t+\delta_tA_{i_t}\). Stop when \(\lambda_{\max}(L^{t+1})\ge1\), and output \(\widehat x=x^{t+1}/\lambda_{\max}(L^{t+1})\), which is packing-feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-exponential weight penalizes loaded eigendirections while coordinate updates increase the most favorable positive packing variable; final scaling ensures feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\succeq0\), \(A_i\ne0\), and \(c_i>0\) for every \(i\).
A step satisfying \(\eta\delta_t\|A_{i_t}\|_2\le1\) is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned vector satisfies \(\widehat x\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\widehat x_iA_i\preceq I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the packing-method leaf, and scaling by the maximum eigenvalue gives feasibility whenever the stopping point is reached. However, no source supports this particular coordinate-selection and step-size scheme, and the stated upper bound on the step size does not ensure termination. A source is required before the algorithmic prescription can be relied upon.

children.title: Covering SDP Methods
children.top_down_role: Specialized algorithms for positive semidefinite covering structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Covering SDP Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-exponential multiplicative update for positive covering constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the covering problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq I,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(A_i\succeq0\) and \(c_i>0\), choose \(\eta>0\). Initialize \(x^0=0\) and \(L^0=0\). At iteration \(t\), set \(W^t=\exp(-\eta L^t)\), choose \(i_t\in\arg\max_i\langle W^t,A_i\rangle/c_i\), select \(\delta_t>0\) satisfying \(\eta\delta_t\|A_{i_t}\|_2\le1\), and update \(x_{i_t}^{t+1}=x_{i_t}^t+\delta_t\) and \(L^{t+1}=L^t+\delta_tA_{i_t}\). Stop and output \(x^{t+1}\) when \(\lambda_{\min}(L^{t+1})\ge1\); otherwise report failure after a prescribed iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decreasing matrix-exponential weight emphasizes insufficiently covered eigendirections, guiding positive coordinate increments until the covering matrix dominates the identity.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\succeq0\) and \(c_i>0\) for every \(i\).
There exists \(x\ge0\) with \(\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the stopping test holds, the output satisfies \(x\ge0\) and \(\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the covering-method leaf, and the stopping test conditionally certifies covering feasibility. No source is supplied for the matrix-exponential coordinate rule, termination behavior, or any relationship between the selected steps and the objective. The conditional feasibility observation alone does not validate the proposed method.

children.title: Mixed Packing-Covering SDP
children.top_down_role: Algorithms for coupled positive packing and covering constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Packing-Covering SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected smooth-potential method for coupled positive matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P(x)=\sum_i x_iP_i\) and \(C(x)=\sum_i x_iC_i\), where \(P_i,C_i\succeq0\), and seek \(x\in[0,R]^m\) with \(P(x)\preceq I\) and \(C(x)\succeq I\). For \(\eta>0\), define
\[\Phi_\eta(x)=\eta^{-1}\log\operatorname{tr}\exp(\eta(P(x)-I))+\eta^{-1}\log\operatorname{tr}\exp(\eta(I-C(x))).\]
Initialize \(x^0\in[0,R]^m\) and update \(x^{t+1}=\Pi_{[0,R]^m}(x^t-\alpha_t\nabla\Phi_\eta(x^t))\). Stop when \(\lambda_{\max}(P(x^t))\le1+\varepsilon\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(C(x^t))\ge1-\varepsilon\). If an iteration limit is reached, return the iterate with smallest potential and report that the feasibility test was unmet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected gradient minimizes smooth spectral penalties for packing overload and covering deficit, stopping only when both matrix inequalities meet tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i,C_i\succeq0\) for every \(i\).
The search region \([0,R]^m\) is prescribed and nonempty.
\(\alpha_t>0\) is chosen by a valid smooth convex descent rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output satisfies \(P(x)\preceq(1+\varepsilon)I\) and \(C(x)\succeq(1-\varepsilon)I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the mixed packing-covering leaf, and the successful stopping test matches the stated approximate matrix inequalities. No source supports this particular summed log-trace-exponential potential as a mixed positive-SDP algorithm, and the phrase 'valid smooth convex descent rule' does not specify conditions ensuring that projected descent reaches the feasibility test. A specific algorithmic source is required.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Preprocessing

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Preprocessing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial reduction for a feasible equality-form SDP lacking strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\), initialize \(U_0=I_n\). At step \(k\), find a nonzero exposing matrix \(W_k\succeq0\) satisfying \(\langle W_k,X\rangle=0\) for every \(X\in F\cap U_k\mathbb S_+^{r_k}U_k^T\). Let the columns of \(V_k\) span \(\ker(U_k^TW_kU_k)\), and set \(U_{k+1}=U_kV_k\). Stop when the reduced system \(\mathcal A(U_kZU_k^T)=b\), \(Z\succeq0\), has a solution \(Z\succ0\), or when an exposing certificate establishes infeasibility. Output the reduced SDP in \(Z\); its cone is the minimal face containing \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly intersect the PSD cone with exposed faces containing the feasible set, then parameterize the resulting minimal face until relative strict feasibility or infeasibility is certified.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
\(F\) is nonempty unless an infeasibility certificate is returned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{U_kZU_k^T:Z\succeq0,\ \mathcal A(U_kZU_k^T)=b\}\) on the identified minimal face.

notation.meaning: cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Redundancy Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy criterion for equality constraints in standard-form SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider constraints \(\langle A_i,Xangle=b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Constraint \(j\) is algebraically redundant whenever coefficients \(\lambda_i\), \(i
e j\), satisfy \(A_j=\sum_{i
e j}\lambda_iA_i\) and \(b_j=\sum_{i
e j}\lambda_ib_i\). In that case every matrix satisfying the remaining equalities automatically satisfies equality \(j\). Removing this constraint preserves the affine constraint set and therefore preserves the feasible set, optimal value, and primal optimizers of any SDP using the same objective and cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality constraint may be deleted when both its matrix and right-hand side are the same linear combination of the remaining constraint data.

children.title: Constraint-Rank Reduction

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Rank Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-row-rank representation of a consistent SDP equality operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have rank \(r\). Choose a surjective operator \(\mathcal B:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^r\) whose coordinate functionals form a basis of the row space of \(\mathcal A\). Then there is a full-column-rank matrix \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) such that \(\mathcal A=T\mathcal B\). If \(b\in\operatorname{range}(T)\), the vector \(c\) satisfying \(Tc=b\) is unique, and \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal B(X)=c\). Thus the equality system can be reduced from \(m\) coordinates to \(r\) independent coordinates without changing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the equality operator through a basis of its row space; consistency then yields an equivalent full-row-rank system with fewer constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear with rank \(r\).
\(b\in\operatorname{range}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(X)=b\iff\mathcal B(X)=c\), where \(Tc=b\).

notation.meaning: rank of the original constraint operator

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Coordinate Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate reduction after identifying a proper face of the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every feasible primal matrix lies in the face \(\{UZU^T:Z\in\mathbb S_+^r\}\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has orthonormal columns. For the SDP \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ X\succeq0\}\), substitute \(X=UZU^T\) and define \(C'=U^TCU\) and \(A_i'=U^TA_iU\). The compressed problem is \(\min\{\langle C',Z\rangle:\langle A_i',Z\rangle=b_i,\ Z\succeq0\}\). The substitution is a bijection between its feasible set and the original feasible set, and it preserves objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent matrices in a known PSD face using a smaller symmetric variable; projected data define an equivalent lower-dimensional SDP.
assumptions_latex: Every original feasible matrix belongs to \(U\mathbb S_+^rU^T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=UZU^T\) gives a value-preserving bijection between the two feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal SDP Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible congruence scaling of a primal equality-form SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an invertible \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), substitute \(X=DZD^T\) into \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ X\succeq0\}\). Define \(C_D=D^TCD\) and \(A_{i,D}=D^TA_iD\). Because congruence by \(D\) is an automorphism of the positive-semidefinite cone, the scaled problem is \(\min\{\langle C_D,Z\rangle:\langle A_{i,D},Z\rangle=b_i,\ Z\succeq0\}\). The maps \(Z\mapsto DZD^T\) and \(X\mapsto D^{-1}XD^{-T}\) give a value-preserving bijection between feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible congruence transforms primal matrix data and variables while preserving PSD feasibility, objective values, and optimal solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible.
\(A_i,C\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=DZD^T\) yields an equivalent primal SDP with data \(A_{i,D}=D^TA_iD\) and \(C_D=D^TCD\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual SDP Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-slack transformation paired with invertible primal congruence scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual SDP \(\max\{b^Ty:C-\sum_{i=1}^my_iA_i=S,\ S\succeq0\}\), let \(D\) be invertible and define \(C_D=D^TCD\), \(A_{i,D}=D^TA_iD\), and \(S_D=D^TSD\). Then \(C_D-\sum_{i=1}^my_iA_{i,D}=S_D\succeq0\) if and only if the original dual slack equation holds with \(S\succeq0\). The multiplier \(y\) and dual objective \(b^Ty\) are unchanged, while slacks correspond bijectively through \(S_D=D^TSD\). Hence congruence scaling preserves dual feasibility and optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The congruence used to scale primal data also transforms dual slacks, leaving multipliers and dual objective values unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible.
\(A_i,C,S\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\succeq0\iff S_D=D^TSD\succeq0\), with identical feasible multipliers \(y\).

knowledge_statements.title: SDP Operator Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating diagonal equilibration of SDP constraint matrices and equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric matrices \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\), initialize positive diagonal \(D=I_n\) and positive row weights \(w_i=1\). Repeatedly form \(\widehat A_i=w_iD^TA_iD\); update each \(w_i\) so that nonzero values \(\|\widehat A_i\|_F\) approach a common target, and update the diagonal entries of \(D\) so that aggregate coordinate energies \(\sum_i\|e_j^T\widehat A_i\|_2^2\) approach a common target. Stop when prescribed norm-ratio tolerances hold or an iteration limit is reached. Output transformed data \(\widehat A_i\), \(\widehat b_i=w_ib_i\), and \(\widehat C=D^TCD\), together with inverse maps for recovering primal and dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately scale constraint rows and matrix coordinates until their norms are approximately balanced, retaining inverse transformations for solution recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i,C\in\mathbb S^n\).
Only positive, finite scaling factors are accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat A_i=w_iD^TA_iD\), \(\widehat b_i=w_ib_i\), and \(\widehat C=D^TCD\) define an equivalent scaled SDP.

children.title: Scaling-Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where scaling fails to restore adequate balance.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural limitations and numerical breakdown of invertible SDP scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Any invertible row scaling and invertible congruence scaling preserve exact linear dependencies among equality constraints, ranks of primal and dual slack matrices, the existence or failure of Slater points, and the dimension of the minimal cone face containing the feasible set. Consequently, scaling alone cannot remove algebraic redundancy, repair weak feasibility, or convert a proper-face feasible set into a full-cone strictly feasible set. Moreover, if a sequence of scaling matrices satisfies \(\kappa_2(D_k)\to\infty\), recovery through \(X=D_kZD_k^T\) or its inverse can amplify relative floating-point errors without bound. Such regimes require reduction or regularization rather than further scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible scaling cannot repair structural degeneracy, and increasingly ill-conditioned scaling can make variable recovery arbitrarily sensitive to numerical error.
assumptions_latex: All row and congruence scalings are invertible.
Numerical recovery uses finite-precision arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(D_k)\to\infty\) permits unbounded recovery sensitivity while structural degeneracies remain invariant.

children.title: SDP Regularization Strategies

knowledge_statements.title: SDP Regularization Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive diagonal regularization of semidefinite-program Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior-point iteration, let the symmetric positive-semidefinite normal-equation matrix be \(H\) and the right-hand side be \(r\). Choose \(\rho>0\), solve \((H+\rho I)\Delta y=r\), recover the associated primal and slack directions from \(\Delta y\), and accept the step only if residual reduction and cone-interiority tests pass. If factorization is unstable or the tests fail, increase \(\rho\); after successful well-conditioned steps, decrease \(\rho\) toward zero. Stop according to the original primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity gap, not merely the regularized linear-system residual. Output the unregularized SDP iterates together with the final residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilize singular or ill-conditioned Newton systems with an adaptive diagonal shift, while judging convergence using the original SDP residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_+^m\).
\(\rho>0\) at every regularized solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\rho I\succ0\), so the regularized Newton equation has a unique solution.

children.title: SDP Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Controlled perturbation settings used to improve numerical tractability.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP Perturbation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regimes defined by distance from SDP data to ill-posed instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an SDP instance by data \(d=(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m,b)\) in a fixed product norm, and let \(\Sigma\) be the set of ill-posed data lying on a boundary between distinct feasibility or boundedness statuses. Define \(\sigma(d)=\inf_{d'\in\Sigma}\|d-d'\|\). A perturbation \(\Delta d\) is subcritical when \(\|\Delta d\|<\sigma(d)\), critical when equality holds, and supercritical when \(\|\Delta d\|>\sigma(d)\). Subcritical perturbations cannot cross \(\Sigma\) along the line segment from \(d\) to \(d+\Delta d\); critical or supercritical perturbations may change qualitative problem status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify data perturbations by comparing their size with the instance's distance to the boundary of ill-posed SDP data.
assumptions_latex: The SDP data space is finite-dimensional and equipped with a fixed norm.
\(\Sigma\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\Delta d\|<\sigma(d)\) keeps the segment \(d+t\Delta d\), \(0\le t\le1\), disjoint from \(\Sigma\).

notation.meaning: distance from the instance to ill-posedness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distance-based construction is coherent once a closed ill-posed set and norm are fixed, and definition fits the perturbation-regimes container. No source defines Sigma or the relevant feasibility and boundedness status partition, so the intended mathematical regime cannot be validated.

children.title: Stability Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between numerical stability, fidelity to the original instance, and recoverable accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning improvement and direction bias under diagonal Newton regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), let \(Hx=r\), and define the regularized direction \(x_\rho=(H+\rho I)^{-1}r\) for \(\rho>0\). Then \(\kappa_2(H+\rho I)=(\lambda_{\max}(H)+\rho)/(\lambda_{\min}(H)+\rho)\le\kappa_2(H)\), while \(x_\rho-x=-\rho(H+\rho I)^{-1}x\). Consequently, \(\|x_\rho-x\|_2\le \rho(\lambda_{\min}(H)+\rho)^{-1}\|x\|_2\). Increasing \(\rho\) therefore improves spectral conditioning but enlarges the worst-case deviation from the unregularized SDP Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger diagonal shift improves the Newton system's condition number but can increase bias in the computed search direction.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\).
\(r\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(H+\rho I)\le\kappa_2(H)\) and \(\|x_\rho-x\|_2\le\frac{\rho}{\lambda_{\min}(H)+\rho}\|x\|_2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eigenvalue formula, direction identity, and norm bound are correct for symmetric positive-definite H, and property fits the stability-tradeoffs container. The record supplies no citation, so it lacks the evidence required for this nontrivial quantitative claim.

children.title: Stabilization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Instance regimes where stabilization obscures feasibility status or materially changes solution recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakly feasible SDP whose status changes under arbitrarily small perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\), consider feasibility of \(X\in\mathbb S_+^2\) subject to \(X_{11}=0\) and \(X_{12}=\varepsilon\). When \(\varepsilon=0\), every matrix \(X=\operatorname{diag}(0,t)\) with \(t\ge0\) is feasible, but no feasible matrix is positive definite. When \(\varepsilon\ne0\), positive semidefiniteness and \(X_{11}=0\) force the first row and column of \(X\) to vanish, contradicting \(X_{12}=\varepsilon\). Thus an arbitrarily small right-hand-side perturbation changes feasibility, so no uniformly status-preserving stabilization neighborhood exists at this weakly feasible instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-by-two weakly feasible SDP becomes infeasible under every nonzero perturbation of one equality, marking a sharp stability boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^2\) is constrained by \(X\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon=0\Rightarrow F_\varepsilon\ne\varnothing\), whereas \(\varepsilon\ne0\Rightarrow F_\varepsilon=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the perturbed SDP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-by-two counterexample is mathematically correct: a PSD matrix with a zero diagonal entry must have the corresponding row and column zero. The failure_boundary kind fits the exact container, but the record has no source for the example or its stability interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedded Starting Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasible-start initialization using residual offsets in a homogeneous self-dual SDP embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix integers \(m,q\geq1\) and an affine residual map \(R:\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^q\). Choose \(X_0\succ0\), \(S_0\succ0\), \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\tau_0>0\), and \(\kappa_0>0\), and set \(z_0=(X_0,y_0,S_0,\tau_0,\kappa_0)\). Define \(r_0=-R(z_0)\), so that \(R(z_0)+r_0=0\). Set \(\mu_0=(\langle X_0,S_0\rangle+\tau_0\kappa_0)/(n+1)\), and output \((z_0,r_0,\mu_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose positive-definite matrix blocks, an unrestricted multiplier, and positive embedding scalars. Negating the affine residual makes this interior point satisfy the shifted equations, and its average matrix-and-scalar complementarity defines the initial path parameter.
assumptions_latex: The embedded conic blocks are \(\mathbb S_+^n\times\mathbb R_+\) and their dual blocks.
A fixed homogeneous self-dual embedding is represented by an affine residual map \(R:\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(R(z_0)+r_0=0\), has strictly interior conic blocks, and has \(\mu_0>0\).

notation.meaning: Positive-definite primal and dual matrix variables

children.title: Embedded Central-Path Construction

assumptions_latex: The shifted embedded affine equations admit a strictly interior point.
The logarithmic barrier is used for the semidefinite and nonnegative scalar blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each admissible \(\mu>0\), the displayed equations define an embedded central-path point.

source_refs.locator: 5.5 Existence of the central path - a constructive proof p. 124

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(z)+r_0=0\) denote the shifted affine equations of the homogeneous self-dual embedding. Its logarithmic-barrier central path consists of interior points \(z(\mu)=(X(\mu),y(\mu),S(\mu),\tau(\mu),\kappa(\mu))\), indexed by \(\mu>0\), satisfying \[R(z(\mu))+r_0=0,\qquad X(\mu)S(\mu)=\mu I,\qquad \tau(\mu)\kappa(\mu)=\mu,\] with \(X(\mu)\succ0\), \(S(\mu)\succ0\), \(\tau(\mu)>0\), and \(\kappa(\mu)>0\). Equivalently, the matrix and scalar complementarity products share the same barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The embedded central path satisfies the affine embedding equations while matrix and scalar complementarity products both equal the common positive barrier parameter.

children.title: Initialization Compatibility Regimes

assumptions_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding permits fixed affine residual offsets.
