knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each regime is compatible precisely when its stated affine and interior requirements hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for feasible-start, residual-shifted, and canonical self-dual initialization.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An initial point \(z_0\) is compatible with a feasible-start regime when \(R(z_0)=0\) and every conic block of \(z_0\) is interior. It is compatible with a residual-shifted regime when its conic blocks are interior and the offset is chosen as \(r_0=-R(z_0)\). It is compatible with a prescribed canonical self-dual start only when the embedding's normalization equations are also satisfied. In all three regimes, the initial complementarity measure must obey \(\mu_0>0\); otherwise no logarithmic-barrier neighborhood can contain \(z_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization is compatible when it is interior and satisfies either the original embedding equations, correctly shifted equations, or the embedding's canonical normalization.

children.title: Path-Neighborhood Interfaces

assumptions_latex: The current embedded point has \(X\succ0\), \(S\succ0\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\kappa>0\).
The neighborhood parameter satisfies \(0\leq\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) supplies the centrality interface used by path-following step and termination rules.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an interior embedded point, define \(\mu=(\langle X,S\rangle+\tau\kappa)/(n+1)\). The Frobenius central-path neighborhood of radius \(\theta\) is \[\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\left\{(X,S,\tau,\kappa):\ \|X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}-\mu I\|_F\leq\theta\mu,\quad |\tau\kappa-\mu|\leq\theta\mu\right\}.\] An algorithmic interface accepting a trial iterate requires satisfaction of the embedded affine residual tolerance, positivity of all conic blocks, and membership in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\). These checks expose centrality independently of the particular Newton linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface accepts an interior iterate when its matrix and scalar complementarity products remain within a prescribed neighborhood of their common mean.

children.top_down_role: Interpretation of embedded outcomes as primal-dual solutions.

assumptions_latex: The primal SDP is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), with dual slack \(S=C-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\).
An embedded outcome satisfies its homogeneous equations with \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling by \(1/\tau\) recovers a primal-dual feasible pair, and vanishing complementarity recovers optimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery from a positive-scale homogeneous self-dual embedded outcome.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Algorithms and Software p. 41

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an embedded outcome \((X,y,S,\tau,\kappa)\) with \(\tau>0\), return \(\widehat X=X/\tau\), \(\widehat y=y/\tau\), and \(\widehat S=S/\tau\). For an exact embedded solution, the homogeneous equations imply \(\mathcal A(\widehat X)=b\) and \(\mathcal A^*(\widehat y)+\widehat S=C\), while cone membership gives \(\widehat X\succeq0\) and \(\widehat S\succeq0\). The recovered duality gap is \(\langle C,\widehat X\rangle-b^T\widehat y=\langle\widehat X,\widehat S\rangle\). Hence zero recovered complementarity certifies primal-dual optimality; otherwise these quantities define residual and gap termination tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the embedding scale is positive, divide all primal-dual blocks by it; the resulting feasibility residuals and complementarity determine solution quality.

children.title: Embedded Infeasibility Recovery

knowledge_statements.title: Embedded Infeasibility Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction and normalization of strong primal- or dual-infeasibility rays from a zero-scale embedded outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and let \(\mathcal A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) be its adjoint. At a zero-scale embedded outcome, inspect the nonzero homogeneous ray. If it supplies \(v\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(\mathcal A^*v\succeq0\) and \(b^Tv<0\), replace \(v\) by \(v/(-b^Tv)\) and return it as a primal-infeasibility certificate. If it supplies \(D\in\mathbb S_+^n\) with \(\mathcal A(D)=0\) and \(\langle C,D\rangle<0\), replace \(D\) by \(D/(-\langle C,D\rangle)\) and return it as a dual-infeasibility certificate. If neither strict negative pairing is available, return no strong-infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inspect a zero-scale embedded ray and normalize any multiplier or positive-semidefinite direction having the appropriate homogeneous equations and a strictly negative data pairing. If neither test succeeds, the ray does not yield a strong-infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The primal feasibility equations are \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) with \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), and dual feasibility is \(\mathcal A^*y+S=C\) with \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(S\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
The embedded terminal outcome has negligible homogeneous residual, \(\tau=0\), and \(\kappa>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned normalized ray is a directly verifiable strong-infeasibility certificate for the corresponding feasibility system.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for the standard equality-form primal-dual SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have adjoint \(\mathcal A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\), and define \[r_p=\mathcal A(X)-b,\qquad r_d=\mathcal A^*y+S-C.\] Fix the Euclidean norm on \(\mathbb R^m\), the Frobenius norm on \(\mathbb S^n\), and positive normalizers \(d_p,d_d\). The tuple \((X,y,S)\in\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\) is an \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d)\)-residual certificate when \(X\succeq0\), \(S\succeq0\), \(\|r_p\|_2/d_p\leq\varepsilon_p\), and \(\|r_d\|_F/d_d\leq\varepsilon_d\). Exact residual certification has \(r_p=0\) and \(r_d=0\). These residual bounds do not by themselves bound the objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-semidefinite primal and slack matrices together with bounded, explicitly normalized primal and dual equation residuals certify approximate feasibility and stationarity, but not objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The SDP data satisfy \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\).
The normalizers satisfy \(d_p>0\) and \(d_d>0\), and the tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed cone and residual tests give a directly checkable approximate primal-dual feasibility and stationarity certificate.

children.title: Duality-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Objective-quality assessment from compatible primal and dual points.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute duality-gap certificate for exactly feasible primal and dual SDP points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For a primal-feasible \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and a dual-feasible pair \((y,S)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S_+^n\), define \[g=\langle C,X\rangle-b^Ty=\langle S,X\rangle.\] Then \(g\geq0\). If \(g\leq\varepsilon\), the feasible dual and primal objective values form a lower and upper bound separated by at most \(\varepsilon\). If the primal optimal value is finite, each bound is within \(\varepsilon\) of it. If \(g=0\), both feasible points are optimal and the primal and dual optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compatible feasible points, the nonnegative objective gap equals matrix complementarity. A small gap brackets the optimal value within that gap, and a zero gap certifies optimality and equality of the primal and dual optimal values.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), and the dual is \(\max\{b^Ty:\mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ S\succeq0\}\).
The supplied primal and dual points are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound \(g\leq\varepsilon\) gives an absolute objective-quality certificate, while \(g=0\) certifies optimality of both feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type strong-infeasibility certificate for equality-form SDP feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(L=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\). A strong primal-infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[\mathcal A^*y\succeq0,\qquad b^Ty<0.\] It may be normalized so that \(b^Ty=-1\). When \(L\neq\varnothing\), existence of this certificate implies \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier with positive-semidefinite adjoint image and strictly negative data pairing is a finite strong-infeasibility certificate; for a nonempty affine constraint set, it certifies positive distance from the semidefinite cone.
assumptions_latex: The primal feasibility system is \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) with \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), where \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\).
The affine set \(L=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(y\) is a finite, directly verifiable certificate of strong primal infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The system is weakly infeasible exactly when \[L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing,
\qquad \operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)=0.\] A sequential witness consists of matrices \(Z_k\succeq0\) and \(X_k\in L\) such that \(\|Z_k-X_k\|_F\to0\). Equivalently, one may give \(Z_k\succeq0\) with \(\|\mathcal A(Z_k)-b\|\to0\), provided the residual-to-distance implication for \(\mathcal A\) is controlled on the relevant affine subspace. No multiplier can satisfy both \(\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\) and \(b^Ty<0\) in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak infeasibility is witnessed by positive semidefinite matrices approaching the affine constraints arbitrarily closely although no exact feasible matrix exists.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Certificates
children.top_down_role: Extended certificates derived from exposed-face reduction sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One facial-reduction step certified by a dual exposing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(F\) be a face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\), and suppose every feasible matrix belongs to \(F\). A facial-reduction certificate for \(F\) is a multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) whose exposing matrix \(W=\mathcal A^*y\) satisfies \[W\in F^*,\qquad b^Ty=0,
\qquad F\cap W^\perp\subsetneq F.\] The certificate identifies \(F\cap W^\perp\) as a proper face containing every feasible matrix. A sequence of such certificates may reduce the cone to a face on which the feasibility system is strictly feasible relative to that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exposing multiplier with zero data pairing certifies that all feasible matrices lie in a specified proper subface, providing one verifiable facial-reduction step.
assumptions_latex: The current cone is a face \(F\) of \(\mathbb S_+^n\), and every feasible matrix lies in \(F\).
The constraint map is \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), with equations \(\mathcal A(X)=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exposing matrix \(W\) certifies that every feasible matrix belongs to the proper face \(F\cap W^\perp\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)=0\), strict separation fails: there is no \(y\) satisfying \(\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\) and \(b^Ty<0\). Moreover, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some \(Z_\varepsilon\succeq0\) lies within \(\varepsilon\) of \(L\), so residual tests with any fixed positive tolerance can report apparent feasibility. Thus strong Farkas certificates terminate exactly beyond the positive-distance boundary; weakly infeasible instances require limiting witnesses, facial reduction, or additional exact structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong certificates fail sharply for zero-distance infeasibility: arbitrarily accurate approximate feasible points exist, but neither exact feasibility nor strict separation does.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Solution Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact KKT certificate for a factorized primal solution, with optional strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tuple \((R,y,S)\) is a low-rank optimality certificate when \(X=RR^{\mathsf T}\), \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(S=C-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\), and \(SR=0\). Then \(X\succeq0\), primal and dual feasibility hold, and \(\langle C,X\rangle-b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle S,X\rangle=\|S^{1/2}R\|_F^2=0\), so \(X\) and \((y,S)\) are optimal. If also \(\operatorname{rank}(R)+\operatorname{rank}(S)=n\), then \(\operatorname{range}(R)=\ker S\), and the certificate establishes strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank primal factor and positive semidefinite dual slack certify optimality when feasibility and complementary action hold; complementary ranks also identify the exact active eigenspaces.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual SDP is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*y=S\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact satisfaction certifies primal-dual optimality; the rank equality additionally certifies complementary eigenspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP Condition Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Renegar-style normwise conditioning of homogeneous SDP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero SDP data \(d\notin\Sigma\), its distance-to-ill-posedness condition measure is \[\kappa(d):=\frac{\|d\|_{\mathcal D}}{\delta(d)},\qquad \delta(d):=\inf_{d'\in\Sigma}\|d-d'\|_{\mathcal D}.\] The reciprocal \(\kappa(d)^{-1}\) is the infimum of \(\|\Delta d\|_{\mathcal D}/\|d\|_{\mathcal D}\) over perturbations satisfying \(d+\Delta d\in\Sigma\). The convention gives \(\kappa(d)=+\infty\) when \(d\in\Sigma\). The set \(\Sigma\) and the data norm are part of the definition and must be stated when reporting the measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP condition measure is the data norm divided by the distance to a declared ill-posed set; its reciprocal is the relative stability radius.
assumptions_latex: The nonzero data vector \(d\) lies outside a closed set \(\Sigma\) of ill-posed SDP instances.
The data norm and induced distance are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative condition measure is \(\kappa(d)=\|d\|_{\mathcal D}/\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal D}(d,\Sigma)\).

children.title: Distance-to-Ill-Posedness Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric proximity of problem instances to feasibility or optimality boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-to-Ill-Posedness Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric stability radius around a well-posed SDP instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta(d)=\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal D}(d,\Sigma)>0\). Then \[B(d,\delta(d))\cap\Sigma=\varnothing.\] Consequently, every perturbation \(\Delta d\) satisfying \(\|\Delta d\|_{\mathcal D}<\delta(d)\) remains outside \(\Sigma\). Conversely, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(d_\varepsilon\in\Sigma\) with \(\|d-d_\varepsilon\|_{\mathcal D}<\delta(d)+\varepsilon\). Thus \(\delta(d)\) is the maximal guaranteed open perturbation radius avoiding ill-posedness, and its level sets form metric offsets of \(\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to the ill-posed set is exactly the largest open perturbation radius guaranteed not to reach ill-posed SDP data.
assumptions_latex: The ill-posed set \(\Sigma\) is nonempty and closed in the finite-dimensional normed data space.
The datum satisfies \(d\notin\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every perturbation smaller than \(\delta(d)\) remains outside \(\Sigma\), and this open stability radius is maximal.

notation.meaning: Closed set of ill-posed SDP data.
Distance from d to the ill-posed set.
Open norm ball centered at d with radius r.

The strictly stable regime is [1m[0m\(\rho<1\), because [1m[0m\(U_\eta(d)\cap\Sigma=\varnothing\). A transition regime occurs as [1m[0m\(\rho\uparrow1\), where the remaining stability margin [1m[0m\(\delta(d)-\eta\) vanishes. At [1m[0m\(\rho=1\), intersection with the closed ball is guaranteed when a nearest ill-posed datum exists.

children.title: Attainable Accuracy Limits
children.top_down_role: Accuracy limitations associated with conditioning and proximity to ill-posed instances.

assumptions_latex: Only perturbed data [1m[0m\(\widetilde d\) are observed, with unknown exact data satisfying [1m[0m\(\|d-\widetilde d\|_{\mathcal D}\le\eta\).
Each admissible datum has a nonempty solution set [1m[0m\(\mathcal S(d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No data-only output can uniformly guarantee forward error below half the solution-set ambiguity diameter.

notation.meaning: Exact solution set for data d.
Worst pairwise separation of compatible solutions.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indistinguishable perturbed inputs impose a minimax half-diameter lower bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic forward-accuracy floor under bounded data uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the ambiguity diameter [1m[0m\[D_\eta(\widetilde d):=\sup\{\|z_1-z_2\|_{\mathcal Z}:d_1,d_2\in U_\eta(\widetilde d),\ z_i\in\mathcal S(d_i)\}.\] Any algorithm receiving only [1m[0m\(\widetilde d\) returns the same output [1m[0m\(\widehat z\) for all compatible exact data. By the triangle inequality, for every compatible pair [1m[0m\((z_1,z_2)\), at least one error [1m[0m\(\|\widehat z-z_i\|_{\mathcal Z}\) is at least [1m[0m\(\|z_1-z_2\|_{\mathcal Z}/2\). Hence no uniform guarantee below [1m[0m\(D_\eta(\widetilde d)/2\) is attainable; the floor may be infinite near pathological instances.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted half-diameter lower bound does not follow for forward error to solution sets: two widely separated selected solutions may belong to overlapping or broad solution sets. A sourced theorem using singleton solutions or an appropriate separation between solution sets is required.

children.top_down_role: Post-solution interfaces converting SDP outputs into objects for the originating problem.

children.title: Randomized Rounding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Distributional recovery procedures driven by PSD solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is an optimal or approximately optimal SDP relaxation matrix.
The target discrete feasible set is \(\{-1,1\}^n\), and feasibility is invariant under a common sign reversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(x\) is a discrete random vector whose distribution is determined by \(X\), with \(\mathbb E[x_i x_j]=\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(X_{ij})\) when \(X_{ii}=1\).

notation.meaning: PSD relaxation matrix, normalized to unit diagonal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian hyperplane rounding for unit-diagonal correlation SDPs.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\succeq0\) with \(X_{ii}=1\), compute a Gram factorization \(X=VV^{\mathsf T}\), where row \(v_i\) satisfies \(\lVert v_i\rVert_2=1\). Draw \(g\sim N(0,I_r)\), set \(x_i=\operatorname{sign}(v_i^{\mathsf T}g)\), and return \(x\), optionally selecting the best feasible sample among repeated independent draws. For every \(i,j\), the induced signs satisfy \(\mathbb E[x_i x_j]=1-2\arccos(X_{ij})/\pi=(2/\pi)\arcsin(X_{ij})\). A stopping rule specifies either a fixed sample count or termination once a prescribed recovered objective value is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the PSD solution into vectors, sample a Gaussian hyperplane, and return the induced signs. Their pairwise correlations are an explicit arcsine transform of the SDP entries.

children.title: Deterministic Spectral Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery based on leading eigenspaces or low-rank embeddings.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is a solved relaxation matrix.
A target rank \(k\geq1\) and a deterministic normalization or downstream projection rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns the best rank-\(k\) PSD approximation \(X_k\) in Frobenius norm and a deterministic embedding derived from its leading eigenspace.

notation.meaning: eigenvalues of the relaxation matrix in nonincreasing order

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leading-eigenspace truncation followed by a fixed problem-specific projection.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute an eigendecomposition \(X=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i u_i u_i^{\mathsf T}\) with \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\). For prescribed \(k\), form \(X_k=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i u_i u_i^{\mathsf T}=V_kV_k^{\mathsf T}\), where \(V_k=[\sqrt{\lambda_1}u_1,\ldots,\sqrt{\lambda_k}u_k]\). Return \(V_k\), or apply the specified deterministic projection to its rows or leading eigenvector. By spectral truncation, \(X_k\) minimizes \(\lVert X-Y\rVert_F\) over PSD matrices \(Y\) of rank at most \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncate the solved PSD matrix to its leading eigenspace, producing the best low-rank PSD approximation, then apply a specified deterministic projection to recover a candidate solution.

children.title: Rank-One Extraction Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Extraction Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue-based detection and extraction from a PSD matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(X=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)U^{\mathsf T}\) with \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\). Declare numerical rank one when \(\lambda_1>0\) and \(\lambda_2\leq\tau\max\{1,\lambda_1\}\). If accepted, set \(x=\sqrt{\lambda_1}u_1\), choose its sign or scale using the lifted formulation's normalization, verify the original constraints, and return \(x\). For \(\tau=0\), acceptance gives \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\); for \(\tau>0\), the residual is \(\lVert X-xx^{\mathsf T}\rVert_2=\lambda_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test whether only one eigenvalue is significant. If so, extract its scaled eigenvector, fix the formulation-dependent sign or scale, and verify the original constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is available within numerical tolerance \(\tau\geq0\).
The original lifted formulation identifies feasible rank-one matrices as \(xx^{\mathsf T}\), possibly with an affine normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the rank-one test passes, the returned \(x\) satisfies \(xx^{\mathsf T}=X\) exactly when \(\tau=0\), and approximately otherwise.

children.title: Rank-Based Tightness Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Numerical rank patterns used to assess recovery prospects.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Based Tightness Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware numerical-rank diagnostics for PSD relaxation solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(r_\tau(X)=\#\{i:\lambda_i>\tau\max\{1,\lambda_1\}\}\). Rank-one proximity may be reported through \(r_\tau(X)\), the eigenvalue ratio \(\lambda_2/\lambda_1\) when \(\lambda_1>0\), and the relative spectral tail \(\bigl(\sum_{i\geq2}\lambda_i^2\bigr)^{1/2}/\lVert X\rVert_F\). In exact arithmetic, a nonzero PSD matrix has rank one precisely when its rank is one, equivalently when the eigenvalue ratio and spectral tail vanish. With finite tolerances, \(r_\tau(X)=1\) together with small ratio and tail values indicates recovery prospects, but exactness additionally requires feasibility and objective consistency for the extracted original-variable solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholded numerical rank, the second-to-first eigenvalue ratio, and the spectral tail quantify rank-one proximity. A numerical rank of one together with small ratio and tail values supports recovery but does not by itself certify exactness.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is a computed relaxation solution with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\).
A relative threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantities \(r_\tau(X)\), \(\lambda_2/\lambda_1\), and the spectral tail measure proximity to rank-one structure but do not alone prove relaxation exactness.

children.title: Dual Tightness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual solution structures used to verify relaxation exactness.

assumptions_latex: The primal SDP is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\).
The dual is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S,\ S\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A primal-dual feasible triple with zero gap is optimal; if its primal matrix is a valid rank-one lift, the relaxation is exact.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual zero-gap certificate combined with valid rank-one recovery.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,y,S)\) satisfy \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(X\succeq0\), \(C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S\), and \(S\succeq0\). The identity \(\langle C,X\rangle-b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle S,X\rangle\) makes the nonnegative duality gap directly verifiable. If \(\langle S,X\rangle=0\), then \(X\) and \((y,S)\) are primal-dual optimal and satisfy complementarity. If additionally \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) under the original lift and \(x\) is feasible for the nonconvex problem, then its objective equals the SDP bound, certifying relaxation exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual feasibility plus a zero duality gap certify SDP optimality. A feasible rank-one primal lift then certifies that the original relaxation is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Tightness Certificates

children.title: Integrality-Gap Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Computational comparison of relaxation bounds and recovered discrete solutions.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem, and its SDP relaxation gives lower bound \(L\).
A recovered feasible discrete solution has objective value \(U\geq L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute gap \(U-L\) and a stated relative normalization quantify observed relaxation quality; zero gap certifies optimality when both bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori gap for minimization using an SDP bound and recovered feasible value.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(L\) be the valid SDP relaxation value and let \(U\) be the objective of a recovered feasible original solution. Define the absolute observed integrality gap by \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\geq0\). A scale-robust reported version is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\), although any alternative denominator must be stated explicitly. The diagnostic must report solver tolerances and feasibility residuals. If \(U=L\) in exact arithmetic, the recovered solution is globally optimal and the relaxation is tight at that instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare the SDP lower bound with a recovered feasible objective. Their nonnegative difference is the observed gap; a zero gap certifies optimality when both values are valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Diagnostics

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After solving level \(d\), copy all shared moment entries of \(X_d\) into \(E_d(X_d)\) at level \(d+1\), initialize new entries by a specified completion rule, and regularize the resulting PSD blocks if required. Likewise embed shared components of \((y_d,S_d)\) into the next dual variables and initialize new multipliers and slack blocks. Supply these values, together with inherited eigenspaces or factorizations, as the level-\(d+1\) initial iterate. Stop only according to the next-level solver's feasibility and optimality tests; warm starting alone asserts neither feasibility nor complexity improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embed shared primal, dual, and spectral data from one hierarchy level into the next, initialize new coordinates, then let the next solver restore feasibility and certify termination.

children.title: Sparse Hierarchy Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Coupling of moment sparsity with chordal and block SDP solvers.

assumptions_latex: Polynomial variables and constraints admit cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) satisfying the running-intersection property.
Each local moment or localizing matrix uses monomials supported within one clique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sparse hierarchy is represented by smaller PSD blocks with overlap equalities, enabling chordal or block SDP solvers while preserving local consistency.

notation.meaning: local truncated moment sequence on clique k
local moment matrix at order d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correlative-sparsity moment relaxation with running-intersection coupling.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each clique \(C_k\), construct a local sequence \(y^{(k)}\) and impose \(M_d(y^{(k)})\succeq0\) together with the required localizing constraints. Whenever \(C_k\cap C_\ell\neq\varnothing\), equate all represented moments on the overlap: \(y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha\) for every shared multi-index \(\alpha\). The resulting SDP consists of clique-indexed PSD blocks coupled by linear consistency equations. Under the running-intersection property these blocks align with a chordal decomposition and can be passed directly to sparse or block-structured SDP solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build moment and localizing matrices per variable clique, then equate moments on clique overlaps. The resulting chordal block SDP exposes sparsity to specialized solvers.

children.title: Finite-Convergence Detection
children.top_down_role: Computational indicators used to identify finite convergence within SDP hierarchies.

assumptions_latex: At relaxation order \(d\), a feasible truncated moment sequence \(y^*\) attains value \(p_d\).
A flat-extension rank equality holds for an order decrement compatible with the constraint degrees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The flat solution has a finite atomic representing measure supported on feasible global minimizers, so \(p_d=p^*\) and the hierarchy has converged finitely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat-extension finite-convergence certificate for polynomial moment relaxations.

source_refs.locator: 4.8 Extracting Finite Point Sets p. 184
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\) be the maximum half-degree offset required by the defining constraints. If an optimal moment solution satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-s}(y^*)=r\), and its localizing constraints enforce support in the feasible set, then \(y^*\) admits an \(r\)-atomic representing measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\) with \(w_i>0\). Each atom \(x^{(i)}\) is feasible and globally minimizing, and the relaxation value satisfies \(p_d=p^*\). Thus the displayed rank equality plus feasibility constitutes a finite-convergence certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat moment-matrix rank equality yields a finite atomic measure on feasible global minimizers. It certifies equality of the current relaxation value and the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Convergence Detection

children.title: Rank-Based Termination Tests
children.top_down_role: Rank-structure interfaces supporting hierarchy termination decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(y\) is a feasible truncated moment sequence at order \(d\).
The constraint degree offset is \(s\), and a numerical rank threshold \(\tau\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of the thresholded ranks of \(M_d(y)\) and \(M_{d-s}(y)\), followed by extraction validation, is an implementable termination test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical flatness test with a constraint-dependent degree offset.

source_refs.locator: 4.8 Extracting Finite Point Sets p. 184
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(r_\tau(M)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M)>\tau\max\{1,\sigma_1(M)\}\}\). The rank-based termination predicate at order \(d\) is \(r_\tau(M_d(y))=r_\tau(M_{d-s}(y))\). In exact arithmetic, replace \(r_\tau\) by matrix rank. A numerical implementation may terminate only after the candidate atoms extracted from this flat structure satisfy the original constraints and reproduce the required moments and objective within declared tolerances. Failure of rank equality means this flatness-based test is inconclusive, not that finite convergence is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate on numerical flatness only when two degree-separated moment matrices have equal rank and the extracted atoms pass feasibility, moment-reproduction, and objective checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Based Termination Tests

children.title: Optimizer Extraction
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for recovering candidate optimizers from terminating hierarchy levels.

assumptions_latex: A flat moment matrix \(M_d(y)\) has rank \(r\).
A basis of \(r\) independent monomial columns is selected and the induced multiplication matrices are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint eigenvalue tuples of the commuting multiplication matrices give the support points, which are retained only after feasibility and moment-reproduction checks.

notation.meaning: basis matrix formed from independent moment columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplication-matrix extraction from a flat truncated moment sequence.

source_refs.locator: 4.8 Extracting Finite Point Sets p. 184

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a monomial basis whose columns form a full-rank submatrix \(B\) of \(M_d(y)\). For each coordinate \(x_j\), express multiplication of the basis monomials by \(x_j\) in the same column space, obtaining \(T_j\). Under flatness, the matrices \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\) commute and are simultaneously diagonalizable. Compute their joint eigenvalue tuples \(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\), solve the linear moment equations for weights, and return those tuples passing original feasibility and objective checks. Stop with extraction failure if conditioning prevents stable joint diagonalization or validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct coordinate multiplication matrices from a flat moment basis. Their joint eigenvalues are candidate optimizers, accepted after weight recovery, feasibility, and objective validation.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Extraction

knowledge_statements.title: Measure Recovery Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite atomic representing-measure recovery after flat support extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given extracted points \(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\), recover weights \(w_1,\ldots,w_r\) from \(y_\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i(x^{(i)})^\alpha\) for a full-rank set of monomial indices \(\alpha\), with \(w_i>0\) and \(\sum_iw_i=y_0\). Define \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\). Accept \(\mu\) only if it reproduces every available moment within tolerance and its support satisfies the localizing constraints. Under exact flatness, this finite atomic measure represents the truncated sequence and has exactly \(r\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit positive weights to the extracted support points so their atomic measure reproduces every available moment, then validate positivity, normalization, support feasibility, and residuals.
assumptions_latex: The truncated moment sequence \(y\) satisfies a flat-extension condition with rank \(r\).
The extracted support points \(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\) are distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the Vandermonde moment equations recovers a unique positive atomic measure representing all available moments when the residual and positivity tests pass.

children.title: Extraction Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where termination evidence is inconclusive or recovered solutions remain numerically ambiguous.

knowledge_statements.title: Extraction Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for optimizer or atomic-measure extraction from a truncated moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) be a feasible truncated moment sequence for a polynomial optimization relaxation on \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge 0\}\), and let \(r=\max_j\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Exact flat-extension extraction is not certified when \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)>\operatorname{rank}M_{d-r}(y)\). Even if numerical ranks appear equal, extraction must be declared unsuccessful unless the rank is stable under prescribed tolerances and the recovered atoms \(x_i\) and weights \(w_i>0\) satisfy \(x_i\in K\) and reproduce the supplied moments within the prescribed residual tolerance. Failure of these tests does not prove that no representing measure or optimizer exists; it only invalidates certified extraction from the current relaxation output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extraction is uncertified when flatness fails, numerical rank is unstable, or recovered positive atoms violate feasibility or moment residual tolerances; failure does not establish nonexistence of optimizers or representing measures.
assumptions_latex: \(M_d(y)\succeq 0\) and the required localizing matrices are positive semidefinite.
A numerical extraction routine uses fixed rank and residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified extraction from \(y\) is unavailable whenever flatness or the stated numerical validation tests fail.

notation.meaning: moment matrix of order t associated with the truncated sequence y
largest half-degree, rounded upward, among the constraint polynomials
